- **Viṣṇu's Boon and Garuḍa Becomes His Mount** — Impressed in the amṛta-flight, Viṣṇu grants Garuḍa immortality without drinking the nectar and a perch above him, setting him on his banner and making him his vāhana _(actors: Garuḍa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Yajña-Varāha allegory of the boar's body as sacrifice** — Every limb of the boar is equated with a component of the Vedic yajña, making the lift a cosmic sacrifice sustaining the world _(actors: Varāha as yajña-mūrti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.13.34–44)
- **Yami Becomes the River Yamuna** — In Puranic tradition Yami's grief at Yama's death transforms her into the sacred river Yamuna _(actors: Yami/Yamuna)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Puranas)
- **Aitareya Upaniṣad embedded** — AĀ 2.4–2.6 forms the Aitareya Upaniṣad, opening 'ātmā vā idam eka evāgra āsīt' and stating 'prajñānaṃ brahma' _(actors: Mahidāsa Aitareya; the Ātman/Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Aitareya Āraṇyaka 2.4–2.6 (Aitareya Upaniṣad))
- **Alignment of Dhruva, Meru and the lokas** — The Śiśumāra-cakra occupies the starry region above the planetary spheres and Mount Meru, with Dhruva as the celestial pole directly above the Meru world-axis, all contained within the one Brahmāṇḍa _(actors: Dhruva, Mount Meru, the lokas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/shishumara-chakra.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.20-23; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.8-9)
- **Atman splits into male and female** — In the beginning the Self alone, lonely, desires a second and splits into husband and wife, from whose union all beings arise through name and form _(actors: Atman/Self)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4)
- **Atman splits into male and female (Upanishadic monism)** — The lonely Self (Atman) desires a second, splits into husband and wife, and from their union all beings arise through name and form _(actors: Atman/Brahman)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brihadaranyaka Upanishad 1.4)
- **Bhrigu's journey to the other world** — The proud Bhrigu, sent by his father Varuna to the next world, witnesses men devoured by the men, animals and plants they had consumed in life; returns chastened to be taught the Agnihotra's inner meaning _(actors: Bhrigu, Varuna, the eaten and the eaters in the afterworld)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Jaiminiya Brahmana I.42-44 (cf. Shatapatha Brahmana 11.6.1))
- **Birth of Bṛhaspati, guru of the gods** — Aṅgiras fathers Bṛhaspati, lord of sacred speech and Devaguru, structural counterpart to Śukra guru of the asuras _(actors: Aṅgiras, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Mahābhārata; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Birth of the daitya twins Hiraṇyākṣa and Hiraṇyakaśipu** — Diti bears twin daitya sons by Kaśyapa at a feared twilight conception; they are the first demonic birth of Jaya and Vijaya _(actors: Diti, Kaśyapa, Hiraṇyākṣa, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Jaya–Vijaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.16–17)
- **Birth of the Dānavas from Danu** — From Danu descend the Dānavas including Vṛtra and the Vipracitti line _(actors: Kaśyapa, Danu, the Dānavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Birth of the eight diggajas from Brahmā's chanting** — Per the Mātaṅgalīlā, Airāvata and the seven other world-elephants spring from Brahmā chanting hymns over Garuḍa's eggshell, forming the aṣṭa-diggaja that uphold the quarters of space _(actors: Brahmā, Airāvata)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mātaṅgalīlā; Amarakośa)
- **Daksha's sons renounce; Narada is cursed** — Narada dissuades Daksha's Haryashva and Shabalashva sons from procreating; the enraged Daksha curses Narada to wander eternally _(actors: Daksha, Narada, the Haryashvas, the Shabalashvas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 6.5; Vishnu Purana)
- **Genesis of the Shakti Pithas** — Vishnu's Sudarshana Chakra dismembers Sati's corpse as the grief-stricken Shiva dances; each landing-spot of a body-part becomes a Shakti Pitha _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu, Sati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Devi-Bhagavata VII, Kalika Purana, Mahabhagavata Purana, Pithanirnaya)
- **Horse-head affixed; demon Hayagrīva slain** — By the Goddess's decree a horse's head is joined to Viṣṇu's body, forming Hayagrīva, who then slays the demon Hayagrīva killable only by a horse-headed being _(actors: Viṣṇu as Hayagrīva, the Great Goddess, the asura Hayagrīva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hayagriva.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.5)
- **Instruction to abide as the unattached witness** — The swan instructs the realized soul to abandon false identification with body and mind, remain unattached amid sense-experience, and rest in the Self — the paramahaṃsa ideal _(actors: Viṣṇu as Haṃsa, the Four Kumāras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hamsa-avatar.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.13.35-39)
- **Kardama Weds Devahuti** — The prajapati Kardama performs tapas, marries Svayambhuva Manu's daughter Devahuti, builds an aerial palace, and fathers nine daughters and a son who is Vishnu _(actors: Kardama, Devahuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.21-24)
- **Mahānārāyaṇa hymns to Nārāyaṇa and the Puruṣa-sūkta** — Taittirīya Āraṇyaka prapāṭhaka 10 (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad) hymns Nārāyaṇa as supreme Brahman and houses an expanded Yajurvedic Puruṣa-sūkta recension _(actors: Nārāyaṇa, Puruṣa, the gods)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/taittiriya-brahmana.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 3 / 10 (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad))
- **Manu re-progenerates humanity through Iḍā** — Sole survivor Manu offers an oblation into the waters from which the woman Iḍā arises, and through her he regenerates the human race _(actors: Manu, Iḍā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1.6–10)
- **Mooring at Naubandhana on the northern peak** — The fish tows the boat to the highest Himālaya peak (Naubandhana, 'ship-binding'), where the sages secure it _(actors: the fish, Manu, the saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa 1.8.1; Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Origin of Chitragupta from Brahma's Body** — Chitragupta springs from the body (kaya) of Brahma to keep the master-ledger of every being's deeds when Yama could not track them all _(actors: Chitragupta, Brahma, Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yama.md) — (Garuda Purana; Padma Purana; Kayastha tradition)
- **Prātiśākhyas as predecessors of Pāṇini** — The oldest extant Indian linguistic science supplies the vocabulary and pada-analysis that Pāṇini's Aṣṭādhyāyī inherits and generalizes into universal grammar _(actors: Prātiśākhya authors; Pāṇini)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/pratishakhyas.md) — (Prātiśākhyas; Aṣṭādhyāyī of Pāṇini)
- **Pulaha fathers creature-classes** — Pulaha by his wife Kṣamā/Gati fathers various beasts, demi-races and sons (Karmaśreṣṭha, Varīyāṃs, Sahiṣṇu) _(actors: Pulaha; Kṣamā/Gati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-mind-born-seers.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1)
- **Sindhu in the Bhāratavarṣa river-rosters** — The Purāṇic geographies catalogue the Sindhu among the holy northern rivers of the karma-bhūmi as sacred attention shifts east to the Gaṅgā _(actors: Purāṇic compilers; the river Sindhu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-sindhu-and-the-indus-rivers.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 2.3; Vāyu Purāṇa; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Sukeśa weds Devavatī; birth of Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī** — Sukeśa marries Devavatī and fathers the celebrated triad Mālyavān, Sumālī and Mālī, the great rākṣasa kings _(actors: Sukeśa, Devavatī, Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **The Golden Womb (Hiranyagarbha) Arises** — A golden germ/egg arises as the sole lord of creation, sustaining heaven and earth, named in the final verse as Prajapati — the seed of the later cosmic egg and Brahma _(actors: Hiranyagarbha, Prajapati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.121 (Hiranyagarbha Sukta))
- **The Kuśa-Grass Trick and the Serpents' Forked Tongues** — Garuḍa delivers the amṛta to the nāgas to free Vinatā but sets it on kuśa grass; while they bathe Indra snatches it back, and the nāgas licking the grass split their tongues — the aetiology of the forked tongue _(actors: Garuḍa, Indra, nāgas, Vinatā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/garuda.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **The number-litany of the Chamakam** — A Chamakam anuvāka enumerates the odd (1–33) and even (4–48) numbers as 'ca me' requests, asking that all numerical orders of reality including the 33 Vedic gods be made favourable through sacrifice _(actors: Rudra–Śiva; the 33 Vedic gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-rudram-namakam-chamakam.md) — (Taittirīya Saṃhitā 4.7.11)
- **The Saramā–Paṇi dialogue and refusal** — In the saṃvāda hymn the Paṇis try to bribe Saramā to defect; she refuses as Indra's envoy, foretelling that Indra and the Aṅgirases will break Vala _(actors: Saramā, the Paṇis, Indra, the Aṅgirases)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.108; Bṛhaddevatā; Sāyaṇa's commentary)
- **The seven patalas roster and their rulers** — Atala (Bala), Vitala (Siva as Hatakeshvara), Sutala (Bali), Talatala (Maya), Mahatala (Kadru's Nagas), Rasatala (the Pani Daityas/Danavas), and Patala (Vasuki) are named in descending order _(actors: Bala, Hatakeshvara-Siva, Bali, Maya, the many-hooded Nagas, the Nivata-kavacas/Kaleyas, Vasuki)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.24.16-31)
- **Unfolding of the cosmic egg (Adi-Sāṅkhya cosmogony)** — From the unmanifest Pradhāna arise mahat, ahaṃkāra, the tanmātras and gross elements, condensing into the golden cosmic egg (brahmāṇḍa) within which Brahmā fashions the worlds _(actors: Brahmā, Pradhāna)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmanda-purana.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Prakriyā/Anuṣaṅga pādas))
- **Vishnu Appears as an Old Man to Sage Nārada at Vridha Badri** — Vishnu appears in the form of an old man to sage Narada during his penance at Animath, where the current Badrinath idol carved by Vishvakarma was first worshipped _(actors: Vishnu, Narada, Vishvakarma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Badari-mahatmya))
- **Vāyu breaks the peak of Meru to form Laṅkā** — Incited by Nārada and after Garuḍa abandons his shielding post, Vāyu shears off the summit of Mount Meru and hurls it into the southern ocean, where it becomes the three-peaked Trikūṭa island of Laṅkā _(actors: Vāyu, Nārada, Garuḍa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Purāṇic tradition)
- **Aṅgiras's wider progeny — Utathya, Saṃvarta and the gotra lines** — Aṅgiras fathers sons including Utathya (ancestor of Bharadvāja) and Saṃvarta, seeding the Āṅgirasa house _(actors: Aṅgiras, Utathya, Saṃvarta, Bharadvāja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Mahābhārata (Ādi & Anuśāsana); Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Antaryāmin: Nārāyaṇa as inner controller** — The Supreme is named the Antaryāmin, the inner ruler dwelling in and governing all beings, an explicitly Vaiṣṇava reading later central to Rāmānuja's body-soul theology _(actors: Nārāyaṇa as Antaryāmin; later Rāmānuja)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad; cf. Bṛhadāraṇyaka Antaryāmin-brāhmaṇa)
- **Bali installed in Sutala by Vamana** — After surrendering the three worlds to Vamana/Trivikrama, the virtuous Daitya emperor Bali is granted kingship of Sutala, with Vishnu standing guard at his gate _(actors: Bali (Mahabali), Vamana/Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.24.18-21; 8.22)
- **Birth of the Nāgas from Kadru** — From Kadru are born the thousand serpents Śeṣa, Vāsuki, Takṣaka and the rest _(actors: Kaśyapa, Kadru, the Nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21; Bhāgavata 6.6)
- **Brahmā composes the Daṇḍanīti and the first king is instituted** — In primeval anarchy men appeal to Brahmā, who composes a vast treatise on polity; Śiva abridges it and the first king is installed to wield the rod of punishment _(actors: Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12.59)
- **Divine contest myths and saman origins** — The Jaiminiya Brahmana preserves numerous myths of Indra's exploits, the gods' rivalries, and the seizing of soma, many tied to the origin of particular saman-melodies _(actors: Indra, Kutsa, the gods, rishis who 'saw' the samans)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/panchavimsha-brahmana.md) — (Jaiminiya Brahmana)
- **Hiraṇyākṣa drags the Earth into the deep** — The boon-emboldened Hiraṇyākṣa challenges Varuṇa, then seizes the Earth and drags her down into Rasātala/the lower waters _(actors: Hiraṇyākṣa, Varuṇa, the Earth)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.17–18)
- **Indra and the Aṅgirases split Vala and release the cows** — Acting on Saramā's report, Indra with the Aṅgirases breaks open the Vala cave and frees the cows/dawns _(actors: Indra, the Aṅgirases, the cosmic cows, Saramā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Bṛhaddevatā; Sāyaṇa on ṚV 10.108)
- **Kapila's Teaching to Devahuti** — Vishnu incarnate as the sage Kapila instructs his mother Devahuti in Sankhya, bhakti-yoga, and liberation, and she attains moksha _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **Kauṣītaki / Śāṅkhāyana Āraṇyaka composed** — Fifteen-adhyāya Rigvedic forest text of the rival Kauṣītaki school treating the Mahāvrata, Puruṣa-vidyā, and the inner Agnihotra _(actors: Kauṣītaki; Śāṅkhāyana)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Śāṅkhāyana (Kauṣītaki) Āraṇyaka)
- **Kratu fathers the Vālakhilyas** — Kratu by his wife Kriyā fathers the sixty thousand thumb-sized Vālakhilya ascetics who escort the Sun's chariot; in the Mahābhārata their austerity generates Garuḍa _(actors: Kratu; Kriyā; the Vālakhilyas; Garuḍa; Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-mind-born-seers.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.10; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Lotus-born Brahma from Vishnu's navel** — During pralaya Vishnu reclines on Shesha on the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma, the delegated creator _(actors: Vishnu (Narayana), Brahma, Shesha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8, Vishnu Purana)
- **Parvati's rebirth and tapas to win Shiva** — Sati reincarnates as Parvati, daughter of Himavan, and undertakes ferocious austerities (Aparna) to win the meditating Shiva, passing his Brahmin-disguise test _(actors: Parvati, Himavan, Shiva, Narada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Parvati Khanda, Kumarasambhava 1-5, Devi-Bhagavata)
- **Pravargya and the severed head of the sacrifice** — The Pravargya hot-milk rite identifies the red-hot Mahāvīra pot with the sun and the severed head of the sacrifice (Makha/Viṣṇu), whose decapitation myth anchors the rite _(actors: Makha/Viṣṇu, Agni, Sūrya, the Adhvaryu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa kāṇḍa 14 (Pravargya))
- **Rudrābhiṣeka and graded Rudra-japa** — The Śrī Rudram becomes the supreme abhiṣeka-chant for bathing the Śiva-liṅga, recited in graded tiers (Rudra, Ekādaśa-rudri, Laghu-rudra, Mahā-rudra, Ati-rudra) framed by laghu-nyāsa and Śānti _(actors: Śaiva priests and devotees; Rudra–Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/sri-rudram-namakam-chamakam.md) — (Rudra-yajña paddhati; laghu-nyāsa; living temple liturgy)
- **The Kumāras' liberation and the swan's disappearance** — Having grasped the teaching, the Four Kumāras worship the swan, who then vanishes — the entire span of the avatāra _(actors: The Four Kumāras, Viṣṇu as Haṃsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hamsa-avatar.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.13.40-42)
- **The Matsya in-flood teaching (brahma-jñāna)** — During the night of dissolution Matsya expounds knowledge of the Self and Absolute to Satyavrata and the sages (the 'Matsya Purāṇa') _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Satyavrata, the saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Vishnu reclines on Shesha and projects Brahma** — During the cosmic night Vishnu reclines on the serpent Shesha upon the causal ocean; at creation's dawn a lotus springs from his navel bearing Brahma the delegated creator _(actors: Vishnu (Narayana), Shesha, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8; Vishnu Purana; Matsya Purana)
- **Viśvakarmā builds Laṅkā** — At the brothers' request the divine architect Viśvakarmā raises the golden city of Laṅkā on Mount Trikūṭa for the first rākṣasa masters _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Mālyavān, Sumālī, Mālī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rakshasas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Agnicayana rebuilds Prajāpati as the bird-altar** — The fire-altar of 10,800 bricks in five layers shaped as a falcon reassembles the dismembered Prajāpati and Agni, encoding the year in its bricks _(actors: Prajāpati, Agni, the yajamāna)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa kāṇḍas 6–10)
- **Ananta-Shesha reclines below Patala** — Beneath the lowest tier Patala, the cosmic serpent Ananta-Shesha bears all the worlds on a single hood _(actors: Ananta-Shesha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.24.31; 5.25)
- **Birth of Garuḍa and Aruṇa from Vinatā** — From Vinatā are born Aruṇa and Garuḍa, and the Kadru–Vinatā wager seeds the eternal serpent–bird enmity _(actors: Kaśyapa, Vinatā, Kadru, Garuḍa, Aruṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 16-34)
- **Brahma born from the navel-lotus of Vishnu** — Within each cosmic egg, Vishnu reclines on the Garbhodaka womb-ocean and from his navel-lotus is born Brahma, who then builds the dvipas and lokas _(actors: Vishnu (Garbhodaka-shayi), Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahmanda-and-bhuvana-kosha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8; Brahma-samhita 5.51)
- **Creation of the worlds by the Self (Aitareya Upanishad)** — The Self/Atman, alone in the beginning, creates the worlds, the cosmic Person and the deities, then enters his creation through the crown of the head _(actors: Atman (the Self), the cosmic Purusha, the deities)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/aitareya-brahmana.md) — (Aitareya Aranyaka II; Aitareya Upanishad 1)
- **Devi slays Madhu and Kaitabha (Prathama-carita)** — The Goddess as Yoganidra/Mahamaya rouses Vishnu from cosmic sleep to slay the demons Madhu and Kaitabha who threatened Brahma _(actors: Mahakali (Devi), Vishnu, Brahma, Madhu, Kaitabha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana (Devi Mahatmya ch. 1))
- **Formation of the eight Āṅgirasa gaṇas** — The Āṅgirasa pravara-cluster, largest of the brahmin gotra groupings, organizes into eight gaṇas including the Bharadvāja and Gautama lines _(actors: Aṅgiras, Āṅgirasa gotra-founders)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Baudhāyana Śrautasūtra pravara lists; gotra–pravara tradition)
- **Garuḍa wins the amṛta to free his mother Vinatā** — Garuḍa, son of Kaśyapa and Vinatā, wins the amṛta from Indra to ransom his enslaved mother, whereupon Viṣṇu grants him immortality and makes him his mount and banner _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Kaśyapa, Indra, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (World History Encyclopedia, Garuda; Wikipedia)
- **Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad embedded** — Adhyāyas 3–6 form the Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad, teaching Prāṇa = Brahman, the Indra–Pratardana dialogue, and the Devayāna soul-journey _(actors: Indra; Pratardana; the soul on the Devayāna)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Kauṣītaki Āraṇyaka 3–6 (Kauṣītaki Upaniṣad))
- **Lingodbhava — the pillar of fire** — Shiva manifests as the infinite pillar of fire between Brahma and Vishnu, establishing the linga as supreme; carried by the Kurma Purana _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana)
- **Slaying of Madhu and Kaitabha** — Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, ordering creation against primordial chaos _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Brahma, Yoganidra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Mahabharata, Devi Mahatmya 1, Bhagavata Purana)
- **The Sārameyas guard Yama's path of the dead** — Saramā's two four-eyed brindled hounds, Śyāma and Śabala/Śarvara, watch the road the dead must travel to reach Yama's realm and serve as his messengers _(actors: Śyāma, Śabala/Śarvara (Sārameyas), Yama, Saramā, the dead)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/mythic-beasts-and-composites.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.14.10–12)
- **The thousand-year underwater duel** — Varāha and Hiraṇyākṣa fight a colossal mace-and-grapple battle for a thousand years; Brahmā warns Viṣṇu to finish before dusk _(actors: Varāha, Hiraṇyākṣa, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.18)
- **Vac Ambhrini Proclaims Herself the Supreme Power** — The seeress Vac Ambhrini, daughter of Ambhrina, speaks in the first person proclaiming the goddess Speech as the supreme power pervading all gods — the Vedic seed of Shakta theology _(actors: Vac Ambhrini)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedic-deities-and-suktas.md) — (Rigveda 10.125 (Devi Sukta))
- **Veda-theft by the demon and recovery** — A demon (Hayagrīva/Śaṅkhāsura) steals the Vedas from a sleeping Brahmā; Matsya slays him and restores the scriptures (Purāṇic strand) _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Brahmā, demon Hayagrīva / Śaṅkhāsura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24)
- **Wedding of Shiva and Parvati** — After Parvati's penance, the Saptarishi arrange the divine wedding of Shiva and Parvati, drawing all the gods to Himavan's city _(actors: Shiva, Parvati, Himavan, Saptarishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Kumarasambhava 6-7, Shiva Purana)
- **Aṅgiras takes up the function of fire** — When Agni withdraws, Aṅgiras blazes as the sacrificial fire and is honoured as Agni's first kindler/father _(actors: Aṅgiras, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Mahābhārata (Anuśāsana / Vana Parvan))
- **Birth of birds, beasts and remaining classes** — From Tāmrā, Surabhi, Surasā, Ariṣṭā, Krodhavaśā, Irā, Khasā and Muni descend birds, cattle, Gandharvas, beasts, plants, Yakṣas/Rākṣasas and Apsarases _(actors: Kaśyapa, his remaining wives, the bestiary)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.21)
- **Doctrine of the three births and Prajnanam Brahma** — The Aitareya Upanishad teaches a man's three births (seed, womb, rebirth), cites Vamadeva's prenatal knowledge, and proclaims the mahavakya prajnanam brahma _(actors: Vamadeva, the embodied self)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/aitareya-brahmana.md) — (Aitareya Aranyaka II; Aitareya Upanishad 2-3)
- **Hiraṇyākṣa-vadha and re-establishment of the Earth** — Varāha sets the Earth on the waters and slays Hiraṇyākṣa with a blow at the root of the ear, discharging the first Jaya–Vijaya birth _(actors: Varāha, Hiraṇyākṣa, the Earth, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/varaha-hiranyaksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.19, 7.1)
- **Kadrū–Vinatā wager over Uccaiḥśravas' tail** — The wager between Kadrū and Vinatā over the colour of the churning-born horse Uccaiḥśravas' tail triggers Vinatā's enslavement, the origin of Garuḍa's nectar-quest and the Nāga–bird enmity _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, Uccaiḥśravas, Garuḍa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Uchchaihshravas (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Madhu-Kaitabha slain by Vishnu** — Two demons born from Vishnu's ear-wax threaten the newborn Brahma and steal the Vedas; Vishnu slays them, asserting order against primordial chaos _(actors: Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Mahabharata; Devi Mahatmya 1; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Narakas placed as a distinct tier below the patalas** — The 28 punitive narakas are located below all seven patalas in Yama's southern quarter, kept textually and geographically separate from the paradisal bila-svarga _(actors: Yama, the sinful dead)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/bila-svarga-and-the-patalas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.26.5)
- **Parvati becomes Gauri and Annapurna** — Parvati performs tapas to shed her dark complexion as Gauri (the cast sheath becoming Kali), and manifests as Annapurna at Kashi to feed even Shiva _(actors: Parvati (Gauri, Annapurna), Shiva, Kali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana, Annapurna Upanishad / Sthala-purana)
- **Satyavrata reborn as Vaivasvata Manu** — When the waters recede Satyavrata is installed as Vaivasvata, the seventh Manu and progenitor of the present Manvantara _(actors: Satyavrata / Vaivasvata Manu, Matsya (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/matsya-pralaya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.24)
- **Taittirīya Āraṇyaka composed** — Ten-prapāṭhaka Krishna-Yajurveda forest text spanning the Āruṇa solar section, Pravargya, Pitṛmedha, and embedded Upaniṣads _(actors: Taittirīya school Adhvaryus)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (10 prapāṭhakas))
- **The Cosmic Egg (Brahmanda) splits open** — The creator's golden seed becomes an egg incubating on the waters; it splits — upper shell to heaven, lower to earth, the space between to sky _(actors: Brahma (Svayambhu))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Manusmriti 1.5-13, Vishnu Purana 1.2)
- **Yājñavalkya's Upaniṣadic dialogues (Bṛhadāraṇyaka)** — The closing kāṇḍa records Yājñavalkya's dialogues with Maitreyī, Gārgī, and King Janaka, articulating neti neti and Ātman = Brahman _(actors: Yājñavalkya, Maitreyī, Gārgī, King Janaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/shatapatha-brahmana.md) — (Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa, closing kāṇḍa (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad; Mādhyandina kāṇḍa 14 / Kāṇva book 17))
- **Aṅgiras teaches Śaunaka the two knowledges** — In the Atharvanic transmission Aṅgiras instructs the householder Śaunaka in the parā/aparā (higher/lower) knowledge distinction _(actors: Aṅgiras, Śaunaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 1.1)
- **Forging of Sudarśana, Triśūla, and Puṣpaka from Sūrya's radiance** — When Saṃjñā could not bear Sūrya's heat, Viśvakarmā grinds the sun on his lathe and forges Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra, Śiva's Triśūla, and the Puṣpaka Vimāna from the shavings of solar radiance _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Sūrya, Saṃjñā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia); Ayudhapurusha)
- **Taittirīya Upaniṣad embedded** — Praśnas 7–9 form the Taittirīya Upaniṣad with its three vallīs (Śikṣā, Brahmānanda, Bhṛgu) _(actors: Bhṛgu; Varuṇa; the teacher-pupil)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 7–9 (Taittirīya Upaniṣad))
- **Varaha lifts the Earth at the Kalpa's dawn** — At the dawn of the current Shveta-Varaha Kalpa, Vishnu as the boar Varaha lifts the Earth from the cosmic waters, the act that names this Day of Brahma _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha avatara))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.4; Bhagavata Purana 3.13)
- **Varaha lifts the earth at the Shveta-Varaha Kalpa's dawn** — The current kalpa is named Shveta-Varaha for Vishnu's boar avatara who lifted the earth at its dawn on the first day of Brahma's 51st year _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha))_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalpa-and-pralaya.md) — (Vishnu Purana I.4)
- **Aṅgiras's manvantara recurrences** — On the scriptural clock Aṅgiras re-manifests across world-ages as Saptarṣi/Prajāpati, his name an office recurring each cycle and distinguished from his later namesake descendants _(actors: Aṅgiras, the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/angiras.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.1–2)
- **Brahma seeks the root of the lotus-stalk** — Brahma, born on the lotus and ignorant of his origin, descends the stalk seeking its root, fails, performs tapas, and is granted vision of Vishnu, establishing Vishnu's supremacy _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.8-9)
- **Devi creates the Trimurti (Shakta account)** — The Supreme Goddess (Adi Parashakti) brings forth Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti from her own portions _(actors: Mahadevi (Adi Parashakti), Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana 3, Devi Mahatmya)
- **Kaśyapa drains lake Satīsaras and founds Kashmir** — Kaśyapa, with Viṣṇu and the gods, breaches the mountain at Varāhamūla to drain lake Satīsaras; Viṣṇu slays Jalodbhava and the valley Kaśmīra is named for and settled by Kaśyapa _(actors: Kaśyapa, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Jalodbhava, the Nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Nīlamata Purāṇa; Rājataraṅgiṇī 1.25–28)
- **Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad as TĀ prapāṭhaka 10** — Prapāṭhaka 10 of the Taittirīya Āraṇyaka is the Mahānārāyaṇa (Yājñikī) Upaniṣad, hymning Nārāyaṇa as Brahman and supplying sandhyā and sannyāsa mantras _(actors: Nārāyaṇa as supreme Brahman/Antaryāmin)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka 10 (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad))
- **Martanda cast away and reclaimed as Surya** — In the Rigvedic account Aditi casts away her eighth son Martanda, who is reclaimed as Surya the Sun _(actors: Aditi, Martanda/Surya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Rigveda)
- **Agastya Mediates Indra and the Maruts** — As Rigvedic seer Agastya composes hymns mediating a quarrel between Indra and the storm-gods, reconciling the Indra-Maruts dispute _(actors: Agastya, Indra, the Maruts)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/agastya.md) — (Rigveda 1.165, 1.170-1.171)
- **Brahma forms within the cosmic egg and splits it** — The creator's seed becomes a golden egg incubating a divine year; Brahma develops within and splits it into heavens, earth, and the sky between, with fluids becoming mountains and oceans _(actors: Brahma / Svayambhu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Manusmriti 1.5-13; Vishnu Purana 1.2)
- **Embedded suktas and famous mantras housed in the TĀ** — The Taittirīya Āraṇyaka houses Yajurvedic Puruṣa-, Nārāyaṇa-, Bhū-, Durgā-, and Medhā-sūktas plus the Mṛtyuñjaya/Tryambaka mantra _(actors: Puruṣa; Nārāyaṇa; Rudra-Tryambaka; Durgā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Taittirīya Āraṇyaka (3, 10))
- **Kaśyapa father of Vāmana** — On Kaśyapa's instruction Aditi performs the Payovrata and Viṣṇu is born to the couple as the dwarf Vāmana to reclaim the worlds from Bali _(actors: Kaśyapa, Aditi, Vāmana/Viṣṇu, Bali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kashyapa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.16–18)
- **Primary unfolding of prakriti (Prakrita sarga)** — From Vishnu's will, unmanifest prakriti is disturbed and the gunas lose equilibrium, emitting mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses, and gross elements into the cosmic egg _(actors: Vishnu, Brahma, Prakriti)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.2, Bhagavata Purana 3.5)
- **Viśvakarmā forges the twin bows Pināka and Śārṅga** — To settle the Śiva–Viṣṇu superiority contest, Viśvakarmā crafts the twin bows Pināka (Śiva) and Śārṅga (Viṣṇu); Viṣṇu 'wins' and Śiva's bow passes to the kings of Mithilā _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Śiva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa; divine-bows tradition)
- **Bhairava severs Brahmā's fifth head** — From his fury at the arrogant fifth head of Brahmā, Śiva manifests Kāla Bhairava, who shears off the offending head, incurring brahmahatyā that clings as a skull until expiated at Kāśī _(actors: Kāla Bhairava, Brahmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Śatarudra-saṃhitā; Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Brahma creates the universe and begins time (Ugadi charter)** — The Gudi Padwa/Ugadi charter marks the day Brahma created the universe and began kala (time) — Yuga-adi, the 'beginning of the age' _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (traditional)
- **Lingodbhava — the infinite pillar of light** — Brahma and Vishnu dispute supremacy when an endless fiery jyotirlinga appears; neither finds its end and Shiva emerges from the linga as the true source of both _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Āraṇyaka–Upaniṣad embedding map** — Each surviving Āraṇyaka embeds a principal Upaniṣad; the Bṛhadāraṇyaka is simultaneously Āraṇyaka and Upaniṣad of the Śukla Yajurveda _(actors: Yājñavalkya; the four śruti strata)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/aranyakas.md) — (Aitareya, Kauṣītaki, Taittirīya, Bṛhadāraṇyaka traditions)
- **The nine creations (sargas) of Brahma** — Creation proceeds through nine graded sargas — three elemental (Prakrita) and five derived (Vaikrita) plus the Kaumara — from Mahat down to the Kumaras _(actors: Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.5, Bhagavata Purana 3.10)
- **Birth of the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — Brahma produces from his mind the Brahmarshis/Prajapatis — Bhrigu, Pulastya, Pulaha, Kratu, Angiras, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, Vasishtha — progenitors of all beings _(actors: Brahma, the nine Prajapatis)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7, Manusmriti 1.34-35)
- **Yoganidra withdraws so Vishnu slays Madhu-Kaitabha** — At a cycle's start the Goddess as Yoganidra withdraws from the sleeping Vishnu so he can wake and slay Madhu and Kaitabha, showing the Goddess drives even Vishnu's creative role _(actors: Devi (Yoganidra/Mahamaya), Vishnu, Madhu, Kaitabha)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Devi brings forth the Trimurti** — The Supreme Goddess brings forth Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, assigns their cosmic functions, and grants each a consort-shakti who is her own portion _(actors: Mahadevi, Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana 3)
- **The Kumaras refuse to procreate** — Brahma's first sons, the four eternal celibate Sanaka-kumaras, reject creation and remain renunciant, frustrating Brahma's plan to populate the world _(actors: Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanatana, Sanatkumara, Brahma)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12, Vishnu Purana 1.7)
- **Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the sacrificial fire** — Lalita Tripurasundari manifests from the cosmic fire of the gods' sacrifice and creates and orders the worlds _(actors: Lalita Tripurasundari)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Brahmanda Purana (Lalitopakhyana))
- **Lingodbhava establishes Shiva's supremacy** — Shiva manifests as an infinite column of fire whose top (Brahma as swan) and bottom (Vishnu as boar) neither can find, establishing his supremacy and grounding the 12 Jyotirlingas _(actors: Shiva, Brahma, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana Vidyeshvara Samhita)
- **Brahma splits into Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his body into male and female halves becoming Svayambhuva Manu (the first Manu) and Shatarupa, whose union begins the human dynastic line _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7, Manusmriti 1.32)
- **Primary unfolding of prakriti into the tattvas** — From Vishnu's will unmanifest prakriti is disturbed, the gunas lose equilibrium, and mahat, ahamkara, the tanmatras, senses and gross elements emerge in sequence, forming the cosmic egg _(actors: Vishnu, Prakriti/Pradhana)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.2; Bhagavata Purana 3.5, 3.26)
- **Brahma emanates the mind-born sons (Manasaputras)** — Brahma produces his Brahmarshi/Prajapati sons from his mind, the progenitors of all beings _(actors: Brahma, Bhrigu, Marichi, Daksha, Atri, Vasishtha and others)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7; Manusmriti 1.34-35)
- **Daksha populates the worlds (maithuni srishti)** — Daksha Prajapati fathers numerous daughters who, married to gods and sages, become mothers of devas, asuras, animals, and all living kinds, beginning sexual generation _(actors: Daksha, Kashyapa, Aditi, Diti, Danu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.15, 1.21, Bhagavata Purana 6.6)
- **Birth of Rudra from Brahma's anger** — Enraged at the Kumaras' refusal, Brahma emits Rudra (half male, half female) from his brow; bidden to divide, the male becomes eleven Rudras and the female the shaktis _(actors: Brahma, Rudra)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/cosmogony-creation-accounts.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.7; Bhagavata Purana 3.12)
- **Vishnu's cosmic sleep induced by Mahamaya** — Vishnu's cosmic sleep is induced by Yoganidra/Mahamaya, the deluding power of the Goddess, in the Devi Mahatmya opening _(actors: Vishnu, Mahamaya (Yoganidra))_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/maya-and-avidya.md) — (Devi Mahatmya 1)
- **Innumerable universes from Maha-Vishnu's breath** — Universes (brahmandas) emanate like bubbles with each exhalation of Maha-Vishnu, each sealed in seven concentric layers, a Brahma born in each _(actors: Maha-Vishnu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/brahma-lifetime.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2.5, 3.11, Brahma Samhita 5.11-13)
- **Birth of Narmada from Shiva** — The river Narmada is born from a drop of Shiva's sweat during the tandava and granted to be imperishable, alone flowing through pralayas _(actors: Shiva, Narmada, Markandeya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Skanda Purana, Reva-khanda; Narmada Purana)
- **The cosmic lotus and Brahmā spring from reclining Viṣṇu** — From the navel of Viṣṇu reclining on Ananta-Śeṣa springs the cosmic lotus bearing Brahmā, who begins the next creation _(actors: Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Śeṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Birth of the Maruts from Rudra and Pṛśni** — In the Vedic account the storm-troop Maruts are born together as sons of Rudra and the dappled cow-goddess Pṛśni, self-arising from the storm _(actors: Rudra, Pṛśni, Maruts)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-maruts.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.85; 5.57–60)
- **Brahmā emits the mind-born sons** — At the dawn of the kalpa Brahmā emits his first conscious beings, the mānasaputra Prajāpatis and seers, from his mind/body without sexual union _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Manusmṛti 1.34–35; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **The four Kumāras refuse procreation** — Brahmā's first mind-sons, the four Kumāras, are born fully realized and choose eternal childhood and celibacy, the 'failed first creation' that forces Brahmā to emit the procreating Prajāpatis _(actors: Brahmā, Sanaka, Sanandana, Sanātana, Sanatkumāra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12.4–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Brahmā emits Manu Svāyambhuva and Śatarūpā** — To get creation moving Brahmā emits from his body the first man Manu Svāyambhuva and the first woman Śatarūpā _(actors: Brahmā, Manu Svāyambhuva, Śatarūpā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **The Kumāras curse Jaya and Vijaya** — Barred from Vaikuṇṭha by the gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya, the wrathful Kumāras curse the pair to three demonic births, the engine of three of Viṣṇu's avatāra-descents _(actors: Kumāras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-prajapatis.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.15–16, 7.1)
- **Aditi casts away and recovers Mārtāṇḍa** — In the original Āditya account, the mother Aditi flings away the 'dead egg' eighth son Mārtāṇḍa (Sūrya) and then recovers him _(actors: Aditi, Mārtāṇḍa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Ṛgveda 2.27; 10.72.8–9)
- **Rudras born from Brahmā's weeping brow** — The eleven Rudras are born from Brahmā's brow when he wept, hence their name from rud, 'to cry' _(actors: Brahmā, Rudras)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/the-thirty-three-devas.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.12)
- **Birth of the Vālakhilyas to Kratu** — The Saptarṣi-Prajāpati Kratu and his wife Sannati beget sixty-thousand thumb-sized celibate ascetic sons, the Vālakhilyas, who escort the Sun's chariot _(actors: Kratu, Sannati, Vālakhilyas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Mahābhārata)

## The Earlier Manvantaras (1–6) & Primordial Reigns  ·  485 events

*Events of the six manvantaras before ours, and the primordial kings/sages (Dhruva, Pṛthu, Vena, Daksha).*

- **Aṅga Abandons the Throne over Vena** — King Aṅga weds Sunīthā, daughter of Death, whose evil grandson Vena is born; despairing of his wicked son, Aṅga abandons the throne for the forest _(actors: Aṅga, Sunīthā, Vena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.13; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Ajāmila's fall and life of sin** — The virtuous brāhmaṇa Ajāmila is ruined by lust for a dāsī, abandons his wife and dharma, and lives by theft and deceit, naming his youngest son Nārāyaṇa _(actors: Ajāmila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.1)
- **Atri and Anasūyā's austerity for a divine son** — The sage Atri and his wife Anasūyā perform severe tapas seeking a son equal to the Supreme, and the Trimūrti grant that portions of all three will be born to them _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Avatar Satyasena destroys the evil spirits** — Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and Dharma, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas and lying bhutas, fighting beside Indra Satyajit _(actors: Satyasena, Sunrita, Dharma, Indra Satyajit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1.25)
- **Avatar Vaikuntha creates the realm of Vaikuntha** — Vishnu's avatar Vaikuntha, born of his own accord, creates his eternal abode Vaikuntha at the request of his consort Rama (Lakshmi) _(actors: Vaikuntha (Vishnu), Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Betrothal of Ruru and Pramadvarā** — The Bhārgava youth Ruru is betrothed to Pramadvarā, foundling daughter of the apsarā Menakā reared by sage Sthūlakeśa, and a wedding-day is fixed _(actors: Ruru, Pramadvarā, Pramati, Sthūlakeśa, Menakā, Viśvāvasu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva (~1.8–12))
- **Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu's chest, origin of the Śrīvatsa mark** — The sage Bhṛgu kicks Viṣṇu on the chest to test which of the three gods is greatest (the trimūrti-test). Far from angered, Viṣṇu honours and embraces the foot-mark; the auspicious whorl left on his breast becomes the Śrīvatsa, and Lakṣmī (Śrī), born of the milk-ocean, takes her seat there _(actors: Bhṛgu, Viṣṇu, Lakṣmī/Śrī)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-symbols-and-emblems.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.89)
- **Birth of Andhaka from Parvati's covering of Shiva's eyes** — Parvati playfully covers Shiva's three eyes, plunging the cosmos into darkness; a drop of her sweat becomes the blind, deformed boy Andhaka _(actors: Parvati, Shiva, Andhaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Birth of Cyavana** — The Rākṣasa Puloman abducts the pregnant Pulomā, and the unborn Bhārgava child slips prematurely from the womb (hence 'Cyavana'), his radiance burning the Rākṣasa to ashes _(actors: Bhṛgu, Pulomā, Puloman, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 5–6)
- **Birth of Jalandhara from Shiva's brow-fire** — The fire from Shiva's opened third eye is cast into the ocean and gestated into the asura Jalandhara _(actors: Shiva, Indra, Brahma, Samudra (ocean), Jalandhara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Rudra-samhita, Yuddha-khanda))
- **Birth of Kapila to Kardama and Devahuti** — Viṣṇu descends as the son of the patriarch Kardama and Devahūti in the Svāyambhuva Manvantara to teach Sāṃkhya-yoga _(actors: Kardama, Devahūti, Kapila (Viṣṇu avatāra), Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.22–24, 1.3.10)
- **Birth of Rishabhadeva from Merudevi** — King Nabhi and Merudevi perform a sacrifice longing for a son, and Vishnu descends, born as Rishabha (the bull), counted an avatara of Narayana _(actors: Nabhi, Merudevi, Vishnu/Rishabhadeva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.3; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Birth of the avatar Vaikuntha** — In the Raivata Manvantara Vishnu manifests of his own accord as Lord Vaikuntha, born together with the deva-class called Vaikunthas _(actors: Vaikuntha, the Vaikuntha gods, Rama (Lakshmi))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Birth of Vaivasvata Manu** — Vaivasvata, the 7th and current Manu, is born of Surya (Vivasvat) and Saranyu/Chhaya, becoming the present progenitor of humankind _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Surya, Saranyu/Chhaya)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13)
- **Birth of Viśravas from Pulastya** — The rākṣasa line descends from Brahmā's mind-born son Pulastya, whose circumstance at Tṛṇabindu's hermitage produces the sage Viśravas _(actors: Pulastya, Viśravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 2–3)
- **Birth of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā to Ākūti and Ruci** — Viṣṇu descends as the twin Yajña (a portion of Viṣṇu) alongside his sister-consort Dakṣiṇā, born to Ākūti (daughter of Svāyambhuva Manu) and the Prajāpati Ruci _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Yajña), Dakṣiṇā, Ākūti, Ruci, Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.3.10, 4.1.4–7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Brahma to Vaivasvata Manu Descent** — The cosmological spine runs Brahma to Marichi to Kashyapa to Vivasvan (Surya) to Vaivasvata Manu, whose children fork into the two royal dynasties _(actors: Brahma, Kashyapa, Surya, Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV; Bhagavata Purana IX)
- **Chakshusha Manu's previous-birth as Ananda** — Before becoming the sixth Manu, the future Chakshusha lives as Ananda, switched at birth by a cat into a royal household, and on learning the truth withdraws to the forest for tapas, whereupon Brahma blesses him to be reborn as Manu _(actors: Ananda/Chakshusha, Anamitra, King Vikranta, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **Daṇḍa violates Arajā** — Ikṣvāku's son Daṇḍa, king at Madhumanta, ravishes Arajā the daughter of Śukrācārya in the forest near the sage's hermitage _(actors: Daṇḍa, Arajā, Śukrācārya (Uśanas Kāvya))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dandakaranya-rama-forest.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 79–81)
- **Dadhīci teaches the Madhu-vidyā through a horse's head** — To evade Indra's curse, the Aśvins fit Dadhyañc with a horse's head so he can teach them the honey-doctrine, then restore his own head _(actors: Dadhīci (Dadhyañc), the Aśvins, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 2.5; Ṛgveda 1.116–117)
- **Daksha's Yajna and Snub of Shiva** — Daksha Prajapati holds a great sacrifice and deliberately omits to invite Shiva and Sati out of contempt for his ascetic son-in-law _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana)
- **Descent of the Gomatī from Vasiṣṭha's tapas** — The river-goddess Gomatī is born as the daughter of the brahmarṣi Vasiṣṭha, flowing forth from his tapas to purify the earth; she wells up at the spring-tank Gomat Tāl (Fulhar Jheel) and becomes the river of Naimiṣāraṇya _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Gomatī (nadī-devatā))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sacred-rivers-and-descent-myths.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.75.6 (Nadīstuti); Gomatī-māhātmya / Skanda Purāṇa; sthala-tradition)
- **Dhruva is slighted by his stepmother and vows penance** — The boy-prince Dhruva, pushed from his father's lap by queen Suruci's scorn, resolves to win the highest station and leaves for the forest _(actors: Dhruva, Suruci, Sunīti, Uttānapāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Founding of Ayodhya by Manu Vaivasvata** — Vaivasvata Manu lays out Ayodhya on the south bank of the Sarayu as the capital of Kosala, founding the Suryavamsha/Ikshvaku city _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/ayodhya.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Bala-kanda 1.5; Skanda Purana Ayodhya-mahatmya)
- **Founding of Ayodhyā by Manu Vaivasvata** — Ayodhya, the unconquerable city and Suryavamsha capital, is founded by Manu Vaivasvata himself as one of the oldest cities _(actors: Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Founding of Videha-Mithilā** — The bodiless king Nimi's churned-out son Mithi founds Mithilā, establishing the Videha/Janaka line that will rule from Janakpur _(actors: Nimi, Mithi, the Janaka dynasty)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/janakpur-mithila-sita-janmabhumi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa 70-71; Viṣṇu Purāṇa)
- **Gajendra-moksha** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile and dragged toward death over a thousand celestial years, surrenders to the Supreme and is rescued by Vishnu, who arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his Sudarshana chakra _(actors: Gajendra, Vishnu (avatar Hari), the crocodile (Huhu), Garuda)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Gajendra-moksha (liberation of Gajendra)** — The elephant-king Gajendra, seized by a crocodile, surrenders to the Supreme; Vishnu arrives on Garuda and severs the crocodile with his chakra _(actors: Gajendra, the crocodile (Huhu), Vishnu, Indradyumna)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-8.4)
- **Jahnu listed among the sons of Kuru** — Purāṇic rosters place Jahnu as a son of Kuru in the Pauravā throne-line, though son-lists vary by recension _(actors: Jahnu, Kuru)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.22)
- **Jaratkāru beholds his Pitṛs over the pit** — The celibate ascetic Jaratkāru finds his forefathers hanging head-down over an abyss, their lineage-rope gnawed by the rat of Time because he refuses to beget a son _(actors: Jaratkāru; his Pitṛs (ancestors))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva (~1.13–53))
- **Kacha steals the Mṛtasañjīvanī vidyā** — Bṛhaspati's son Kacha serves Śukra to learn the dead-reviving mantra; killed thrice by the asuras and revived from Śukra's own belly, he masters it _(actors: Kacha, Śukrācārya, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 71-72)
- **Kapila descends and teaches Samkhya to Devahuti** — The sage Kapila, an avatara of Vishnu, descends and expounds the Samkhya tattva-system (the Kapila-gita) to his mother Devahuti, the foundational teaching of the school _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/the-samkhya-tattvas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **Krishna teaches the imperishable yoga to Vivasvan, Manu, and Ikshvaku** — Krishna recounts that at the dawn of the current Manvantara he first taught this imperishable yoga to the sun-god Vivasvan, who told Manu, who told Ikshvaku, a royal-sage lineage later lost and now restored _(actors: Krishna, Vivasvan, Manu, Ikshvaku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/03-to-06-karma-shatka.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 4.1-3)
- **Kubera's penance and Brahma's boons** — Kubera performs severe tapas standing on one leg and Brahma grants him immortality, lordship of all wealth and the nine nidhis, the office of Lokapala of the North, and the Pushpaka vimana _(actors: Kubera, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kubera.md) — (Ramayana; Puranic tradition)
- **Mṛkaṇḍu's Boon and Choice** — The childless sage Mṛkaṇḍu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son destined to live only sixteen years over a dull long-lived one _(actors: Mṛkaṇḍu, Marudvatī, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Penance of Tāraka's sons** — Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, and Kamalākṣa undertake fierce penance to avenge their slain father Tāraka _(actors: Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa (sons of Tāraka))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā); Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Pravara rejects Varuthini** — The pious brahmana Pravara, stranded in the Himalayas after a flying-paste wears off, is propositioned by the lovesick apsaras Varuthini but refuses her, bound by his vow of one wife _(actors: Pravara, Varuthini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **Saraṇyū flees Vivasvat and the substitute is made** — After bearing Vivasvat twin children, Saraṇyū vanishes; the gods fashion a likeness (savarṇā) in her place, on whom the Aśvins are later begotten _(actors: Saraṇyū, Vivasvat, Tvaṣṭṛ)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.17.1-2; Nirukta 12.10; Bṛhaddevatā 6.162ff)
- **Sati born as Daksha's daughter** — The Great Goddess consents to be born as a daughter of the Prajapati Daksha, named Sati, specifically to win Shiva as her husband _(actors: Adi Shakti (Sati), Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita Sati Khanda; Devi-Bhagavata Purana VII)
- **Satyasena destroys the Yakshas and evil spirits** — Vishnu's avatar Satyasena, born of Sunrita and accompanied by the Satyavratas, destroys the Yakshas, Rakshasas, and lying evil spirits, fighting alongside Indra Satyajit in the Uttama manvantara _(actors: Satyasena, Sunrita, Satyavratas, Indra Satyajit)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1.25)
- **Saudāsa's clash with Śakti and the curse of cannibalism** — Ikṣvāku king Saudāsa meets Vasiṣṭha's son Śakti on a narrow path, insults/strikes him, and is cursed to become a man-eating rākṣasa _(actors: Saudāsa (Mitrasaha), Śakti (Śaktri, son of Vasiṣṭha))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva (Vasiṣṭha upākhyāna))
- **Soma abducts Tara** — The moon-god Soma, proud after his Rajasuya, carries off Tara, the chaste wife of Brihaspati, and refuses to return her _(actors: Soma, Tara, Brihaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Soma abducts Tārā, igniting the Tārakāmaya War** — The moon-god Soma carries off Tārā, wife of Bṛhaspati, and refuses to return her, sparking the fifth Devāsura war _(actors: Soma (Chandra), Tārā, Bṛhaspati, Śukra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.6; Devī-Bhāgavata 1.11)
- **Sukanyā pierces the anthill-sage Cyavana's eyes** — Princess Sukanyā blinds the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn; his tapas afflicts her father Śaryāti's army _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Suruci humiliates the child Dhruva** — When five-year-old Dhruva climbs onto his father Uttānapāda's lap, the proud queen Suruci taunts that the royal lap is not for a rival's son unless he is reborn from her or wins it by propitiating Viṣṇu _(actors: Dhruva, Suruci, Uttānapāda, Uttama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Surya weds Saranyu and she flees as a mare** — Surya weds Saranyu, daughter of Vishvakarma, but unable to bear his blaze she leaves behind her shadow-double Chhaya and flees as a mare _(actors: Surya, Saranyu/Sanjna, Chhaya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Rig Veda 10.17; Markandeya & Matsya Puranas)
- **The sages slay the tyrant Vena** — King Vena forbids all sacrifice and proclaims himself the sole god; the enraged brāhmaṇas kill him with charged mantras _(actors: Vena, the sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.14; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **The twelve-year drought and Varuṇa's boon** — During a long Deccan drought, sage Gautama propitiates Varuṇa and gains unfailing grain/water at Brahmagiri, feeding the starving sages _(actors: Gautama, Ahalyā, Varuṇa, gathered ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya))
- **The twelve-year sattra of Shaunaka at Naimisha** — 88,000 sages assemble in Naimisharanya for a perpetual long-session Soma-sacrifice led by Kulapati Shaunaka, the setting for hearing the Puranas _(actors: Shaunaka, the 88,000 rishis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1.4; Vayu Purana 1.11-12)
- **Tāraka's tapas and boon** — The daitya Tāraka performs fierce penance and wins from Brahmā the boon that he can die only by a (seven-day-old) son of Śiva _(actors: Tāraka, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Kumāra-khaṇḍa); Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Trimūrti test Anasūyā and are reborn as her sons** — Sent to break Anasūyā's chastity, Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva are turned into infants by her power and reborn as Soma, Dattātreya, and Durvāsā _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Viṣṇu gifts Ambarīṣa the Sudarśana and the Ekādaśī vow** — Pleased by Ambarīṣa's total devotion, Viṣṇu awards him the Sudarśana-cakra as guardian; the king undertakes a year-long Ekādaśī vow _(actors: Ambarīṣa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4)
- **Yama becomes the first mortal to die and king of the dead** — Yama, son of Vivasvat and twin of Yami, is the first mortal to die and thereby becomes king of the dead, lord of Naraka in the southern quarter _(actors: Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/narakas-and-afterlife.md) — (Rig Veda 10.14; Garuda Purana)
- **Yuvanāśva drinks the consecrated fertility-water** — The childless Ikṣvāku king Yuvanāśva, parched at night, accidentally drinks the mantra-charged conception-water the sages had prepared for his queen _(actors: Yuvanāśva, the ṛṣis (officiants of the Indra-yajña), the queen (intended drinker))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.28–33)
- **Ajāmila cries 'Nārāyaṇa' and is saved by the Viṣṇudūtas** — Dying, Ajāmila calls his son's name 'Nārāyaṇa'; four Viṣṇudūtas stop the Yamadūtas and debate the saving power of the holy name _(actors: Ajāmila, Viṣṇudūtas, Yamadūtas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.1–6.2)
- **Anasūyā turns the Trimūrti into infants** — When the disguised Trimūrti demand to be served food naked to break her vow, Anasūyā by the power of her chastity transforms them into crying babies and serves them without sin _(actors: Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Andhaka adopted by Hiranyaksha and granted a boon** — Shiva gives the dark boy to the childless daitya Hiranyaksha, who rears him; Andhaka wins from Brahma a boon making him slayable only if he lusts after his own mother _(actors: Shiva, Hiranyaksha, Andhaka, Brahma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana; Matsya Purana; Vamana Purana)
- **Atri serves as Saptarṣi of the Vaivasvata Manvantara** — Atri is installed among the Seven Sages presiding over the present Vaivasvata Manvantara _(actors: Atri, the Saptarṣi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.1)
- **Bharata gives the dynasty its name** — From Dushyanta and Shakuntala is born Bharata, after whom Bharata-varsha and the Mahabharata are named _(actors: Dushyanta, Shakuntala, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 68-74)
- **Birth of Māndhātṛ from his father's side** — The child gestates within Yuvanāśva and is delivered by splitting open the king's flank, the father surviving by the sages'/Aśvins' grace _(actors: Yuvanāśva, the infant Māndhātṛ, the sages / Aśvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.34–36)
- **Birth of Mārkaṇḍeya** — The radiant son is born and named Mārkaṇḍeya, mastering the Vedas precociously while his parents conceal his death-date _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Mṛkaṇḍu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Birth of Nandi** — The bull-faced Nandi is born to sage Shilada by Shiva's grace and is made chief of Shiva's hosts and eternal gatekeeper and mount _(actors: Nandishvara (Shiva), Shilada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Birth of Nara and Narayana** — The twin sage-incarnations of Vishnu, Nara and Narayana, are born as sons of Dharma and Murti/Ahimsa, becoming the perpetual ascetics of Badarikashrama (later reincarnated as Arjuna and Krishna) _(actors: Nara, Narayana, Dharma, Murti)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Puranic Encyclopaedia / Devi-Bhagavata; (variant: Bhagavata Purana 4.1 places in Svayambhuva))
- **Birth of the avatar Hari** — Vishnu manifests in the Tamasa Manvantara as the avatar Hari, son of sage Harimedha and his wife Harini, born expressly to liberate the devotee Gajendra _(actors: Hari, Harimedha, Harini)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-04-tamasa.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Brahma's prophecy and naming** — The infant grips Brahma's beard; Brahma names him Jalandhara and decrees he can be slain only by Shiva _(actors: Brahma, Jalandhara, Samudra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda))
- **Brahmā restores Tārā; birth and naming of Budha** — Brahmā halts the war and recovers the pregnant Tārā; she confesses the child is Soma's, and Soma names the boy Budha, founder of the Lunar line _(actors: Brahmā, Soma, Tārā, Bṛhaspati, Budha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 4.6; Bhāgavata 9.14)
- **Brahmā's boon of the three cities** — Brahmā grants three impregnable flying cities destructible only by a single arrow at a once-in-a-millennium alignment _(actors: Brahmā, the three asura brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa)
- **Creation of Svayambhuva Manu and Shatarupa** — Brahma divides his own body into male and female halves, the male becoming Svayambhuva Manu and the female Shatarupa, the first human couple and progenitors of mankind _(actors: Brahma, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Manusmriti 1; Vishnu Purana 1; Bhagavata Purana 3-4)
- **Creation of Vaikuntha realm** — At the request of his consort the goddess Rama (Lakshmi), the avatar Vaikuntha creates the supreme eternal abode known as Vaikuntha to please her _(actors: Vaikuntha, Rama/Lakshmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5)
- **Dadhīci gives his bones for Indra's vajra** — To slay Vṛtra, Dadhīci yields his life so his thunder-charged spine can be forged by Viśvakarman into the vajra _(actors: Dadhīci, Indra, Viṣṇu, Viśvakarman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dadhichi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9–10)
- **Dakṣa-prajāpati's daughters wed the gods** — Dakṣa's daughters marry Kaśyapa, Soma and others, seeding the gods, demons, and creatures in the standard Prajāpati genealogy _(actors: Dakṣa, Kaśyapa, Soma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus of nature** — As the avadhūta sage, Dattātreya tells King Yadu how he learned liberation from twenty-four teachers drawn from the natural world _(actors: Dattātreya, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.7–9)
- **Devahuti's plea for liberation** — The aged, lonely Devahūti approaches her divine son Kapila and asks him to dispel the darkness of saṃsāra, opening the discourse _(actors: Devahūti, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.25.7–11)
- **Devi-Mahatmya frame: Suratha and Samadhi worship the Goddess** — In the Svarochisha manvantara King Suratha and the merchant Samadhi worship the Goddess, and Suratha is reborn as the future Savarni Manu _(actors: King Suratha, Samadhi, the Goddess)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/README.md) — (Markandeya Purana / Devi-Mahatmya)
- **Dhruva's great penance and Viṣṇu's darśana** — Instructed by Nārada in the Vāsudeva mantra, Dhruva's escalating austerity in Madhuvana chokes the worlds and wins Viṣṇu's appearance _(actors: Dhruva, Nārada, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8–4.9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Dhruva's tapas and exaltation as the Pole Star** — The child prince Dhruva, slighted by his stepmother, performs extreme austerity, receives Vishnu's darshana, and is exalted as the immovable Dhruva-loka (Pole Star) _(actors: Dhruva, Uttanapada, Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1); cf. Bhagavata 4)
- **Dhruva's vow and departure to the forest** — Consoled by his mother Sunīti to seek refuge in Viṣṇu, the boy Dhruva resolves to win a station higher than any being ever attained and leaves the palace alone for the forest _(actors: Dhruva, Sunīti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11)
- **Durvāsā's wrath and the Sudarśana's pursuit** — Enraged over the Dvādaśī water-sip, Durvāsā hurls a fire-demon at Ambarīṣa; the Sudarśana burns it and chases the sage across the three worlds _(actors: Durvāsā, Ambarīṣa, Sudarśana, Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4)
- **Gaṅgā's descent floods Jahnu's sacrifice** — As Bhagīratha leads the descending Gaṅgā across the plains, her torrent drowns sage-king Jahnu's sacrificial enclosure _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha, Jahnu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **Gajendra's hymn of surrender and rescue by Viṣṇu** — Helpless Gajendra offers the Gajendra-stuti to the unnamed Absolute; Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa and severs the crocodile with the Sudarśana _(actors: Gajendra, Viṣṇu, Garuḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.3)
- **Gods Elect Nahuṣa as Indra** — The gods and sages install the earthly emperor Nahuṣa on heaven's throne for his unmatched tapas, augmenting his merit to hold the office _(actors: Nahuṣa, devas, ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 11-12)
- **Ila/Sudyumna and the Founding of the Lunar Line** — Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna unites with Budha (son of Candra), and their son Pururavas founds the Candravamsha _(actors: Ila/Sudyumna, Budha, Pururavas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IX.1; Shatapatha Brahmana)
- **Śiva's axe severs Gaṇeśa's tusk (Ekadanta origin)** — When the boy Gaṇeśa barred Śiva's door, Śiva's axe (the paraśu later given to Paraśurāma) struck off one of Gaṇeśa's tusks, which he refused to dodge out of respect for his father's weapon — the origin of his epithet Ekadanta ('one-tusked') _(actors: Śiva, Gaṇeśa, (Paraśurāma in variant tellings))_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Purāṇic Gaṇeśa traditions)
- **Jaratkāru vows to marry on strict conditions** — Recognizing himself as the sonless descendant, Jaratkāru pledges to wed only a same-named bride given freely whom he need not support, reserving the right to leave at the first displeasure _(actors: Jaratkāru; his Pitṛs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Kakudmi and Revati visit Brahmaloka (time dilation)** — King Kakudmi takes his daughter Revati to Brahmaloka to seek a husband; Brahma reveals 27 chaturyugas have passed on Earth during the brief wait _(actors: Kakudmi (Raivata), Revati, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-05-raivata.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.3.27-36; Vishnu Purana 4.1)
- **King Janaka attains perfection through action** — Krishna cites King Janaka and others who reached liberation through action itself, the standing proof that ruling and self-realization can coexist _(actors: Janaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/03-to-06-karma-shatka.md) — (Bhagavad Gita 3.20)
- **King Kuru Ploughs the Field of Dharma** — King Kuru ploughs the Kurukṣetra plain with a golden plough, sowing eight dharmic virtues to make it a Dharma-kṣetra _(actors: Kuru, Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Vamana Purana, Kurukshetra-mahatmya)
- **Kubera made world-guardian and lord of Laṅkā** — Kubera, son of Viśravas, wins by austerity the lordship of the north, the yakṣas, and wealth, gaining the Puṣpaka chariot and the golden city of Laṅkā _(actors: Kubera, Brahmā, Viśravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 13–15)
- **Marriage of Śaṅkhacūḍa and Tulasī; the double armor** — Śaṅkhacūḍa weds Tulasī, becoming invincible through her pativratya plus the Viṣṇu-Kavaca, and conquers the three worlds _(actors: Śaṅkhacūḍa, Tulasī, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Marriage of Kardama and Devahuti at Bindu-sarovara** — Svayambhuva Manu brings his daughter Devahuti to wed Kardama, who creates an aerial vimana for their ascetic married life _(actors: Kardama, Devahuti, Svayambhuva Manu, Shatarupa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bindu-sarovar-siddhpur.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.22-23)
- **Marriage of Yajña and Dakṣiṇā and birth of the twelve Yāmas** — Yajña weds his twin Dakṣiṇā and they father the twelve Yāma gods, who become the deva-class of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara _(actors: Yajña, Dakṣiṇā, the twelve Yāmas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1.7; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Pauloma and the birth of Cyavana** — A Rakshasa abducts the pregnant Puloma, causing the premature birth of Cyavana whose radiance burns the Rakshasa to ash, founding the Bhrigu line _(actors: Puloma, Cyavana, a Rakshasa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Pauloma Parva)
- **Pramadvarā killed by snakebite** — On the eve of the wedding Pramadvarā treads on a hidden snake and dies instantly, struck down by fate _(actors: Pramadvarā, a serpent)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Pṛthu churned from Vena's corpse and crowned first king** — The sages churn Niṣāda then the Viṣṇu-marked Pṛthu from Vena's body; Pṛthu is consecrated the first anointed king _(actors: Pṛthu, the sages, Niṣāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.15; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **Pulastya fathers Vaishravana (Kubera)** — The Prajapati Pulastya fathers Vaishravana/Kubera, who is granted lordship of wealth and the city of Lanka, angering his father's line _(actors: Pulastya, Kubera)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 257)
- **Rebirth of Vasishtha's seven sons as the Saptarishis of the Uttama manvantara** — The seven sons Vasishtha had by his wife Urja in the Svayambhuva manvantara are reborn as the Saptarishis of the third (Uttama) period, a clear sage-reincarnation statement _(actors: The seven sons of Vasishtha, Vasishtha, Urja)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-03-uttama.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.1)
- **Rishabha rains on his realm and fathers a hundred sons** — When envious Indra withholds rain, Rishabha rains by yoga-power on Ajanabha; he marries Jayanti and fathers a hundred sons, eldest Bharata, after whom the land becomes Bharata-varsha _(actors: Rishabha, Indra, Jayanti, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.4; 5.7)
- **Sañjñā creates the shadow-wife Chhāyā and flees** — Scorched by Sūrya's blaze, Sañjñā creates an identical shadow-double Chhāyā to act as his wife, then flees to the northern forests in the form of a mare _(actors: Sañjñā, Sūrya, Chhāyā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa)
- **Sati's Self-Immolation** — Sati attends Daksha's sacrifice uninvited, is insulted, and gives up her body in the sacrificial fire (or by yogic agni), the act that names sati _(actors: Sati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana; Kalika Purana)
- **Sati's tapas and marriage to Shiva** — Sati performs the Nanda-vrata austerities to obtain the ascetic Shiva, who grants the boon and weds her against Daksha's will _(actors: Sati, Shiva, Daksha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana Rudra Samhita; Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4)
- **Sukanyā pierces Cyavana's eyes** — King Śaryāti's daughter Sukanyā pierces the glowing eyes of the anthill-buried sage Cyavana with a thorn, blinding him, whereupon his tapas afflicts the king's army with retention of urine and stool _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 122–123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Sukanyā wed to Cyavana; the Aśvins restore his youth** — Sukanyā is given in atonement to the aged Cyavana; refusing the Aśvins' advances, she correctly picks her husband from three identical youths after they rejuvenate him _(actors: Sukanyā, Cyavana, the Aśvins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123–124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Suta Ugrashravas recites the Puranas to the assembly** — The bard Suta Ugrashravas (son of Romaharshana), in the transmission chain Vyasa to Romaharshana to Ugrashravas, narrates the eighteen Puranas to the Naimisha sages _(actors: Suta Ugrashravas, Romaharshana, Vyasa, the rishis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1-1.4; Vayu Purana 1.16; Vishnu Purana 1.1)
- **The Atri-Anasuya triad: birth of Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas** — From the chaste Anasuya the Trimurti take partial birth: Brahma as Soma, Vishnu as Dattatreya, Shiva as Durvasas _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **The gandharva's deception and birth of Svarocis** — A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's form to seduce Varuthini; meditating on the true Pravara's radiance she bears the self-luminous Svarocis _(actors: the gandharva, Varuthini, Svarocis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The gandharva's deception and conception of Svarocis** — A spurned gandharva takes Pravara's exact form and unites with Varuthini; because she conceived meditating on the true Pravara's radiance, her son Svarocis is born self-luminous, giving the manvantara its name _(actors: The gandharva, Varuthini, Svarocis)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The sages' jealousy and conspiracy** — When rains return, the other sages grow envious of Gautama's merit and honour and plot to drive him from his hermitage _(actors: Gautama, jealous ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The thousand-year struggle and Gajendra's surrender** — After a thousand-year contest in which his herd abandons him and his strength fails, Gajendra at last lets go of pride and turns his whole mind to the Supreme, raising a lotus and pouring out the Gajendra-stuti of total surrender _(actors: Gajendra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.2–8.3)
- **Tāraka's oppression of the devas** — Tāraka conquers the three worlds, seizes Indra's heaven and the divine treasures, and inverts cosmic order _(actors: Tāraka, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa)
- **Śukra's curse creates the wilderness** — Enraged Śukra curses Daṇḍa so Indra rains a seven-day dust-storm burying the kingdom for a hundred yojanas, making the desolate Daṇḍaka forest (Arajā's grove alone spared) _(actors: Śukrācārya, Daṇḍa, Indra, Arajā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dandakaranya-rama-forest.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa 81; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Vasishtha-Vishvamitra cow rivalry and Vishvamitra's penance** — King Vishvamitra covets Vasishtha's wish-cow Kamadhenu, who conjures an army that routs his forces; humiliated, he renounces his throne and undertakes millennia of penance to rise from Rajarshi to Brahmarshi _(actors: Vishvamitra, Vasishtha, Kamadhenu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana Bala Kanda 51-65; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Vena's Misrule and Execution** — Crowned Vena forbids all sacrifice, proclaiming himself the sole object of worship; when he refuses the sages' appeal, the brāhmaṇas slay him with mantra-charged kuśa-grass _(actors: Vena, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.14; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Vimāna passed to Ikṣvāku and the Sūryavaṃśa** — Brahmā grants the Raṅga-vimāna to Ikṣvāku, and it is worshipped down the Solar dynasty to Ayodhyā _(actors: Brahmā, Ikṣvāku, Sūryavaṃśa kings)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srirangam-ranganatha.md) — (Śrīraṅga-māhātmya)
