- **Viśvāmitra sends a rākṣasa to possess the king** — Viśvāmitra, exploiting his feud with Vasiṣṭha, dispatches a rākṣasa to possess the cursed Saudāsa so the curse falls on Vasiṣṭha's sons _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Saudāsa, the rākṣasa Kiṃkara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Viśvāmitra waives the fee; Gālava insists** — Viśvāmitra dismisses his devoted pupil Gālava owing no guru-dakṣiṇā, but Gālava proudly insists on paying _(actors: Gālava, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~105–106)
- **Ajāmila's repentance and liberation at Haridvāra** — Restored to life and transformed, Ajāmila renounces all, practices bhakti-yoga at Haridvāra, and is borne to Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Ajāmila, Viṣṇudūtas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ajamila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.2)
- **Andhaka conquers the three worlds and lusts after Parvati** — The mighty blind asura overruns the devas and seizes the three worlds, then beholds Parvati on Kailasa and resolves to take her, not knowing she is his mother _(actors: Andhaka, Indra, devas, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Śarmiṣṭhā casts Devayānī into the well** — After a quarrel of precedence, Śarmiṣṭhā throws Devayānī into a dry well; King Yayāti rescues her by the hand, which she treats as betrothal _(actors: Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 75-76; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Atri-Anasuya triad birth (Soma, Dattatreya, Durvasas)** — From the chaste Anasuya, wife of sage Atri, the Trimurti take partial birth — Brahma as Soma/Candra, Vishnu as Dattatreya, and Shiva as Durvasas — anchoring the great guru-avatar Dattatreya's origin here _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Soma/Candra, Dattatreya, Durvasas)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Puranic Encyclopaedia)
- **Bharata-varsha Named After King Bharata** — The southern karma-bhumi varsha is named after King Bharata, son of Rishabha (Bhagavata) or son of Dushyanta and Shakuntala (epic tradition) _(actors: Bharata, Rishabha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bharatavarsha-and-puranic-geography.md) — (Vishnu Purana 2.3; Bhagavata Purana 5.19; Mahabharata)
- **Birth of Dattātreya, Soma, and Durvāsā** — Pleased by Anasūyā and restored by her, the Trimūrti are born as her sons — Soma (Brahmā-portion), Dattātreya (Viṣṇu-portion), and Durvāsā (Śiva-portion), the triple-deity avatar fused in three heads and six arms _(actors: Anasūyā, Atri, Dattātreya, Soma, Durvāsā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Birth of Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, and Śūrpaṇakhā** — From the rākṣasī Kaikasī and Viśravas are born Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, the gentle Vibhīṣaṇa, and the sister Śūrpaṇakhā _(actors: Kaikasī, Viśravas, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 9–10)
- **Birth of the nine daughters and of Kapila; Kardama's renunciation** — Devahuti bears nine daughters wed to the rishis and a son Kapila, Vishnu incarnate; Kardama then takes sannyasa _(actors: Devahuti, Kardama, Kapila, the rishis (Marici, Atri, Anasuya))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bindu-sarovar-siddhpur.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24)
- **Birth of Vasiṣṭha and Agastya from Mitra-Varuṇa** — The sages Vasiṣṭha and Agastya are miraculously born from the seed of Mitra-Varuṇa at the sight of the apsaras Urvaśī, Agastya being pitcher-born _(actors: Mitra, Varuṇa, Urvaśī, Vasiṣṭha, Agastya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/varuna.md) — (Ṛgveda 7.33)
- **Birth of Vishravas from Pulastya's anger** — Slighted when Kubera attends Brahma over him, Pulastya produces the sage Vishravas from half his own being, into whom his wrath passes _(actors: Pulastya, Vishravas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 258)
- **Brahma's infatuation with Shatarupa and Shiva striking off his head** — In a variant, Brahma is infatuated with his daughter Shatarupa, sprouts extra heads to keep her in view, and Shiva later strikes one off _(actors: Brahma, Shatarupa, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Matsya Purana; Brahma Purana)
- **Chhāyā curses Yama and the deception is exposed** — Chhāyā curses Yama in anger, revealing she cannot be the true mother; Yama complains to Sūrya, who interrogates Chhāyā and uncovers the substitution _(actors: Chhāyā, Yama, Sūrya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Churning of the Ocean of Milk (Ajita as Kurma)** — Vishnu's avatar Ajita bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the milk-ocean _(actors: Ajita (Vishnu/Kurma), devas, asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Churning of Vena's Body — Birth of Niṣāda** — From Vena's churned thigh emerges the dark hunter Niṣāda, ancestor of the forest peoples, carrying away all of Vena's accumulated sin _(actors: the sages, Niṣāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.14; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Cyavana creates Mada and wins the Aśvins their soma-share** — Cyavana paralyzes Indra's arm and creates the giant Asura Mada to force the Aśvins' admission to the soma-cult, then distributes Mada into the four kingly vices _(actors: Cyavana, Indra, the Aśvins, Mada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5)
- **Death of Vasishtha's hundred sons** — In the feud, Vishvamitra causes king Kalmashapada, possessed by a rakshasa, to devour all of Vasishtha's hundred sons; the grieving Vasishtha attempts suicide but is preserved _(actors: Vishvamitra, Kalmashapada, Vasishtha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Devouring of Śakti and Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons** — The possessed Kalmāṣapāda eats Śakti first and then all of Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons, extinguishing the sage's line of sons _(actors: Kalmāṣapāda, Śakti, Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Dhruva granted the immovable polar seat** — Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the Dhruva-pada, the fixed pole-star station enduring a full Kalpa, plus a long earthly reign _(actors: Dhruva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.9, 4.12; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Founding of the royal lineages by Vaivasvata's sons** — Vaivasvata Manu's sons found the great dynasties, Ikshvaku seeding the Solar line and Ila/Sudyumna seeding the Lunar line through Pururavas _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ikshvaku, Ila/Sudyumna, Pururavas)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2, 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Gods dispossessed appeal to Śiva** — Driven from heaven, the devas petition Brahmā and Śiva, who agrees to destroy Śaṅkhacūḍa _(actors: Devas, Brahmā, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book IX)
- **Gods petition Brahmā for a remedy** — The dispossessed devas approach Brahmā, who reveals that only a son of Śiva, born as war-general, can slay Tāraka _(actors: Indra, the devas, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava II; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Indra names the child 'mām dhāsyati'** — Asked who will suckle the motherless infant, Indra answers 'he shall suckle me' and feeds him nectar from his finger, giving the name Māndhātṛ _(actors: Indra, the infant Māndhātṛ, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~126; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.37–38)
- **Jahnu drinks the entire Gaṅgā** — Enraged at the ruined rite, Jahnu swallows the whole river in one draught by his ascetic power, undoing Bhagīratha's effort _(actors: Jahnu, Gaṅgā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **King Suratha Worships the Goddess and Is Reborn as Savarni** — King Suratha, having lost his kingdom, worships the Goddess Mahamaya/Durga in a forest hermitage alongside the merchant Samadhi and by Her boon is destined to be reborn as Savarni, son of Surya, the future 8th Manu _(actors: King Suratha; Samadhi; Mahamaya/Durga)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Markandeya Purana 81-93 (Devi Mahatmya / Durga Saptashati); Devi Bhagavata)
- **Marriage of Atri and Anasūyā** — Anasūyā, daughter of Kardama and Devahūti and sister of Kapila, becomes Atri's wife and the archetypal pativratā _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Kardama, Devahūti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Bhāgavata 3.24.22–24)
- **Marriage of Cyavana and Sukanyā** — To appease the wronged sage, Śaryāti bestows his young daughter Sukanyā in marriage on the aged blind ascetic Cyavana, and she devotedly serves him _(actors: Cyavana, Sukanyā, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 123; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.7)
- **Marriage of Jaratkāru and Manasā (Vāsuki's sister)** — Vāsuki offers his sister—herself named Jaratkāru (later Manasā)—freely and undertakes her maintenance, fulfilling every condition, so the sage weds her to fulfil Brahmā's promise of a serpent-deliverer _(actors: Jaratkāru; Manasā/Jaratkāru; Vāsuki; the nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Marriage to Vrinda** — Jalandhara, crowned king of the asuras, weds the supremely chaste Vrinda whose pativratya makes him invincible _(actors: Jalandhara, Vrinda, Kalanemi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Maya builds Tripura** — The asura-architect Maya constructs the three fortresses of gold, silver, and iron in heaven, air, and earth _(actors: Mayāsura (architect), the three asura brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya Initiated into the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya Mantra** — Foreseeing his death, Mārkaṇḍeya is initiated into (or composes) the Mahā-Mṛtyuñjaya mantra and devotes himself to ceaseless Shiva worship _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Rigveda 7.59.12)
- **Nahuṣa Covets Śacī** — Corrupted by power, Nahuṣa lusts after Indra's queen Śacī and demands her; she takes refuge with Bṛhaspati and sets a trap-condition _(actors: Nahuṣa, Śacī, Bṛhaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 13-17)
- **Nārada initiates Dhruva with the Vāsudeva mantra** — The sage Nārada tests and then instructs Dhruva, directing him to Madhuvana and bestowing the twelve-syllable mantra 'Oṃ Namo Bhagavate Vāsudevāya' — a canonical first-giving of the dvādaśākṣara mantra _(actors: Nārada, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11–12)
- **Pṛthu inherits the bow Ājagava** — In the Pṛthu-narrative, Śiva's celestial bow Ājagava descends as the royal bow inherited by Pṛthu, the first consecrated king, who uses it to compel the Earth to yield her bounty _(actors: Pṛthu, (Śiva as bow-source))_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa (Pṛthu cycle))
- **Pṛthu milks the Earth-cow; origin of agriculture** — Pṛthu chases the fugitive Earth as a cow, levels the land, and milks her of grains and herbs, whence Earth is named Pṛthvī _(actors: Pṛthu, Pṛthvī (Earth))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.17–18; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.13)
- **Puru and the founding of the Paurava line** — Yayati's son Puru accepts his father's old age, founding the Paurava line from which the Kurus descend _(actors: Yayati, Puru, Kuru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 75-95)
- **Ruru gives half his lifespan to revive her** — A messenger of the gods offers that Pramadvarā will live if Ruru surrenders half his remaining lifespan; he consents and she rises, and they wed _(actors: Ruru, deva-dūta, Yama/Dharma, the gods, Pramadvarā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Ruru Revives Pramadvarā** — The Bhārgava youth Ruru gives half his own lifespan to revive his betrothed killed by snakebite, then vows to slay snakes until a serpent preaches ahiṃsā _(actors: Ruru, Pramadvarā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Shiva's Cosmic Grief-Dance** — Maddened with sorrow, Shiva takes up Sati's charred corpse and roams the worlds in a tandava of grief that threatens to unbalance creation _(actors: Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII.30; Kalika Purana 18)
- **Svarocis rescues and marries Manorama** — Grown Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama from a demon with mantric arrows and weds her, later marrying her two companions who teach him secret vidyas _(actors: Svarocis, Manorama, Vibhavari, Kalavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana 64)
- **Svarocis rescues Manorama and marries her** — Grown and trained, Svarocis saves the maiden Manorama and her companions from a demon using mantric arrows, then marries her _(actors: Svarocis, Manorama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The curse-backstories of Indradyumna and Hūhū revealed** — The slain crocodile and freed elephant are revealed as the cursed king Indradyumna and gandharva Hūhū, both liberated by Viṣṇu _(actors: Indradyumna, Hūhū, Agastya, Devala, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4)
- **The Daksha-yajna and the insult to Shiva** — Daksha organizes a colossal yajna deliberately omitting Shiva and Sati and, when Sati attends, reviles Shiva before the assembly as a skull-bearing cremation-ground madman _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.2-4; Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **The impossible price of 800 horses** — Irritated, Viśvāmitra demands 800 moon-white horses each with a single black ear (śyāmakarṇa) as fee _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Gālava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~106)
- **The Kapila-gita — theistic Sankhya taught to Devahuti** — Kapila delivers a nine-chapter discourse on bhakti-yoga, the tattvas subordinated to Īśvara, aṣṭāṅga-yoga meditating on Viṣṇu's form, grades of devotion, Kāla, and the wheel of rebirth _(actors: Kapila, Devahūti (within Maitreya–Vidura frame))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.25–32)
- **The Māṇḍavya curse on Yama** — Wrongly impaled and surviving, the sage Māṇḍavya curses Yama to be born a man, a Śūdra woman's son, for unjustly punishing a child's act — fulfilled as Vidura _(actors: Aṇī-Māṇḍavya, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vidura-niti.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **The phantom-cow ruse (māyā-dhenu)** — An illusory dying cow enters Gautama's field and collapses dead when he shoos it, framing him for go-hatyā (cow-slaughter) _(actors: Gautama, the jealous ṛṣis, the māyā-cow (variant: Gaṇeśa as the cow))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya); sthala-tradition)
- **The Prachetasas and Daksha's re-creation** — The ten Prachetasa sons emerge from austerity in the waters and, with Daksha, repopulate the world in the secondary creation _(actors: Prachetasas, Daksha)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 2))
- **The Rishabha-gita teaching to his sons** — Before renouncing, Rishabha delivers a celebrated discourse that the body is meant for tapas and self-realization, not sense gratification, and that sadhu-sanga liberates _(actors: Rishabha, his hundred sons)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.5)
- **Ugrashravas re-tells the Mahabharata at Naimisha (outermost frame)** — Arriving from Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, Ugrashravas recites the entire Mahabharata to Shaunaka's sages, forming the epic's outermost narrative layer _(actors: Ugrashravas, Shaunaka, the rishis, (Vaishampayana, Janamejaya offstage))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva 1.1-1.4)
- **Vena slain and Prithu churned forth** — The tyrant Vena is slain by the rishis, who churn from his body the first righteous king Prithu, a Vishnu amshavatara who milks the Earth (Prithvi) of grain and becomes the model cakravartin _(actors: Vena, rishis, Prithu, Prithvi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 1))
- **Vishnu's boon and the fixing of the Pole Star** — Vishnu grants Dhruva the immovable celestial Dhruva-loka, making the North Star the model bhakta _(actors: Vishnu, Dhruva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.9, 4.12)
- **Vishnu slays Kalanemi and Indra slays Virochana** — In the Tarakamaya fighting Vishnu kills the asura Kalanemi and Indra kills Virochana, son of Prahlada _(actors: Vishnu, Kalanemi, Indra, Virochana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Brahmanda Purana)
- **Viṣṇu declares 'I am subject to My devotees'** — Viṣṇu refuses to recall the discus, uttering the bhakta-vātsalya verse and sending Durvāsā back to beg Ambarīṣa's pardon _(actors: Viṣṇu, Durvāsā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.4.63)
- **Viṣṇu rescues Gajendra and slays the crocodile** — Hearing the unsectarian cry, Viṣṇu flies on Garuḍa to the lake, lifts the elephant, and severs the crocodile's head with his Sudarśana Cakra, liberating Gajendra _(actors: Viṣṇu, Garuḍa, Gajendra, the crocodile)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.3)
- **Viṣṇu Tests Kuru and Grants the Liberation-Boon** — Viṣṇu tests Kuru by severing his limbs and head; satisfied, he grants that the land be named Kurukṣetra forever and that bathing, dying, or being dusted by it confers mokṣa _(actors: Kuru, Viṣṇu, Indra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Vamana Purana, Kurukshetra-mahatmya)
- **Yajña assumes the office of Indra of the Svāyambhuva Manvantara** — The Viṣṇu-aṃśa Yajña takes the rotating throne of Indra/king of the devas for the first Manvantara — a rare case of the deva-kingship being held by an incarnation of Viṣṇu _(actors: Yajña (Yajñeśvara), the Yāma devas, Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.1, 8.1.20; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.7)
- **Agastya curses King Indradyumna to be an elephant** — The backstory revealed: the Pāṇḍya king Indradyumna, absorbed in a silent vow, failed to honor the sage Agastya, who cursed him to be reborn as a dull elephant — the prior birth of Gajendra _(actors: Agastya, Indradyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4.6–10)
- **Agastya Curses Nahuṣa to Become a Python** — Yoking the Saptarṣis to his palanquin and kicking Agastya while crying 'sarpa, sarpa,' Nahuṣa is cursed to fall from heaven as a python _(actors: Nahuṣa, Agastya, Saptarṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 17; Vana Parva 178; Bhagavata 6.13)
- **Ajita as Kurma at the churning** — In the Bhagavata frame the avatar Ajita of this manvantara bears Mount Mandara as the tortoise Kurma and distributes the amrita at the devas' churning of the ocean _(actors: Ajita/Kurma, devas, asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Ambarīṣa prays the Sudarśana to spare Durvāsā** — The wronged king prays to the discus to spare his persecutor; the Sudarśana relents and the two reconcile over a feast _(actors: Ambarīṣa, Durvāsā, Sudarśana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ambarisha-durvasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.5)
- **Anasūyā halts the river by her vow** — By the power of her chastity-vow Anasūyā stops a river's flow (or ends a drought), proving satya-saṃkalpa overrides nature _(actors: Anasūyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Purāṇic Anasūyā cycle; Padma Purāṇa [regional])
- **Asura misrule** — After a thousand years the empowered asuras abandon dharma and oppress the worlds, provoking the gods _(actors: The Tripura asuras, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā))
- **Aśvins restore Cyavana's youth** — The Aśvins, after Sukanyā refuses their seduction, enter a magical lake with Cyavana so all three emerge as identical youths; Sukanyā chooses rightly and Cyavana is restored to youth, beauty, and sight _(actors: Aśvins, Cyavana, Sukanyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 124; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.8–13; Ṛgveda 1.116–117)
- **Birth of Pṛthu from Vena's Arms** — From Vena's purified arms the sages draw forth the radiant Pṛthu (with his queen Arci), bearing the cakra and lotus marks of a Viṣṇu aṃśa-avatāra _(actors: Pṛthu, Arci, the sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.15; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Birth of Yajna and Dakshina to Akuti** — Manu's daughter Akuti marries rishi Ruci and bears twins Yajna (the era's Indra and a Vishnu amsa) and Dakshina, who becomes Yajna's wife; their sons are the twelve Yama gods _(actors: Akuti, Ruci, Yajna, Dakshina)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.1)
- **Brahma halts the war and restores Tara** — Facing cosmic ruin, Brahma intervenes and compels Soma to surrender Tara, who is returned to Brihaspati already pregnant _(actors: Brahma, Soma, Tara, Brihaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Budha weds Ilā and founds the Lunar Dynasty** — Budha weds Ilā and fathers Pururavas, first king of the Candravaṃśa, so the adulterous Tārā union seeds an entire royal lineage _(actors: Budha, Ilā, Pururavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/the-gurus-brihaspati-and-shukra.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa; Bhāgavata; Devī Bhāgavata)
- **Daksha's curse on Chandra and the Moon's waxing and waning** — Chandra marries the 27 Nakshatras but favors Rohini, so Daksha curses him to waste away; the relented cyclic curse becomes the waxing and waning of the Moon _(actors: Chandra, Daksha, Rohini)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Mahabharata; Puranas)
- **Dattātreya teaches the 24 gurus to King Yadu** — The avadhūta Dattātreya answers King Yadu by recounting how he took 24 gurus from the natural world — earth, wind, python, courtesan Piṅgalā, spider, wasp and more — each yielding one lesson, freeing Yadu of attachment _(actors: Dattātreya, Yadu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 11.7–9 (Uddhava Gītā))
- **Devahuti's liberation and Kapila's departure** — Devahūti takes up bhakti-yoga, attains realization at the Sarasvatī (Siddhapada), and Kapila departs north-east to abide in samādhi by the sea _(actors: Devahūti, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 3.33)
- **Dhruva's great penance suffocates the worlds** — Through six months of ever-intensifying fasting and breath-suspension on one leg, Dhruva's concentrated heat chokes the three worlds, prompting the alarmed gods to appeal to Viṣṇu _(actors: Dhruva, the gods)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8–4.9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Dhruva's war on the Yakṣas and final ascent** — Avenging his slain brother, Dhruva wars on Alakā until Manu stays his wrath; in old age he ascends to Dhruva-loka with his mother Sunīti _(actors: Dhruva, Svāyambhuva Manu, Kubera, Sunīti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.10–4.12)
- **Dhruva's war with the Yakshas** — After his brother Uttama is slain, Dhruva wars on the Yakshas until Svayambhuva Manu halts him, then ascends a celestial vehicle _(actors: Dhruva, Uttama, Yakshas, Svayambhuva Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.10-12)
- **Embassy to Shiva and outbreak of war** — Andhaka sends an emissary (in some texts Prahlada, who counsels against it) demanding the goddess; refused, he marches on Kailasa and the deva-asura war begins _(actors: Andhaka, Prahlada, Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Vamana Purana)
- **Gajendra-moksha (Hari rescues the elephant-king)** — In the Tamasa manvantara the avatar Hari rescues the elephant-king Gajendra from the crocodile, a variant placement of the Gajendra-moksha _(actors: Hari (Vishnu), Gajendra)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.2-4, 8.1)
- **Garuḍa carries Gālava in search of horses** — After Gālava despairs, Garuḍa appears and flies him across the directions, advising him to seek the generous emperor Yayāti _(actors: Gālava, Garuḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~108–114)
- **Gender-shift of Ila/Sudyumna** — Vaivasvata's offspring Ila/Sudyumna, born female, becomes male and alternates gender, a major lineage variant seeding the Chandravamsha _(actors: Ila/Sudyumna)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/manvantara-system.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Grievance over the Churning and war on the devas** — Jalandhara demands return of the ocean's stolen treasures and routs Indra and the gods, seizing the three worlds _(actors: Jalandhara, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda))
- **Kaca Steals the Sañjīvanī Vidyā** — The deva youth Kaca infiltrates Śukrācārya, is killed thrice and revived, learns the resurrection science from within Śukra's belly, then is cursed by the rejected Devayānī _(actors: Kaca, Śukrācārya, Devayānī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 76-78)
- **Killing of the brāhmaṇa couple and the wife's counter-curse** — The rākṣasa-king devours a forest brāhmaṇa (or serves human flesh as alms); the bereaved wife curses him to die instantly if he ever unites with a woman, blocking procreation _(actors: Kalmāṣapāda, the brāhmaṇa husband and wife, (Madayantī in Purāṇic variant))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.9; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Kāma sent and burned (Kāma-dahana)** — Indra sends Kāmadeva to rouse the ascetic Śiva's desire; Śiva opens his third eye and incinerates Kāma to ash _(actors: Indra, Kāmadeva, Rati, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Kumārasambhava III; Śiva Purāṇa (Rudra-saṃhitā))
- **Kubera's three rakshasis bear the demon clan** — To placate the angry Vishravas, Kubera sends three rakshasa women as wives, from whom spring Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Khara, Shurpanakha, and Vibhishana _(actors: Kubera, Vishravas, Pushpotkata, Raka/Malini)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 258)
- **Matsya rescues Vaivasvata Manu at the manvantara junction** — At the Chakshusha-Vaivasvata sandhya, Vishnu's fish-avatar rescues Vaivasvata Manu from the great flood, ushering in the current age _(actors: Matsya (Vishnu), Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Māndhātṛ's universal conquest and dharmic reign** — Māndhātṛ becomes cakravartin of the seven continents, earns the epithet Trasaddasyu, and his just digvijaya rule becomes the proverbial benchmark of kingship _(actors: Māndhātṛ, Indra (who bestows Trasaddasyu), the kings of the earth)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.39–41; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.2; Mahābhārata Droṇa Parva)
- **Pṛthu's aśvamedhas and Indra's theft of the horse** — Pṛthu's hundred horse-sacrifices threaten Indra, who repeatedly steals the horse until Brahmā and Viṣṇu intervene and Pṛthu forgives him _(actors: Pṛthu, Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.19–20)
- **Rishabha's renunciation and avadhuta wandering** — Rishabha crowns Bharata, abandons his kingdom, and wanders as a naked avadhuta behaving like a madman to escape social entanglement _(actors: Rishabha, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.5-6)
- **Ruru's vow to slay all serpents** — Grief turned to hatred, Ruru vows to kill every snake he meets and roams the forests slaughtering venomous and harmless serpents alike _(actors: Ruru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Rāvaṇa wins Brahmā's boon of invulnerability** — After extreme penance offering his ten heads, Rāvaṇa gains Brahmā's boon of invulnerability to all divine and demonic beings, disdaining protection from men and monkeys — the loophole that dooms him _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 10)
- **Shantanu weds Ganga; the drowning of the Vasus** — King Shantanu weds Ganga, who drowns her first seven sons (the cursed Vasus) and surrenders the eighth, Devavrata, when he breaks his vow _(actors: Shantanu, Ganga, Devavrata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 96-100)
- **Svarocis weds his three wives and receives the secret vidyas** — Svarocis weds Manorama's two companions Vibhavari and Kalavati, who impart esoteric knowledge including the secret Padmini Vidya _(actors: Svarocis, Vibhavari, Kalavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The abrupt departure and the 'asti' prophecy** — When Manasā wakes the sleeping Jaratkāru to save his sunset prayers, he construes it as displeasure and leaves, but first declares a blazing son already lives in her womb—naming him Āstīka _(actors: Jaratkāru; Manasā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **The Bhagavata's opening question at the dawn of Kali** — Troubled by the onset of Kali Yuga, the Naimisha sages ask Suta for the essence of scripture and receive the Bhagavata he heard from Shuka _(actors: Suta, the rishis, (Shuka offstage))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.1.9-1.1.23)
- **The false expiation demanded** — The conspiring sages tell Gautama his sin can be cleared only by bringing the Gaṅgā down to Brahmagiri — an impossible task meant to expel him _(actors: Gautama, the jealous ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The gods propitiate Jahnu** — Devas, ṛṣis and Bhagīratha entreat the angry sage to release the river, asking him to accept her as his daughter _(actors: Devas, ṛṣis, Bhagīratha, Jahnu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **The Kapilopadesha (Devahuti-putra Gita) at Bindu-sarovara** — Kapila expounds theistic Samkhya and bhakti-yoga to his mother Devahuti at the lake, and she attains moksha _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/bindu-sarovar-siddhpur.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.25-33)
- **The Pushkara yajna and Savitri's curse on Brahma** — At Brahma's yajna at Pushkara, the late Savitri arrives to find Brahma has wed the milkmaid Gayatri in her seat and curses Brahma to be worshipped almost nowhere, explaining the near-absence of Brahma temples _(actors: Brahma, Savitri/Sarasvati, Gayatri)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Padma Purana)
- **Trishanku's heaven** — When Vasishtha refuses to send king Trishanku bodily to heaven, Vishvamitra does so by tapas; Indra hurls him back and Vishvamitra freezes him mid-fall and begins building a counter-heaven and a second set of stars _(actors: Vishvamitra, Trishanku, Indra)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana Bala Kanda 57-60)
- **Vishnu's Sudarshana Dismembers Sati** — To free Shiva and restore order, Vishnu severs Sati's corpse piece by piece with his discus; each falling part sanctifies a spot and becomes a Shakti Pitha _(actors: Vishnu, Shiva, Sati)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana; Pithanirnaya / Tantra Cudamani)
- **Viṣṇu begs away the Viṣṇu-Kavaca** — Viṣṇu, disguised as an old brāhmaṇa mendicant, begs Śaṅkhacūḍa to give the Viṣṇu-Kavaca as alms, stripping his first protection _(actors: Viṣṇu, Śaṅkhacūḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Viśvakarmā trims the Sun on the cosmic lathe** — To win Sañjñā back, Sūrya submits to his father-in-law Viśvakarmā/Tvaṣṭṛ, who grinds away one-eighth of his unbearable radiance on a cosmic lathe to make him gentler _(actors: Viśvakarmā, Sūrya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.2)
- **Yajña leads the Yāmas to slay the Rākṣasas assailing Manu's sacrifice** — When hunger-maddened Rākṣasas attack to devour Svāyambhuva Manu and despoil his cosmic yajña, Viṣṇu-as-Yajña takes up arms with his sons the Yāmas and drives them off, defending the sacrifice he embodies _(actors: Yajña, the twelve Yāmas, Svāyambhuva Manu, the Rākṣasas/Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yajna-avatara.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.1.18–20)
- **Yama Comes for Mārkaṇḍeya** — On the appointed day Yama arrives to claim the boy, who clings to a Shiva-liṅga in unbroken worship _(actors: Yama, Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Austerity and the Trimūrti boon** — Atri and Anasūyā perform tapas for a son equal to the Supreme; the Lord grants that portions of Brahmā, Viṣṇu, and Śiva will be born to them _(actors: Atri, Anasūyā, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Bhāgavata 4.1.15–33)
- **Aṣṭāvakra Defeats Bandin at Janaka's Court** — Born crooked from a womb-curse, the boy Aṣṭāvakra defeats the philosopher Bandin in debate, frees those he drowned and recovers his father, later being straightened in a sacred river _(actors: Aṣṭāvakra, Bandin, Janaka, Kahoḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 132-134)
- **Avatar Vibhu instructs the ascetics** — Vishnu's avatar Vibhu, born to Vedashiras and Tushita, lives a lifelong celibate and instructs 88,000 ascetics in self-control _(actors: Vibhu, Vedashiras, Tushita)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1)
- **Birth and rearing of Āstīka** — Āstīka is born half-brāhmaṇa, half-nāga, reared among the serpents and schooled in the Vedas by Cyavana, uniquely fit to mediate between brahminical rite and the nāgas _(actors: Āstīka; Manasā; Vāsuki; Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Birth of Garuda and theft of the Amrita** — Garuda is born of Vinata, raids heaven to steal the amrita to ransom his enslaved mother, and pacts with Vishnu (as mount) and Indra (Nagas as food) _(actors: Garuda, Vinata, Kadru, Vishnu, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Astika Parva)
- **Birth of Kapila and the Devahuti-putra Gita** — Devahuti marries Prajapati Kardama and bears Kapila, the Samkhya teacher and Vishnu avatara, who delivers the Devahuti-putra Gita to his mother _(actors: Devahuti, Kardama, Kapila)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **Birth of the five sons of Yayāti** — Devayānī bears Yadu and Turvaśu while Śarmiṣṭhā, secretly fathered by Yayāti, bears Druhyu, Anu and Pūru, the sons whose lines split the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Yayāti, Devayānī, Śarmiṣṭhā, Yadu, Pūru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 83-84; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Birth of Virabhadra and Bhadrakali** — Learning of Sati's death, Shiva dashes a lock of his matted hair to the ground, from which spring the wrathful warrior Virabhadra and the fierce goddess Bhadrakali to avenge her _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Brahma's wheel founds the Naimisha-kshetra (nemi origin)** — Seeking a sin-free sacrifice ground, the rishis follow Brahma's mind-made wheel whose rim (nemi) sinks at this spot, naming the forest Naimisha and opening the Chakra-tirtha _(actors: Brahma, the rishis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vayu Purana; Brahmanda Purana; Naimisharanya-mahatmya)
- **Chandra's abduction of Tara and the Tarakamaya war** — Chandra abducts Brihaspati's wife Tara, sparking the Tarakamaya war between devas and asuras settled by Brahma; Tara bears Budha, founding the Chandravamsha _(actors: Chandra, Tara, Brihaspati, Budha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Coronation of Pṛthu — First Consecrated King** — The sages and gods crown Pṛthu the first anointed king and cakravartin, the bardic Sūta and Māgadha appear, and the devas endow him with divine emblems _(actors: Pṛthu, sages, devas, Sūta, Māgadha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.15; Vishnu Purana 1.13; Shatapatha Brahmana 3.5.4)
- **Cyavana paralyzes Indra's arm** — At Śaryāti's soma-sacrifice Cyavana offers the Aśvins a soma-cup against Indra's objection, and when Indra raises his vajra the sage withers and freezes Indra's arm in mid-air _(actors: Cyavana, Indra, Aśvins, Śaryāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125)
- **Dattātreya grants boons to Kārtavīrya Arjuna** — As divine teacher Dattātreya imparts brahmavidyā and grants boons to the thousand-armed Haihaya king Kārtavīrya Arjuna, and instructs Alarka and Prahlāda _(actors: Dattātreya, Kārtavīrya Arjuna, Alarka, Prahlāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dattatreya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.3.11)
- **Devala curses the gandharva Hūhū to be a crocodile** — The gandharva Hūhū pulled the bathing sage Devala's leg in sport and was cursed to become a crocodile, with the boon that Viṣṇu himself would one day slay and release him — the prior birth of the crocodile _(actors: Devala, Hūhū)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4.3–5)
- **Embassy to Shiva and lust for Parvati** — Jalandhara (via Rahu) demands Parvati from Shiva; Shiva's fury births a devouring being and war becomes inevitable _(actors: Jalandhara, Rahu, Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda))
- **Establishment of the Shakti Pithas** — At each site where a body part or ornament of Sati fell, a triad is fixed of the fallen anga, a presiding Devi, and her guardian Bhairava, founding the Shakta pilgrimage network _(actors: Devi, Bhairava)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Tantra Cudamani (Pithanirnaya); Mahabhagavata Purana)
- **Gaṅgā released and named Jāhnavī** — Jahnu releases the river from his ear (or thigh, in variants), so she is thereafter called Jāhnavī, 'daughter of Jahnu' _(actors: Jahnu, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44)
- **Gautama's tapas and Śiva's boon** — Gautama undertakes fierce penance to Śiva at Tryambak/Brahmagiri; Śiva appears with Pārvatī and offers a boon _(actors: Gautama, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Impalement on the trishula and the multiplying blood** — Shiva transfixes Andhaka on his trident, but every drop of blood that falls spawns a full-grown Andhaka-clone, filling the field with duplicates _(actors: Shiva, Andhaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Matsya Purana; Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Kurma Purana)
- **Indra Restored to the Throne** — With the usurper fallen, Indra is purified of brahmahatyā and returns to his throne _(actors: Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 18; Bhagavata 6.13)
- **Installation of Vaivasvata Manu (manvantara transition)** — At the close of the Chakshusha age's twilight, a partial dissolution installs Vaivasvata Manu (son of Vivasvan-Surya) as the seventh and current Manu, beginning our manvantara _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Vivasvan/Surya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Kimpuruṣa Granted the Kimpuruṣa-varṣa** — Kimpuruṣa, son of Agnīdhra by the apsarā Pūrvacitti, becomes the eponymous king-ancestor of the kimpuruṣas and is granted the Kimpuruṣa-varṣa as his hereditary portion _(actors: Kimpuruṣa, Agnīdhra, Pūrvacitti)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/gandharvas-and-kinnaras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 5.2)
- **Kumbhakarṇa's boon twisted to sleep** — Asking for destruction of the gods, Kumbhakarṇa is made by Sarasvatī to say 'sleep' instead, gaining his curse of months-long sleep _(actors: Kumbhakarṇa, Sarasvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 10)
- **Māndhātṛ's marriage and progeny** — Māndhātṛ weds Bindumatī and fathers Purukutsa, Mucukunda, Ambarīṣa, and fifty daughters _(actors: Māndhātṛ, Bindumatī, Purukutsa, Mucukunda, Ambarīṣa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.2; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.41)
- **Priyavrata's chariot-furrows form the seven oceans and continents** — Priyavrata circles the Earth seven times in his chariot; the wheel-ruts carve the seven oceans and seven dvipas _(actors: Priyavrata)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.1)
- **Pārvatī's tapas and the divine wedding** — Pārvatī (Satī reborn) wins Śiva by her own austerity and his disguised test, and the two are wed at Himavān's palace _(actors: Pārvatī, Śiva, Himavān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Kumārasambhava V–VII; Śiva Purāṇa (Pārvatī-khaṇḍa))
- **Ravana's boon of invulnerability with the man-and-monkey loophole** — Ravana wins from Brahma immunity from gods, gandharvas, yakshas, and rakshasas but proudly omits men and monkeys, the loophole that necessitates Vishnu's human incarnation _(actors: Ravana, Brahma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 259)
- **Rediscovery and re-establishment of worship (Pururavā)** — King Pururavā of the lunar line rediscovers the buried composite icon, re-establishes worship, and is commanded to keep it coated in sandalwood _(actors: Pururavā, Varāha-Lakṣmī-Narasiṃha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/simhachalam-varaha-narasimha.md) — (Siṃhācala sthala-purāṇa (regional, late text))
- **Rishabha's death by forest fire** — Wandering the Kutakachala region, Rishabha's austerity-emaciated body is consumed by a bamboo-friction wildfire as he quits the body absorbed in the Self _(actors: Rishabha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.6)
- **Sagara's Asvamedha and the stolen horse** — King Sagara of Ayodhyā performs the horse-sacrifice; Indra steals the horse and tethers it beside the meditating Kapila in the netherworld _(actors: Sagara, Indra, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8.7–9; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 38–39)
- **Shiva Slays Yama as Kālāntaka** — When Yama's noose falls around the liṅga, Shiva bursts forth and strikes down Death, earning the epithets Kālāntaka and Mṛtyuñjaya _(actors: Shiva, Yama, Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Tara's confession of Budha's paternity** — With both Soma and Brihaspati claiming the luminous child, Brahma questions Tara, who admits the son is Soma's _(actors: Tara, Brahma, Soma, Brihaspati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14.13-16)
- **The curse-water and the 'spotted-foot' naming** — Stayed by Queen Madayantī from cursing the brāhmaṇa, Mitrasaha pours the curse-charged water on his own feet, scorching them black and earning the name Kalmāṣapāda _(actors: Mitrasaha, Madayantī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.9; Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **The doe and the birth of Svarochisha Manu** — A doe appeals to Svarocis for mercy and asks him to embrace her; when he does she conceives and instantly delivers Svarochisha Manu amid celestial rejoicing and a rain of flowers _(actors: Svarocis, the doe, Svarochisha Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **The dundubha's sermon on ahiṃsā** — A non-venomous dundubha snake stops Ruru's sword and teaches that non-injury (ahiṃsā) is the brāhmaṇa's highest dharma _(actors: Ruru, the dundubha snake)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **The solar off-cuts forged into divine weapons** — The shorn solar brilliance is forged by Viśvakarmā into the great weapons of the gods, including Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra, Śiva's Triśūla, and Kārttikeya's spear _(actors: Viśvakarmā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Vaikuntha manifests the realm Vaikuntha** — In the Raivata manvantara the avatar Vaikuntha, born of Vikuntha, manifests Vishnu's abode Vaikuntha for the pleasure of the goddess Ramaa _(actors: Vaikuntha (Vishnu), Ramaa)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5, 8.1)
- **Viṣṇu as Māyāmoha corrupts the asuras** — Viṣṇu emanates a heretic preacher who seduces the Tripura asuras from Vedic dharma, stripping their protection _(actors: Viṣṇu (as Māyāmoha / deluding monk), the Tripura asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa)
- **Viṣṇu impersonates Śaṅkhacūḍa to break Tulasī's vow** — Viṣṇu assumes Śaṅkhacūḍa's exact form and approaches Tulasī as her husband, breaking her chastity-vow and dissolving the invincibility lock _(actors: Viṣṇu, Tulasī, Śaṅkhacūḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa, Book IX)
- **Viṣṇu's darśana and the Dhruva-stuti** — Viṣṇu manifests to the unwavering child and, touching Dhruva's cheek with his conch, floods him with Vedic eloquence so he pours forth the celebrated Dhruva-stuti hymn _(actors: Viṣṇu, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.9; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Vrinda becomes Tulsi, ever-wed to Vishnu** — Vishnu breaks the chastity of Vrinda (wife of the asura Jalandhara) by taking her husband's form, breaking Jalandhara's invincibility; the transformed Vrinda becomes the Tulsi plant eternally married to Vishnu, re-enacted as Tulsi Vivah _(actors: Vrinda, Jalandhara, Vishnu)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Padma Purāṇa)
- **Yayāti gives his daughter Mādhavī** — Lacking the horses, Yayāti gives Gālava his daughter Mādhavī, who regains her virginity after each childbirth, as renewable bride-wealth _(actors: Yayāti, Gālava, Mādhavī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~115)
- **Ṛṣabhanātha Attains Nirvāṇa on Aṣṭāpada (Kailāsa)** — In Jain tradition the first Tīrthaṅkara Ṛṣabhanātha (Ādinātha) attains nirvāṇa/mokṣa on Kailāsa (Aṣṭāpada), the foundational liberation-site of Jainism _(actors: Ṛṣabhanātha (Ādinātha))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/manasarovar-kailash-yatra.md) — (Jain tradition)
- **Assembly of Śiva's cosmic chariot** — The pantheon becomes Śiva's weapon-system: Earth the chariot, Sun/Moon wheels, Vedas horses, Brahmā charioteer, Meru bow, Viṣṇu arrow _(actors: Śiva, Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Sūrya, Candra, the Vedas, Meru, Vāsuki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva (8.24); Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa)
- **Birth and naming of Budha** — Soma names the boy Budha (Mercury) and takes him to his realm; Budha is the founder of the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Soma, Budha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Birth of Durvasa as Shiva's portion** — Durvasa is born of Atri and Anasuya as the Rudra-portion, the short-tempered sage whose curses drive major plots _(actors: Durvasa (Shiva), Atri, Anasuya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Birth of Vaivasvata Manu and the Surya cycle** — Vivasvat marries Samjna/Chaya, the Sun's excess radiance is trimmed by Vishvakarman, and the Solar dynasty descends through Vaivasvata Manu, opening the present age _(actors: Vivasvat (Surya), Samjna, Chaya, Vishvakarman, Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/markandeya-purana.md) — (Markandeya Purana)
- **Boon of Eternal Deathlessness to Mārkaṇḍeya** — Shiva blesses Mārkaṇḍeya to remain eternally sixteen and never die, granting him chiranjīvi status to outlive kalpas _(actors: Shiva, Mārkaṇḍeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Both Gajendra and Hūhū liberated** — The single stroke of the Sudarśana liberates both beings: Hūhū regains his gandharva form, and Gajendra/Indradyumna is granted a divine form (sārūpya) and taken to Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Viṣṇu, Gajendra, Hūhū)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gajendra-moksha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.4.1–14)
- **Burning of Sagara's 60,000 sons** — Sagara's sixty thousand sons dig up the earth, wrongly accuse the meditating Kapila of theft, and are reduced to ash on the spot _(actors: 60,000 sons of Sagara, Kapila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8.11–13; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 40; Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Conception and birth of Skanda-Kārttikeya** — Śiva's unbearable seed is borne by Agni and Gaṅgā to a reed-bed, where the Kṛttikās nurse the six-faced infant Skanda _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Agni, Gaṅgā, the Kṛttikās, Skanda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Mahābhārata (Śalya-parvan); Skanda Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava)
- **Creation of the Asura Mada** — Cyavana generates from his ascetic energy a colossal Asura, Mada ('Intoxication'), with vast jaws and fangs, who advances to devour Indra and the worlds _(actors: Cyavana, Mada, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125)
- **Destruction of the Daksha-yajna and beheading of Daksha** — Virabhadra, Bhadrakali and Shiva's hordes storm the yajna, maim the assembled gods and priests, and Virabhadra decapitates Daksha, his head thrown into the fire _(actors: Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.5; Vayu Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Durga armed by the devas for the Mahishasura war (Ayudha Puja charter)** — The devas each yield their weapon to arm Durga for her battle with Mahishasura, the charter for worshipping weapons and tools as forms of the Goddess on Maha Navami _(actors: Durga, the devas, Mahishasura)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Devī Māhātmya (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa))
- **Śiva slays Śaṅkhacūḍa with the triśūla** — With both protections gone, Śiva strikes down Śaṅkhacūḍa with his trident, reducing him to ash; his bones become the world's conches _(actors: Śiva, Śaṅkhacūḍa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa, Prakṛti-khaṇḍa)
- **Jalandhara's impersonation of Shiva to seize Parvati** — Jalandhara takes Shiva's form to deceive Parvati, who detects the fraud and incites Vishnu to repay it on Vrinda _(actors: Jalandhara, Parvati, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Kuśika line threaded through Jahnu** — The Bhāgavata routes the Kuśika/Gādhi line through Jahnu's descendants, making him the junction linking the Kuru and Kuśika branches _(actors: Jahnu, Gādhi, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/jahnu.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.15)
- **Loan to Haryaśva of Ayodhyā** — King Haryaśva begets Vasumanas on Mādhavī, pays 200 śyāmakarṇa horses, and returns her virgin _(actors: Haryaśva, Mādhavī, Gālava, Vasumanas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~116)
- **Matsya flood at the Chakshusha-Vaivasvata junction** — Vishnu's fish-avatar rescues Vaivasvata Manu in the deluge that closes the Chakshusha age and ushers in our manvantara (text-dependent boundary placement) _(actors: Matsya/Vishnu, Vaivasvata Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-06-chakshusha.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana)
- **Menaka breaks Vishvamitra's penance and bears Shakuntala** — The apsara Menaka breaks Vishvamitra's penance, and he fathers Shakuntala by her _(actors: Vishvamitra, Menaka, Shakuntala)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Mithilā as Śakti Pīṭha (Satī's left shoulder)** — During Śiva's grief-wandering with Satī's corpse, her left shoulder falls at Mithilā, fixing the Śakti Umā and Bhairava Mahodara _(actors: Satī, Śiva, Viṣṇu, Devī Umā, Bhairava Mahodara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/janakpur-mithila-sita-janmabhumi.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Tantra Cūḍāmaṇi / Pīṭhanirṇaya)
- **Nārada provokes the goddesses** — Nārada praises Anasūyā as the most chaste woman alive, stinging Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, and Pārvatī into sending their husbands to test her _(actors: Nārada, Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Prasuti's daughters become mothers of cosmos and dharma** — Prasuti marries the first Daksha and bears daughters including Sati, Aditi, Diti, Danu and the personified virtues, who become mothers of the cosmos and dharma _(actors: Prasuti, Daksha, Sati, Aditi, Diti, Danu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.1; Vishnu Purana)
- **Pṛthu Pursues and Milks the Earth-Cow** — When the famine-stricken Earth withholds all seed, Pṛthu pursues her as a fleeing cow, levels the mountains, and milks her of all grains, originating agriculture; she is named Pṛthvī _(actors: Pṛthu, Pṛthvī, Svāyambhuva Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.17-18; Vishnu Purana 1.13; Atharvaveda)
- **Rebirth of Sati as Parvati** — Sati is reborn as Parvati, daughter of the mountain-king Himavan, and rewins Shiva, closing the loop of the destroyed first marriage _(actors: Parvati, Shiva, Himavan)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/51-shakti-peethas.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana; Kalika Purana)
- **Rishabha as first Tirthankara (Jain account)** — In Jain tradition Rishabhanatha/Adinatha, born to Nabhi and Marudevi at Ayodhya, founds civilization, teaches the six livelihoods, fathers a hundred sons including Bharata and Bahubali _(actors: Rishabhanatha (Adinatha), Nabhi, Marudevi, Bharata, Bahubali, Brahmi, Sundari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Kalpa-sutra; Adi-purana (Jinasena); Hemacandra)
- **Rāvaṇa seizes Laṅkā from Kubera** — On Sumālī's urging Rāvaṇa demands and takes Laṅkā and the Puṣpaka chariot by force; Kubera withdraws to Mount Kailāsa _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Kubera, Prahasta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 11–15)
- **Sahasrapāt revealed and released from his curse** — The dundubha discloses he is the sage Sahasrapāt, cursed into snake-form by Khagama for a jest, and is freed on meeting Ruru, resuming his ṛṣi body _(actors: Sahasrapāt (Ḍuṇḍubha), Khagama, Ruru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Sarasvati cursed to flow with blood (Sthanu-tirtha)** — Caught between the feuding sages, Sarasvati warns Vasishtha instead of bringing him to be killed and is cursed by Vishvamitra to flow with blood; demons drink and bathe in her waters until sages purify her as Aruna and free the demons to heaven _(actors: Sarasvati, Vishvamitra, Vasishtha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saraswati.md) — (Mahabharata, Shalya Parva)
- **Satī's throat falls at Amarnāth** — In the Dakṣa-yajña dismemberment cycle, Satī's throat falls here, fixing the Śakti Pīṭha of Mahāmāyā with Bhairava Trisandhyeśvara _(actors: Satī, Śiva, Viṣṇu (Sudarśana Cakra), Mahāmāyā, Trisandhyeśvara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/amarnath-ice-lingam-and-amar-katha.md) — (Tantra Cūḍāmaṇi / Pīṭhanirṇaya (51 Śakti Pīṭha list))
- **Sūrya and Sañjñā reunite as stallion and mare, begetting the Aśvins** — Gentled, Sūrya finds Sañjñā in mare-form and unites with her as a stallion, producing the horse-faced Aśvins (and Revanta), after which she returns as his full wife _(actors: Sūrya, Sañjñā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Āstīka halts Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice** — At the sarpa-satra Āstīka wins a boon from Janamejaya and asks that the rite cease, saving Takṣaka in mid-air and the surviving serpents—the same sattra at which the Mahābhārata is first recited _(actors: Āstīka; Janamejaya; Takṣaka; Vāsuki and the nāgas; Vaiśampāyana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jaratkaru-and-manasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Āstīka sub-parva)
- **Summoning of the Matrikas/Bhairavas to drink the blood** — Shiva (or the Devi) emanates the Saptamatrika and Bhairava blood-drinkers to lap every drop before it touches the ground, halting the multiplication _(actors: Shiva, Devi, Saptamatrika (Brahmi, Maheshvari, Kaumari, Vaishnavi, Varahi, Aindri, Chamunda), Yogeshvari, Andhaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana; Vamana Purana; Linga Purana)
- **The descent of the Gautamī Gaṅgā (Godāvarī)** — Śiva looses a strand of Gaṅgā from his locks at Brahmagiri; she flows out as the Gautamī Gaṅgā / Godāvarī, washing away the cow-sin and remaining as the Dakṣiṇa Gaṅgā _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Gautama)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Gautamī-māhātmya))
- **The Nimisha demons slain in a wink (alternate name-legend)** — A horde of demons is destroyed 'in an instant' (nimisha) at the site, yielding the alternate etymology of Naimisha _(actors: Gauramukha / the rishis, the Nimisha demons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vayu Purana; Mahabharata)
- **The Saubhari parable — sage weds the fifty daughters** — The aged sage Saubhari, desire awoken, makes himself youthful and weds all fifty of Māndhātṛ's daughters, builds palaces of pleasure, then renounces it all in disillusion _(actors: Saubhari, Māndhātṛ, the fifty princesses)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.6.39–54; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.2)
- **The slaying of the tyrant Vena** — Vena bans all sacrifice and claims to be Hari himself; the sages kill him with kusha-grass blades and hum-mantras _(actors: Vena, the sages)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.13-14; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **Śukra curses Yayāti with old age** — Learning the broken oath, Śukra curses Yayāti to instant decrepit old age, granting only the loophole that he may exchange it for a willing person's youth _(actors: Śukra, Yayāti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 85; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Uttaṅka and Madayantī's earrings** — In his man-eating state Saudāsa grants the sage Uttaṅka leave to fetch Queen Madayantī's celestial earrings before being eaten _(actors: Saudāsa/Kalmāṣapāda, Madayantī, Uttaṅka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Āśvamedhika Parva 14.52-58)
- **Vibhu instructs 88,000 ascetics** — The avatara Vibhu, born to the sage Vedashiras and Tushita, lives as a lifelong brahmacarin and instructs 88,000 ascetics in self-control and austerity _(actors: Vibhu, Vedashiras, Tushita)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-02-svarochisha.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.1)
- **Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the polar seat** — Viṣṇu grants Dhruva the immovable celestial station Dhruva-loka above the saptarṣi, enduring a full Kalpa untouched by pralaya, and decrees he will first rule the earth for 36,000 years _(actors: Viṣṇu, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.9, 4.12; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Yavakrī's Pride and Death** — Yavakrī wins Vedic knowledge from Indra by extreme tapas, grows arrogant, molests Raibhya's daughter-in-law, and is slain by a rākṣasa conjured from Raibhya's matted lock _(actors: Yavakrī, Bhāradvāja, Raibhya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 135-138)
- **All Beings Milk the Earth-Cow** — After Pṛthu, every class of being in turn milks the Earth-cow with its own calf and vessel, each drawing the boon proper to its nature _(actors: ṛṣis, devas, pitṛs, nāgas, asuras, yakṣas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata 4.18)
- **Amsuman recovers the horse and learns of Ganga** — Sagara's grandson Aṃśumān reverently approaches Kapila, recovers the horse, and is told only the heavenly Gaṅgā can liberate the ashes _(actors: Aṃśumān, Kapila, Sagara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.8.20–28; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 41–42)
- **Anasuya turns the Trimurti into infants** — To test her chastity the Trimurti come disguised as mendicants demanding to be fed while she is nude; Anasuya turns them into three infants, and they are reborn as her sons Dattatreya, Soma, and Durvasa _(actors: Atri, Anasuya, Trimurti)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Markandeya Purana; Ramayana)
- **Aśvins admitted to the soma-cult** — Faced with annihilation by Mada, Indra relents and concedes the Aśvins their rightful share of soma, ending their exclusion forever — the etiological climax of the tale _(actors: Indra, Aśvins, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa IV.1.5.18)
- **Bahubali's duel with Bharata and renunciation (Jain)** — Rishabha's eldest son Bharata becomes the first cakravartin while his second son Bahubali renounces after a duel with Bharata and attains kevala-jnana _(actors: Bharata, Bahubali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Adi-purana (Jinasena); Hemacandra)
- **Budha fathers Pururavas** — Budha marries Ila, the gender-changing offspring of Vaivasvata Manu, and fathers Pururavas, the first king of the Chandravamsha _(actors: Budha, Ila, Pururavas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/navagraha.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Budha weds Ila** — Budha marries Ila, the gender-shifting child of Vaivasvata Manu, the dynastic hinge of the Lunar line _(actors: Budha, Ila)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.1, 4.6; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Daksa's sacrifice and Sati's self-immolation** — Sati immolates herself at Daksa's sacrifice over the insult to Siva, rupturing the relationship between Daksa and Siva _(actors: Daksa, Sati, Siva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4)
- **Daksha revived with a goat's head** — Pacified by the supplicating gods, Shiva restores the maimed deities and brings Daksha back to life fitted with the head of the sacrificial goat, who becomes his devotee _(actors: Shiva, Daksha, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IV.6-7; Shiva Purana; Vayu Purana)
- **Death of Māndhātṛ at the hands of Lavaṇāsura** — In the Rāma-cycle backstory tradition, the world-conqueror Māndhātṛ is slain by the asura Lavaṇa wielding Śiva's invincible trident _(actors: Māndhātṛ, Lavaṇāsura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Uttara-rāmāyaṇa / Padma Purāṇa traditions; Mahābhārata allusions)
- **Death of Uttama and Suruci by Yakṣas** — During Dhruva's reign his half-brother Uttama is slain by a Yakṣa while hunting in the Himālaya, and the grieving Suruci who goes searching is also killed _(actors: Uttama, Suruci)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.10)
- **Grihapati wins lordship over death** — Born to the brahmin Vishvanara, threatened by death-by-lightning at twelve, Grihapati's worship of Shiva wins him lordship of all directions and the fire-god's domain _(actors: Grihapati (Shiva), Vishvanara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-avatars-and-forms.md) — (Shiva Purana)
- **Kaca steals the Mritasanjivani mantra** — Brihaspati's son Kaca infiltrates Shukracharya's school to steal the death-reviving mantra, and mutual curses doom Devayani to a kshatriya marriage _(actors: Kaca, Devayani, Shukracharya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva)
- **Loan to Divodāsa of Kāśi** — King Divodāsa of Kāśi begets Pratardana on Mādhavī and pays 200 horses _(actors: Divodāsa, Mādhavī, Gālava, Pratardana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~117)
- **Priyavrata takes up kingship** — The reluctant ascetic Priyavrata is persuaded by Brahma to take up kingship, marries Kamya, and fathers ten sons and two daughters, founding dynasties _(actors: Priyavrata, Brahma, Kamya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Vishnu Purana 2.1; Bhagavata Purana 5.1)
- **Prolonged impalement and Andhaka's penitent redemption** — Held aloft on the trident for a vast span until drained, the humbled Andhaka perceives Shiva's majesty, praises him with a hymn, and begs forgiveness _(actors: Shiva, Andhaka, Parvati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Matsya Purana; Kurma Purana)
- **Pūru gives his youth; elder sons cursed** — The four elder sons refuse and are cursed to lesser fates, while the youngest Pūru gladly takes his father's old age and lends his youth _(actors: Yayāti, Yadu, Pūru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yayati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva 85-88; Bhāgavata 9.18)
- **Ruru renounces his vow** — Chastened, Ruru abandons his slaughter of serpents and embraces the gentleness proper to a brāhmaṇa _(actors: Ruru)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Rāvaṇa pinned under Kailāsa and named by Śiva** — Lifting Mount Kailāsa in pride, Rāvaṇa is pinned by Śiva's toe and howls for a thousand years until Śiva releases him, names him Rāvaṇa, and gives him the sword Candrahāsa _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 16)
- **Sati's body-part falls — the Naimisha Shakti Pitha** — In the Daksha-yajna dismemberment a part of Sati (upper lip / heart-portion) falls here, fixing Devi Lingadharini (Lalita) and Bhairava as the resident Shakti Pitha _(actors: Sati, Vishnu, Shiva, Devi Lingadharini/Lalita, Bhairava Chanda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Devi Bhagavata Purana VII; Tantra Chudamani (Pithanirnaya); Shiva Purana)
- **Skanda consecrated senāpati** — The gods anoint the days-old Skanda as commander of the divine army, fulfilling the boon's slayer-clause _(actors: Skanda, Brahmā, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Mahābhārata (Śalya-parvan); Skanda Purāṇa)
- **The binding of the reluctant river** — The released Gaṅgā tries to flee or vanish underground; Gautama/Śiva binds her with darbha grass to flow on, explaining her interrupted spring-fed emergence (Kuśāvarta as ritual source) _(actors: Gautama, Gaṅgā, Śiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa / sthala-tradition)
- **The single arrow burns Tripura** — At the rare alignment Śiva looses one Viṣṇu-arrow incinerating all three cities and their asuras at once _(actors: Śiva (Tripurāntaka), Viṣṇu-arrow, the three asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva; Śiva Purāṇa; Liṅga Purāṇa)
- **Trimūrti's chastity-test and the infants miracle** — Disguised mendicants demand Anasūyā serve them naked; she turns the three gods into infants and serves them sinlessly _(actors: Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śiva, Anasūyā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Vasiṣṭha releases the king from possession** — Refusing vengeance for his slain sons, Vasiṣṭha sprinkles consecrated water on the king, expelling the rākṣasa after twelve years and restoring his mind and kingship _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Kalmāṣapāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4)
- **Vishnu impersonates Jalandhara and breaks Vrinda's vow** — Vishnu conjures a vision of Jalandhara's death, then takes his form so the embrace breaks Vrinda's pativratya _(actors: Vishnu, Vrinda, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Padma Purana)
- **Yamī proposes union to Yama** — In the Ṛgvedic dialogue-hymn Yamī proposes incestuous union to her twin Yama, who refuses on grounds of dharma _(actors: Yamī, Yama)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Ṛgveda 10.10)
- **Andhaka transformed into the gana Bhringi** — Moved by his devotion, Shiva grants Andhaka liberation through service, making him a leader of his ganas, identified in Shaiva tradition with the emaciated devotee Bhringi _(actors: Shiva, Andhaka, Bhringi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/andhakasura-vadha.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda); Linga Purana)
- **Bhārgava lineage transmitted to Śaunaka** — Through Pramadvarā, Ruru fathers Śunaka, ancestor of Śaunaka, the sattra-patron at whose recitation the Mahābhārata is told _(actors: Ruru, Pramadvarā, Śunaka, Śaunaka, Sauti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ruru-pramadvara.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Pauloma sub-parva)
- **Bhrigu kicks Vishnu** — Tasked with judging which of the Trimurti is supreme, Bhrigu kicks the sleeping Vishnu in the chest, who responds by gently massaging his foot, winning the test as most forbearing and originating Vishnu's Shrivatsa mark _(actors: Bhrigu, Vishnu, Lakshmi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.89; Padma Purana)
- **Birth of Pururavas** — From Budha and Ila is born Pururavas, first sovereign of the Chandravamsha (Lunar dynasty) _(actors: Budha, Ila, Pururavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/soma-tara-budha.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.6-7; Bhagavata Purana 9.14)
- **Dadhichi gives his bones at the kshetra (Misrikh)** — At the twin site Misrikh within the Naimisha-kshetra, the sage Dadhichi surrenders his bones to forge the Vajra that slays Vritra _(actors: Dadhichi, Indra, (Vritra))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana 6.9-6.10; local mahatmya)
- **Daksha's Sacrifice and Sati's Self-immolation** — Daksha insults Shiva, Sati self-immolates, Virabhadra wrecks the yajna, and Daksha is restored with a goat's head _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva, Virabhadra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-7)
- **Dhruva's war on the Yakṣa city Alakā** — Enraged at Uttama's death, Dhruva marches on the Yakṣa city Alakāpurī and slaughters them with celestial weapons until his grandfather Svāyambhuva Manu stays his hand against killing innocents _(actors: Dhruva, Svāyambhuva Manu, Yakṣas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dhruva.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.10–4.11; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.12)
- **Dhruva wins the pole-star station** — The child-prince Dhruva performs austerity, wins Viṣṇu's vision, and is granted the immovable pole-star station (Dhruva-loka) _(actors: Dhruva, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4)
- **Distribution of Mada into the four vices** — Having won his point, Cyavana dissolves Mada and parcels 'Intoxication' out among drink, women, dice, and hunting — the origin of the four kingly vices _(actors: Cyavana, Mada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/cyavana-sukanya.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 125; Anuśāsana Parva 13.156)
- **Goddesses' plea and the boon to be born as sons** — The three goddesses beg back their husbands; Anasūyā restores them and the pleased Trimūrti grant they will be born as her sons _(actors: Sarasvatī, Lakṣmī, Pārvatī, Anasūyā, Trimūrti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/atri-anasuya.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa)
- **Indra Steals Pṛthu's Sacrificial Horse** — To prevent Pṛthu's hundredth aśvamedha from unseating him, Indra repeatedly steals the sacrificial horse in heretic disguise until Brahmā and Viṣṇu intervene and Pṛthu forgives him _(actors: Pṛthu, Indra, Brahmā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prithu-prithvi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.19-20)
- **Śiva remains as Tryambakeśvar Jyotirliṅga** — Śiva stays at the Godāvarī's source as the three-faced (Brahmā-Viṣṇu-Śiva) Tryambakeśvar Jyotirliṅga, 'Tryambaka on the bank of the Gautamī.' _(actors: Śiva (as Tryambakeśvar))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/godavari-gautami-dakshina-ganga.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Loan to Uśīnara of the Bhojas** — King Uśīnara begets Śibi on Mādhavī and pays 200 horses; only 600 horses are gathered, with 200 un-findable _(actors: Uśīnara, Mādhavī, Gālava, Śibi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/galava-madhavi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva ~118)
- **Niyoga birth of Aśmaka** — Because the death-on-intercourse curse stands, Vasiṣṭha begets a son on Queen Madayantī by niyoga; after a long gestation the stone-delivered child Aśmaka continues the Ayodhyā Solar line _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Madayantī, Aśmaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kalmashapada-saudasa.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.4; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.9)
- **Priyavrata's chariot-furrows carve the seven oceans and continents** — Driving his chariot around the Earth seven times to make a second sun's daylight, Priyavrata's wheel-ruts carve out the seven oceans and demarcate the seven dvipas _(actors: Priyavrata)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.1)
- **Pṛthu levels the earth and milks Pṛthivī** — The first consecrated king Pṛthu flattens the ground and, threatening the earth-as-cow, milks her of all crops and treasures, giving the earth her name Pṛthivī _(actors: Pṛthu, Pṛthivī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahmanda-purana.md) — (Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa (Vāyu-shared core))
- **Pṛthu milks and names the earth (origin-of-kingship variant)** — In the kingship-origin accounts, the first consecrated king is variously Manu Vaivasvata or Pṛthu son of Vena, from whom the earth (Pṛthivī) is milked and named _(actors: Pṛthu, Vena, Manu Vaivasvata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12)
- **Rishabha attains omniscience and nirvana (Jain)** — Witnessing the dancer Nilanjana's sudden death, Rishabha renounces, fasts a year broken by Shreyamsa's sugarcane juice, attains kevala-jnana at Purimatala, and reaches nirvana on Mount Ashtapada (Kailasa) _(actors: Rishabhanatha, Nilanjana, Shreyamsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Kalpa-sutra; Jain Adi-purana)
- **Rāvaṇa's world-conquest (digvijaya)** — Rāvaṇa defeats kings, yakṣas, and nāgas, subjugates Yama himself, overruns the three worlds, and abducts women _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 18–23)
- **Seed of the Ganga-descent (Bhagiratha)** — After Aṃśumān and Dilīpa fail, Bhagīratha's austerities bring Gaṅgā to earth (Śiva catching her fall) to redeem the 60,000 — the Gaṅgāvataraṇa _(actors: Bhagīratha, Gaṅgā, Śiva, Aṃśumān, Dilīpa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kapila-devahuti.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 42–44)
- **Shakuntala, Dushyanta, and the birth of Bharata** — The hermitage romance and lost signet-ring lead to the birth of Bharata, eponym of Bharata-varsha and founder of the Kuru love-story _(actors: Shakuntala, Dushyanta, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata-minor-episodes.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva)
- **Shiva's Tandava of grief and Vishnu's dismemberment of Sati** — Inconsolable Shiva carries Sati's corpse in a frenzied Tandava that threatens pralaya, so Vishnu cuts the corpse to pieces with his Sudarshana Chakra, the fragments falling across the subcontinent _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu, Sati)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/sati-daksha-and-parvati.md) — (Devi-Bhagavata VII; Kalika Purana; Mahabhagavata Purana)
- **Slaying of Jalandhara by Shiva** — As Vrinda's chastity lapses, Jalandhara's protection fails and Shiva beheads him with a cakra struck from his toe _(actors: Shiva, Jalandhara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jalandhara-vrinda.md) — (Shiva Purana (Yuddha-khanda))
- **Sparing of Maya and devotees** — Śiva spares the architect Maya and remnant true devotees who had not abandoned his worship _(actors: Śiva, Maya, Śaiva devotees)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tripura-dahana.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Tapatī weds Saṃvaraṇa and mothers Kuru** — The solar daughter Tapatī marries the Kuru king Saṃvaraṇa and becomes mother of Kuru, making the Mahābhārata clan partly solar-descended; the river Tāpī is named for her _(actors: Tapatī, Saṃvaraṇa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/surya-and-his-family.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **The milking of the Earth by Prithu** — Prithu pursues the Earth-cow with his bow and milks her of grain (using Manu as calf), naming her Prithvi and leveling the land for cultivation _(actors: Prithu, Earth (Prithvi), Svayambhuva Manu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-01-svayambhuva.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.17-18; Vishnu Purana 1.13)
- **The Māndhātā / Omkāreśvar tīrtha named for the king** — The sacred Narmadā island at Omkāreśvar is traditionally called Māndhātā, said to be named for the king who won the jyotirliṅga's manifestation there through tapas _(actors: Māndhātṛ, Śiva (Omkāreśvar))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mandhata.md) — (Sthala-purāṇa / regional Māhātmya tradition)
- **Tāraka-māya war and slaying of Tāraka** — Skanda leads the devas in the Tāraka-māya war and slays Tāraka with his śakti/spear, restoring the worlds _(actors: Skanda, the devas, Tāraka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/tarakasura-vadha.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Vāmana Purāṇa; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Tulasī curses Viṣṇu and is reborn as river and basil-plant** — Discovering the fraud, Tulasī curses Viṣṇu to become the śālagrāma stone; her body becomes the Gaṇḍakī river and her hair the sacred Tulasī plant _(actors: Tulasī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shankhachuda-tulasi.md) — (Brahma-Vaivarta Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa)
- **Vipula Guards Ruci by Yoga** — Charged to protect his guru's wife from Indra, the disciple Vipula enters her body by yoga to bar the seducer's reach _(actors: Vipula, Ruci, Devaśarman, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Anushasana Parva 40-43)
