- **Indra bears the Kalpavṛkṣa to Svarga** — The wish-fulfilling tree Kalpavṛkṣa emerges at the churning and Indra carries it to his paradise, rooting it in the Nandana-vana _(actors: Indra, Kalpavṛkṣa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Kalpavriksha (Wikipedia); Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **Jyeshtha/Alakshmi rises from the churning** — Alakshmi as Jyeshtha, elder sister of Lakshmi, rises from the churning before the nectar and is later married off to the sage Duhsaha, dwelling wherever inauspiciousness is found _(actors: Jyeshtha (Alakshmi), Duhsaha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/lakshmi.md) — (Linga Purana; Padma Purana)
- **Kapila teaches Devahuti (Kapilopadesa)** — The Kapila avatara, born to Kardama and Devahuti, teaches his mother devotional Sankhya and bhakti-yoga, a primary scriptural Sankhya source _(actors: Kapila, Devahuti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **King Indradyumna Seeks Nila-Madhava** — Satya-Yuga Malava king Indradyumna sends brahmin Vidyapati (who weds the Shabara chief's daughter Lalita) to find the secret Nila-Madhava image; it vanishes, directing the king to worship a sacred floating log instead _(actors: Indradyumna, Vidyapati, Vishvavasu, Lalita)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana)
- **Markandeya conquers death at the Shiva-linga** — At his destined hour of death the boy Markandeya clasps the Shiva-linga chanting the Maha-mrityunjaya mantra; Shiva bursts forth, defeats Yama, and grants him eternal youth _(actors: Markandeya, Shiva, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Skanda/Linga/Padma Puranas; Markandeya Purana)
- **Mohinī's Muktanṛtya dance-trap of Bhasmāsura** — Viṣṇu as Mohinī lures the ash-demon Bhasmāsura into mirroring her dance and touching his own head, reducing him to ashes (regional/folk version of the Vṛkāsura kernel) _(actors: Mohinī (Viṣṇu), Bhasmāsura, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mohini-avatara.md) — (Regional / folk tradition; Kathakali Bhasmāsura Mohinī (cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.88 Vṛkāsura))
- **Nārada initiates the child Dhruva** — Nārada meets the boy Dhruva, tests his resolve, sends him to Madhuvana, and bestows the dvādaśākṣara mantra that ignites Dhruva's penance _(actors: Nārada, Dhruva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 4.8; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.11–12)
- **Prahlāda expounds navadhā bhakti** — Confronting his father, Prahlāda declares Hari is everywhere and teaches the ninefold path of devotion, sealing his father's murderous resolve _(actors: Prahlāda, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5.23–24, 7.8)
- **The Kurma Purana spoken from the tortoise** — Vishnu in tortoise form narrates the Kurma Purana to sages and Devas/Asuras during the churning, the only Mahapurana named for its avatara-narrator _(actors: Vishnu as Kurma, the sages, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kurma-avatara.md) — (Kurma Purana (framing chapters))
- **Gaṅgādhara — Śiva bears the descent of Gaṅgā** — When Bhagīratha's penance brings the celestial Gaṅgā down to redeem Sagara's 60,000 sons, Śiva catches her world-shattering fall in his matted locks and releases her as a tamed stream, humbling her pride _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Śiva catches Gaṅgā in his locks (Gaṅgādhara)** — Śiva traps the plunging Gaṅgā in his matted hair to tame her, releasing her in a thinned stream — the Gaṅgādhara icon _(actors: Śiva, Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 43–44)
- **Mohini distributes the nectar to the Devas** — The Asuras seize the amrita; Vishnu takes the enchantress form Mohini, beguiles them, and serves the nectar only to the Devas _(actors: Vishnu (Mohini), Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Nārada's prenatal instruction of Prahlāda** — Kayādhu shelters in Nārada's hermitage during the deva-asura war and the unborn Prahlāda absorbs Nārada's teaching on Viṣṇu-bhakti, the root of his invincible devotion _(actors: Nārada, Kayādhu, the unborn Prahlāda)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.7)
- **The failed killings of Prahlāda** — Hiraṇyakaśipu has Prahlāda trampled, bitten, hurled from cliffs, burned, poisoned, and cast into the sea; Viṣṇu shields him each time. Folk tradition adds the Holikā fire-ordeal (etiology of Holī) _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Holikā, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.5; later Purāṇic/festival tradition (Holikā))
- **The Unfinished Carving of Jagannatha** — A divine carpenter carves the Puri triad on condition of being undisturbed; the door is opened early, so the images remain armless and legless, and Brahma is brought to consecrate the temple _(actors: Vishnu/Vishvakarma, Indradyumna, Gundica, Brahma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Madala Panji; Skanda Purana; Brahma & Narada Puranas)
- **Virabhadra destroys Daksha's sacrifice** — Enraged at Sati's death, Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of his hair, who destroy the yajna and behead Daksha; Shiva later revives Daksha with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Viṣṇu claims the Kaustubha jewel from the churning** — The supreme jewel Kaustubha emerges from the Samudra Manthana and Viṣṇu claims it, wearing it on his chest alongside the Śrīvatsa and Vaijayantī _(actors: Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8; Vishnu Purana; Kaustubha (Wikipedia))
- **Beheading of Svarbhānu (Origin of Rāhu and Ketu)** — During the Samudra Manthana the asura Svarbhanu disguises himself to sip the amrita; exposed by Sun and Moon, Vishnu as Mohini beheads him with the Sudarshana Chakra, and his immortal head becomes Rahu and body becomes Ketu, who cause eclipses _(actors: Svarbhanu, Vishnu (Mohini), Surya, Chandra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/navagraha-temples.md) — (Samudra Manthana cycle)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse; Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts it into pieces that fall across the land, founding the Shakti Pithas, and Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati, Vishnu, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Harishchandra's Truth-Test** — Harishchandra sells himself, wife, and son to honor a debt to Vishvamitra and is tested mercilessly but never lies, restored and ascending to heaven as the archetype of satya _(actors: Harishchandra, Vishvamitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Aitareya Brahmana; Devi-Bhagavata)
- **Indra Slays Vṛtra with the Vajra** — The drought-serpent Dānava Vṛtra withholds the cosmic waters and is slain by Indra with the vajra forged from sage Dadhīci's bones, releasing the seven rivers — the foundational Vedic combat _(actors: Indra, Vṛtra, Tvaṣṭṛ, Dadhīci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda 1.32; Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9-13)
- **The descent reaches the sea and redeems the ashes at Gaṅgāsāgar** — Gaṅgā follows Bhagīratha's chariot to the ocean and over the ashes of the 60,000 at Sāgara-dvīpa, granting them heaven — establishing the first ancestral water-rite tīrtha _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha, the 60,000 sons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gangasagar-sagara-dvipa-kapila-ashram.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 44; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.9)
- **The pillar challenge and Narasiṃha bursting forth** — Hiraṇyakaśipu strikes a pillar to disprove Viṣṇu's omnipresence; Narasiṃha, the man-lion, erupts from it roaring _(actors: Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.12–22; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 1.20; Narasiṃha Purāṇa)
- **Varāha lifts the Earth** — Viṣṇu as the boar (Varāha) raises the Earth from the cosmic waters — a Satya-Yuga / Manvantara-boundary avatāra event framing the Varāha Purāṇa _(actors: Varāha (Viṣṇu), Earth (Bhūmi))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Varāha Purāṇa)
- **Indra Decapitates Namuci with Sea-Foam** — Bound by a truce and a no-wet-no-dry boon, Indra beheads the asura Namuci at twilight with sea-foam wrapped on the vajra — the loophole-archetype and origin of his brahmahatyā guilt-stain _(actors: Indra, Namuci)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Ṛgveda; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Nārada instructs Prahlāda in the womb** — Nārada teaches the unborn Prahlāda (via Kayādhu), seeding the Vaiṣṇava devotion of the Narasiṃha cycle _(actors: Nārada, Prahlāda, Kayādhu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narada.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7)
- **Skanda slays Tārakāsura** — The Skanda Purāṇa records Skanda/Kārttikeya's birth and his slaying of the demon Tārakāsura _(actors: Skanda/Kārttikeya, Tārakāsura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa)
- **The threshold disembowelment of Hiraṇyakaśipu** — At twilight, on the doorway threshold, on his lap, with bare claws, Narasiṃha disembowels Hiraṇyakaśipu — voiding every loophole of the boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.8.23–29)
- **Uccaiḥśravas emerges from the churning** — The seven-headed snow-white horse-king Uccaiḥśravas arises at the Samudra-manthana, born of the amṛta, and is seized by Indra (or claimed by Bali) _(actors: Uccaiḥśravas, Indra, Bali)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.8)
- **War over the nectar and Indra restored** — Strengthened by the amrita, the Devas with Vishnu defeat the Asuras in the post-churning war and Indra is reinstated to Svarga _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras, Vishnu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/samudra-manthana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11; Mahabharata)
- **Agastya Drinks the Ocean Dry, Kālakeyas Slain** — The ocean-hiding Kālakeyas devour sages by night until the gods beg Agastya, who drinks the entire ocean dry, exposing and enabling the slaughter of the Kālakeya asuras _(actors: Agastya, Kālakeyas, Devas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Bhagiratha Brings Down the Ganga** — Through epic tapas Bhagiratha brings Ganga from heaven to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons, with Shiva catching her in his locks; the river is named Bhagirathi for him _(actors: Bhagiratha, Ganga, Shiva)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata IX.9)
- **Curse of the Sanaka-kumaras on Jaya and Vijaya** — Brahma's four child-sages curse Vishnu's gatekeepers Jaya and Vijaya to three demonic births, setting off the Hiranyaksha/Hiranyakashipu and later demon incarnations _(actors: Sanaka-kumaras, Jaya, Vijaya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.12, 3.15-3.16, 7.1)
- **Kāmadahana — the burning of Kāma** — Sent by the gods to kindle Śiva's desire for Pārvatī so a son can slay Tārakāsura, Kāmadeva fires his arrow and Śiva's third eye burns him to ash; Śiva later restores him bodiless (Ananga) _(actors: Śiva, Kāmadeva, Rati, Pārvatī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-myth-cycle.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa Rudra-saṃhitā; Matsya Purāṇa; Kālidāsa's Kumārasaṃbhava)
- **Prahlāda pacifies Narasiṃha's wrath** — Narasiṃha's fury terrifies even the gods and Lakṣmī; the child Prahlāda alone calms him with the Nṛsiṃha-stuti and is offered any boon _(actors: Narasiṃha, Prahlāda, Brahmā, Rudra, Indra, Lakṣmī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.9–7.10)
- **Samudra Manthana - the curse that triggers it** — Sage Durvasa gives Indra a divine garland which Indra's elephant Airavata tramples; Durvasa curses the devas to lose their fortune and strength, and Lakshmi withdraws into the ocean _(actors: Durvasa, Indra, Airavata, Lakshmi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.5; Vishnu Purana 1.9)
- **Varaha rescues Bhudevi from the cosmic ocean** — As Bhudevi, the Earth goddess is rescued by the boar Varaha from the cosmic ocean _(actors: Varaha, Bhudevi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/kamadeva-and-minor-deities.md) — (Daskavatara tradition)
- **Hiraṇyakaśipu liberated; Prahlāda enthroned** — Slain by the Lord's own hand, Hiraṇyakaśipu attains liberation (dveṣa-bhakti), discharging curse-birth #1; Narasiṃha enthrones Prahlāda as righteous daitya king, whose line leads to Bali _(actors: Narasiṃha, Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda, Bali (descendant))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/prahlada-narasimha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7.1, 7.10)
- **Kurma supports Mount Mandara** — As the churning rod Mount Mandara sinks, Vishnu becomes the giant tortoise Kurma and bears the mountain on his back as the pivot for churning the Ocean of Milk for amrita _(actors: Kurma/Vishnu, devas, asuras, Vasuki, Mandara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Vishnu Purana)
- **The Kadrū–Vinatā wager over the horse's tail** — Kadrū and Vinatā wager over the colour of Uccaiḥśravas's tail with the loser to become slave; Kadrū's nāga sons coil as black hairs to deceive, winning and enslaving Vinatā _(actors: Kadrū, Vinatā, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Tārakāsura Slain by Skanda** — The daitya Tāraka, boon-protected to die only by a son of Śiva, forces the gods to engineer Śiva's marriage to Pārvatī, whose son Kārttikeya/Skanda slays him in the Tārakāmaya war _(actors: Tārakāsura, Skanda, Śiva, Pārvatī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Kumārasambhava; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Varaha avatara rescues the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — The Asura Hiranyaksha drags Bhumi to the bottom of the cosmic ocean; Vishnu as the boar Varaha dives in, slays him in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth on his tusks _(actors: Vishnu (Varaha), Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Emergence of the fourteen ratnas** — During the churning fourteen treasures rise from the ocean — including Kamadhenu, Uccaihshravas, Airavata, Kaustubha, Parijata, the Apsaras, Lakshmi, Varuni, Candra, Shankha, and Dhanvantari with the amrita _(actors: the churning devas and asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8.8; Vishnu Purana; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Śiva Burns the Three Cities (Tripurāntaka)** — Three sons of Tāraka win three indestructible flying fortresses destroyable only by a single aligned arrow; Śiva as Tripurāntaka burns all three with one shaft from his earth-chariot _(actors: Śiva, Tārakākṣa, Vidyunmālī, Kamalākṣa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Mahābhārata Karṇa Parva; Śiva Purāṇa)
- **Kadrū curses the reluctant nāgas** — The serpents who refuse to deceive the tail are cursed by their mother Kadrū to perish in King Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, driving the Mahābhārata's nāga frame-story _(actors: Kadrū, the nāgas)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīkaparva)
- **Matsya saves Manu from the pralaya-flood** — Viṣṇu as the fish Matsya saves Manu and the seeds of life across the deluge — the Manvantara-transition framing the Matsya Purāṇa _(actors: Matsya (Viṣṇu), Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Andhaka Impaled by Śiva** — The blind asura Andhaka, born of Pārvatī covering Śiva's eyes, lusts after Pārvatī and is impaled on Śiva's triśūla until his clone-spawning blood dries, drunk by the Mātṛkās; redeemed, he becomes the gaṇa-chief Bhṛṅgi _(actors: Andhaka, Śiva, Pārvatī, Mātṛkās)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa)
- **Garuḍa ransoms Vinatā by stealing the amṛta** — To redeem his enslaved mother Vinatā, Garuḍa is forced to fetch the amṛta from Indra's heaven, originating his nectar-theft, his enmity with the serpents and his recruitment as Viṣṇu's vāhana _(actors: Garuḍa, Vinatā, Indra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/airavata-and-celestial-animals.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādiparva, Garuḍa cycle)
- **Narasiṃha slays Hiraṇyakaśipu** — Viṣṇu as the man-lion Narasiṃha kills the demon Hiraṇyakaśipu to protect the devotee Prahlāda — a Satya-Yuga avatāra event _(actors: Narasiṃha (Viṣṇu), Hiraṇyakaśipu, Prahlāda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Nṛsiṃha (Narasiṃha) Upapurāṇa)
- **Prahlada's devotion survives every attempt to kill him** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-bhakti by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Saptarishi carried across the flood by Vaivasvata Manu** — In the Matsya flood, Vaivasvata Manu carries the seven sages, the seed of all creatures, and the Vedas across the pralaya, re-seeding knowledge for the current humanity _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, the Saptarishi, Matsya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/saptarishi.md) — (Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Shiva drinks the Halahala poison (Nilakantha)** — To save the cosmos from the world-destroying Halahala poison that first rises, Shiva drinks it; Parvati holds his throat so it lodges there, turning it blue and earning him the name Nilakantha _(actors: Shiva, Parvati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Holika burns in the fire - origin of Holi** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but perishes while he survives, the origin myth of the festival of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk/festival tradition)
- **Jalandhara Slain by Śiva** — Jalandhara, born of Śiva's third-eye fire and shielded by his wife Vṛndā's chastity, is undone when Viṣṇu deceives Vṛndā in his form, and Śiva slays him with a toe-carved cakra; Vṛndā self-immolates and becomes the Tulsī plant _(actors: Jalandhara, Śiva, Viṣṇu, Vṛndā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Śiva Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Mohini distributes the amrita** — Vishnu takes the form of the enchantress Mohini, beguiles the Asuras who had seized the nectar pot, and distributes the amrita only to the Devas _(actors: Mohini/Vishnu, Devas, Asuras, Dhanvantari)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.8-8.9)
- **Beheading of Svarbhanu (origin of Rahu and Ketu)** — The Asura Svarbhanu disguises himself among the Devas to drink amrita; exposed by Surya and Candra, he is beheaded by the Sudarshana chakra, his immortal head and body becoming Rahu and Ketu who cause eclipses out of grudge _(actors: Svarbhanu/Rahu/Ketu, Surya, Candra, Mohini/Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Hiranyakasipu's boon of near-invincibility** — Hiranyakasipu obtains a boon of near-invincibility (not by man or beast, day or night, indoors or out), the second life of the Jaya-Vijaya curse _(actors: Hiranyakasipu, Brahma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Mahalakshmi born at the Samudra Manthana** — The supreme Lakshmi, consort of Vishnu, is born from the churning of the Ocean of Milk _(actors: Mahalakshmi, Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Vishnu Purana; Sri Sukta)
- **Narasimha avatara slays Hiranyakashipu** — Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha and kills Hiranyakashipu at twilight on the threshold upon his lap with claws, voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Vishnu (Narasimha), Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Sudarśana severs Rāhu at the churning** — Viṣṇu's Sudarśana Cakra severs the asura Rāhu's head at the Samudra Manthana after he steals a sip of amṛta _(actors: Viṣṇu, Rāhu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Sudarshana Chakra (Wikipedia))
- **The Matsya and Manu flood narrative** — Manu rears a tiny fish that grows into the giant Matsya, who tows his boat to safety through the deluge _(actors: Manu, Matsya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 185)
- **Churning of the Ocean (Samudra Manthana)** — Viśvāmitra tells the Bāla-Kāṇḍa version of devas and asuras churning the Milk-Ocean with Mandara and Vāsuki, yielding the Hālāhala poison, Dhanvantari, apsarases, and Amṛta _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Śiva, Vāsuki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 45)
- **Narasimha disembowels Hiranyakasipu** — The Man-Lion avatara bursts from a pillar at twilight to disembowel Hiranyakasipu, threading every clause of the boon, and saves Prahlada _(actors: Narasimha/Viṣṇu, Hiranyakasipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7)
- **Prahlada enthroned as righteous Asura king** — Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers; Prahlada is enthroned as a virtuous Asura king and becomes ancestor of Bali _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Bali)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **War over the nectar and Indra's reinstatement** — Devas and Asuras battle over the nectar; with strength restored the Devas prevail and Indra is reinstated as king of the gods _(actors: Indra, Devas, Asuras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.10-8.11)
- **Dhruva becomes the Pole Star** — Rebuffed by his stepmother, the boy Dhruva performs intense tapas guided by Narada; Vishnu appears and fixes him as the immovable Dhruva Nakshatra around which the Saptarshi revolve _(actors: Dhruva, Uttanapada, Suniti, Suruci, Narada, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.11-1.12; Bhagavata Purana 4.8-4.12 (canonically Svayambhuva Manvantara))
- **Varaha lifts the Earth and slays Hiranyaksha** — When the Asura Hiranyaksha drags Earth (Bhumi) to the bottom of the cosmic ocean, Vishnu becomes the colossal boar Varaha, slays Hiranyaksha in a thousand-year duel, and lifts the Earth back on his tusks _(actors: Varaha/Vishnu, Hiranyaksha, Bhumi/Prithivi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.13, 3.17-3.19; Vishnu Purana 1.4)
- **Daksha Yajna and Sati's self-immolation** — Prajapati Daksha snubs his daughter Sati and her husband Shiva at a grand yajna; the insulted Sati immolates herself in the sacrificial fire _(actors: Daksha, Sati, Shiva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.2-4.4; Shiva Purana; Kalidasa Kumarasambhava)
- **Hiranyakashipu's boon of near-invulnerability** — Enraged at his brother's death, Hiranyakashipu performs extreme tapas and wins from Brahma a boon that he cannot be slain by man or beast, day or night, indoors or outdoors, on earth or sky, by any weapon, then tyrannizes the three worlds _(actors: Hiranyakashipu, Brahma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.3-7.4; Harivamsha)
- **Nimi and Vasishtha's Mutual Curse** — Nimi and his purohita Vasishtha curse each other to bodilessness over a sacrifice dispute; from Nimi's churned body is born Janaka, founding the Videha/Mithila line _(actors: Nimi, Vasishtha, Janaka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Vishnu Purana IV.5; Bhagavata IX.13)
- **Samudra-manthana (churning of the milk-ocean)** — Devas and asuras churn the milk-ocean with the Kurma avatara as pivot, producing amṛta, Dhanvantari, and Lakṣmi _(actors: Devas, Asuras, Kurma/Viṣṇu, Dhanvantari, Lakṣmi)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Manu and the Flood (Matsya Avatara)** — The fish-avatara (Matsya) saves Manu from the cosmic deluge in the earliest extant Hindu flood narrative recorded in the Shatapatha Brahmana _(actors: Manu, Matsya/Vishnu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/yajurveda.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1)
- **Mohini tricks the asuras out of the nectar** — The Mohini avatara enchants the asuras and distributes the amṛta to the devas, denying the demons immortality _(actors: Mohini/Viṣṇu, Asuras, Devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Prahlada's devotion and survival** — Hiranyakashipu's son Prahlada, taught Vishnu-devotion by Narada in the womb, becomes a supreme devotee and survives his father's repeated murder attempts by poison, elephants, weapons, and fire _(actors: Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu, Narada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.5)
- **Virabhadra's rampage and beheading of Daksha** — Enraged Shiva creates Virabhadra and Bhadrakali from a lock of hair; they destroy the yajna and behead Daksha, who is later revived with a goat's head _(actors: Shiva, Virabhadra, Bhadrakali, Daksha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 4.5-4.7; Shiva Purana)
- **Founding of the Shakti Pithas and Sati's rebirth as Parvati** — Shiva wanders bearing Sati's corpse, which Vishnu's Sudarshana cuts into pieces that fall across the land founding the 51 Shakti Pithas; Sati reincarnates as Parvati _(actors: Shiva, Sati/Parvati, Vishnu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Devi Bhagavata; Kalika Purana; Tantra literature)
- **Holika burned (origin of Holi)** — Prahlada's fire-proof aunt Holika sits with him in flames to burn him but herself perishes while he survives — the origin myth of Holi _(actors: Holika, Prahlada)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; folk tradition)
- **Narasimha Bursts from the Pillar to Slay Hiranyakashipu** — In defense of the boy-devotee Prahlada, the man-lion Narasimha bursts from a pillar at dusk and slays the demon-king Hiranyakashipu _(actors: Narasimha, Prahlada, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.1-10)
- **Ikshvaku founds the Solar dynasty** — Vaivasvata Manu's eldest son Ikshvaku, granted Aryavarta/Kosala, becomes progenitor of the Suryavamsha, the line of Mandhata, Sagara, Bhagiratha, Raghu, and Rama _(actors: Ikshvaku, Vaivasvata Manu, Nimi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.2-4.4; Harivamsha)
- **Matsya saves Satyavrata and the Vedas from the flood** — The Fish avatara saves Satyavrata (Manu), the seeds of life, and the Vedas from the dissolution-flood, the manvantara-transition par excellence _(actors: Matsya/Viṣṇu, Satyavrata/Manu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8)
- **Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu** — When challenged whether Vishnu is in a pillar, Hiranyakashipu smashes it and Vishnu bursts out as the man-lion Narasimha, seizing the Asura at twilight on the threshold upon his lap and disemboweling him with claws — voiding every clause of the boon _(actors: Narasimha/Vishnu, Hiranyakashipu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.8)
- **Pururavas and Urvashi** — The first mortal king of the Lunar line loves the apsara Urvashi under conditions, loses her when they break, and is eventually reunited _(actors: Pururavas, Urvashi)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Rigveda X.95; Shatapatha Brahmana XI; Vishnu Purana)
- **Dhanvantari Emerges at the Churning Bearing Amrita** — The divine physician Dhanvantari rises from the Samudra Manthana carrying the pot of amrita, linking the churning of the ocean to the origin of Ayurveda _(actors: Dhanvantari, devas, asuras)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upavedas-vedangas-darshanas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Ila/Sudyumna and the founding of the Lunar dynasty** — From Vaivasvata Manu's gender-shifting child Ila/Sudyumna springs the Lunar dynasty (Chandravamsha) via Budha _(actors: Vaivasvata Manu, Ila/Sudyumna, Budha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 4.1; Bhagavata Purana 9.1)
- **Prahlada enthroned as Asura king** — After Narasimha's fury is pacified by Prahlada's prayers, Prahlada is enthroned as a righteous Asura king and ancestor of Bali _(actors: Prahlada, Narasimha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.9-7.10)
- **Kapila burns the 60,000 sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates King Sagara's 60,000 sons for accusing him of stealing the ashvamedha horse, the curse later driving Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, Sagara's sons, Bhagiratha)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Kapila burns the sons of Sagara** — Sage Kapila incinerates the 60,000 sons of King Sagara for accusing him of stealing the sacrificial horse — the curse that later drives Bhagiratha's bringing-down of the Ganga _(actors: Kapila, the 60,000 sons of Sagara)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/01-satya-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8; Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Markandeya granted a short brilliant life** — The childless sage Mrkandu propitiates Shiva and chooses a virtuous son fated to die at sixteen; the radiant boy Markandeya is born and masters the Vedas _(actors: Mrkandu, Marudvati/Manasvini, Markandeya, Shiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Matsya Rescues Manu and the Vedas** — The fish-avatara Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge at the pralaya _(actors: Matsya, Manu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Descent of Ganga (Gangavatarana)** — Ganga is brought to earth by Bhagiratha's austerities, her fall broken by Shiva's matted hair, to liberate the ashes of Sagara's sons _(actors: Ganga, Bhagiratha, Shiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Ramayana Balakanda; Bhagavata; Mahabharata)
- **Shiva as Kalantaka conquers Death for Markandeya** — When Yama casts his noose around the boy clinging to a Shiva-linga, Shiva bursts forth as Kalantaka/Mrtyunjaya, strikes down Death, and blesses Markandeya to remain eternally sixteen and deathless _(actors: Markandeya, Shiva (Kalantaka/Mrtyunjaya), Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/markandeya.md) — (Shiva Purana; Linga Purana)
- **Sudarshana Chakra beheads Rahu** — Vishnu's time-disc the Sudarshana Chakra (Kala-chakra) beheads the demon Rahu who stole the amrita, the weapon-face of Time cutting off every form at its appointed moment _(actors: Vishnu, Rahu)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/kalachakra-wheel-of-time.md) — (Mahabharata; Bhagavata Purana; Vishnu Purana)
- **Rishabhadeva avatara born to Nabhi and Merudevi** — Vishnu descends as Rishabha, son of King Nabhi and Merudevi of the Priyavrata line, an avatara of Narayana who fathers a hundred sons, the eldest being Bharata _(actors: Rishabhadeva, Nabhi, Merudevi, Jayanti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.3-5.4; Vishnu Purana 2.1)
- **Rishabha's renunciation and death by forest fire** — After delivering the Rishabha-gita to his sons and crowning Bharata, Rishabha wanders as a naked avadhuta and quits his body, consumed by a wildfire, absorbed in the Self _(actors: Rishabhadeva, Bharata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.5-5.6)
- **Emperor Bharata's reign and renunciation** — Bharata rules Bharata-varsha righteously while inwardly detached, then divides the empire among his sons and retires to Pulaha-ashrama on the Gandaki to meditate _(actors: Bharata, Panchajani)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.7)
- **Bharata's attachment to the deer and rebirth as a deer** — The ascetic Bharata becomes attached to an orphaned fawn he rescues; dying with the deer in his mind, he is reborn as a conscious deer remembering his past life _(actors: Bharata, the fawn/deer)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.8)
- **Jada Bharata the silent sage and the Rahugana teachings** — Reborn as a brahmana, the soul feigns idiocy as Jada Bharata, is nearly sacrificed to Bhadra Kali (who saves him), then teaches King Rahugana the forest-of-samsara allegory and attains liberation _(actors: Jada Bharata, King Rahugana, Bhadra Kali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishabha-bharata-jada.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.9-5.14)
- **Satya Yuga — the Age of Truth** — Dharma stands on all four legs; humans live ~100,000 years in spontaneous righteousness, with meditation as the path to liberation _(actors: humanity)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.3, Bhagavata Purana 12.3)
- **Soma emerges from the churning of the ocean** — In the Samudra Manthana the Moon (Soma/Chandra) emerges among the fourteen ratnas and is taken by Shiva onto his head, fusing the soma-as-nectar and soma-as-moon ideas _(actors: Soma/Chandra, Shiva, devas and asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/chandra-soma.md) — (Bhagavata, Vishnu, Matsya Puranas)
- **Kapila born to Kardama and Devahuti** — Kapila, an avatara of Viṣṇu and founder-sage of Sankhya, is born to the Prajapati Kardama and Devahuti to impart self-knowledge to his mother _(actors: Kapila, Kardama, Devahuti)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/samkhya-karika.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 3.24-33)
- **Matsya rescues Manu and the Vedas from the deluge** — Vishnu as the fish Matsya warns Manu of the coming pralaya, has him build a boat loaded with the seeds of life and the seven sages, tows it through the flood, and (in variants) slays the demon Hayagriva to restore the stolen Vedas — marking the start of our Manvantara _(actors: Matsya (Vishnu), Manu, the saptarshi, Hayagriva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Shatapatha Brahmana 1.8.1; Matsya Purana; Bhagavata Purana 8.24)
- **Kurma supports Mount Mandara at the churning** — As devas and asuras churn the ocean of milk for amrita using Mount Mandara and the serpent Vasuki, the sinking mountain is supported on the back of Vishnu as the giant tortoise Kurma _(actors: Kurma (Vishnu), devas, asuras, Vasuki)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.7-8; Vishnu Purana 1.9; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Dhanvantari and Mohini emerge at the churning** — During the Samudra Manthana the physician-god Dhanvantari emerges bearing the nectar pot, and Vishnu takes the Mohini form to trick the asuras out of the amrita _(actors: Dhanvantari, Mohini (Vishnu), devas, asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8; Vishnu Purana)
- **Narasimha slays Hiranyakashipu and saves Prahlada** — To evade the demon-king Hiranyakashipu's boon, Vishnu bursts from a pillar as the man-lion Narasimha at twilight on a threshold, and disembowels him with his claws while saving his devotee-son Prahlada _(actors: Narasimha (Vishnu), Hiranyakashipu, Prahlada)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 7.2-10; Vishnu Purana 1.16-20)
- **Rahu beheaded at the churning** — At the Samudra Manthana the asura Rahu steals the amrita and is beheaded by Vishnu as Mohini, becoming the eclipse-node _(actors: Rahu, Mohini (Vishnu))_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devas-asuras-and-the-lokas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8; Vishnu Purana)
- **Exile of the Daityas and Danavas** — In Krita/Satya Yuga the Daityas and Danavas are exiled from heaven by the devas and take refuge in the Vindhya mountains and the sea (Patala) _(actors: Daityas, Danavas, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devas-asuras-and-the-lokas.md) — (Puranas)

## Tretā Yuga  ·  974 events

*Dharma on three legs. Vāmana, Paraśurāma, and the Rāmāyaṇa.*

- **Śabarī awaits Rāma at Pampā Sarovar** — Directed by Kabandha, Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa reach the lake-side āśrama where the ascetic Śabarī, having long awaited Rāma's darśana, offers him fruit (famously pre-tasted berries) before attaining liberation _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Śabarī, (Kabandha, sage Mataṅga))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kishkindha-hampi-anegundi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 70–74; folk amplification of the tasted berries)
- **Agastya directs Rāma to Pañcavaṭī** — Agastya gifts Rāma Viṣṇu's bow and divine weapons and names Pañcavaṭī on the Godāvarī as the exiles' dwelling-site _(actors: Rāma, Agastya, Lakṣmaṇa, Sītā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/panchavati-nashik-godavari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 11–13)
- **Śatrughna Slays Lavaṇāsura and Founds Mathurā** — Mathurā is said to be founded where Śatrughna, Rāma's brother, slays the asura Lavaṇa, son of Madhu, bridging the Rāmāyaṇa and Kṛṣṇa eras _(actors: Śatrughna, Lavaṇāsura)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mathura-vrindavan-braj.md) — (Ramayana, Uttara-kanda; Vishnu Purana)
- **Bali's Conquest of the Three Worlds** — Revived and empowered by Śukra and the Bhṛgus, the Asura king Bali storms Svarga and dispossesses Indra, becoming sovereign of all three worlds _(actors: Bali, Śukrācārya, Indra, Devas, Bhṛgu brahmins)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vamana-bali.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.15)
- **Bharadvāja receives Rāma on the exile journey** — On the vana-yātrā, Rāma, Sītā and Lakṣmaṇa cross the Yamunā and reach the sage Bharadvāja's āśrama at the Prayāga confluence; he honours them and directs them onward to Chitrakūṭa as the place of exile-dwelling _(actors: Bharadvāja, Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa sargas ~50–56)
- **Birth and naming of Raghu** — Raghu is born to Dilipa and Sudakshina after Dilipa's service to the wish-cow Nandini, named 'the swift' for his future conquests _(actors: Raghu, Dilipa, Sudakshina, Nandini, Vasishtha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/raghu.md) — (Raghuvamsha 3.1-21)
- **Birth in the Bhargava line** — Paraśurāma, aṃśa of Viṣṇu, is born to the Bhṛgu sage Jamadagni and Reṇukā as the youngest of five sons _(actors: Jamadagni, Reṇukā, Paraśurāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/parashurama.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15; Mahābhārata 3.115)
- **Birth of Hanuman to Anjana and Vayu** — Hanuman is born to the apsara-turned-vanari Anjana and the vanara chief Kesari, conceived through the agency of Vayu, making him Vayuputra _(actors: Hanuman, Anjana, Kesari, Vayu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/hanuman.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Kishkindha Kanda 66; Uttara Kanda 35-36)
- **Birth of Lakṣmaṇa and the pāyasa division** — From Daśaratha's putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice a divine being yields sacred pāyasa; Sumitrā's two half-portions produce the twins Lakṣmaṇa and Śatrughna, Lakṣmaṇa attaching to Rāma _(actors: Daśaratha, Sumitrā, Lakṣmaṇa, Śatrughna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/lakshmana.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa)
- **Birth of Māndhātā from His Father's Body** — The Ikṣvāku cakravartin Māndhātā is born from his father's body after the king drank consecrated fertility-water, and is suckled by Indra _(actors: Māndhātā, Yuvanāśva, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Vana & Drona Parvas; Bhagavata 9; Vishnu Purana)
- **Birth of Rāvaṇa and his siblings** — Approaching Viśravas at an inauspicious twilight, Kaikasī bears the ten-headed Rāvaṇa (marked by ill omens), Kumbhakarṇa, the righteous Vibhīṣaṇa, and Śūrpaṇakhā _(actors: Viśravas, Kaikasī, Rāvaṇa, Kumbhakarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, Śūrpaṇakhā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ravana.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa)
- **Birth of Sītā from the furrow** — Ploughing a sacrificial field, King Janaka turns up an infant girl in the furrow and adopts her as Sītā, an ayonijā born of the Earth-goddess _(actors: Janaka, Sītā, Bhūmi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/sita.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Birth of Tāṭakā from Suketu** — The childless yakṣa Suketu wins from Brahmā a daughter, Tāṭakā, endowed with the strength of a thousand elephants _(actors: Suketu, Brahmā, Tāṭakā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/tataka.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 25)
- **Birth of the Shloka Meter (Valmiki's Curse)** — Grieving a hunter's killing of a mating krauncha bird, Valmiki utters a curse that spontaneously takes metrical form, birthing the shloka (shoka to shloka) — the meter of Sanskrit epic _(actors: Valmiki, the hunter, krauncha birds)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/README.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 2)
- **Birth of Vālī and Sugrīva from Ṛkṣaraja** — The vānara lord Ṛkṣaraja is transformed into a woman; Indra's seed on his hair begets Vālī and Sūrya's on his nape begets Sugrīva _(actors: Ṛkṣaraja, Indra, Sūrya, Vālī, Sugrīva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/sugriva-and-vali.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara-kāṇḍa)
- **Birth of Ṛśyaśṛṅga from a doe** — Vibhāṇḍaka's seed is swallowed by a doe, who bears a single-horned boy raised in total isolation, ignorant of women, his chastity amassing great tapas _(actors: Vibhāṇḍaka, the doe, Ṛśyaśṛṅga)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishyashringa.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~110)
- **Brahmā creates Ahalyā and the contest for her hand** — Brahmā fashions the flawless Ahalyā and sets a circumambulation-of-the-worlds contest; Gautama wins her by a ritual technicality over Indra, seeding Indra's grudge _(actors: Brahmā, Ahalyā, Gautama, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/gautama-ahalya.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa; Padma Purāṇa)
- **Choice of Citrakūṭa on Bharadvāja's counsel** — After crossing the Gaṅgā with Guha and reaching Bharadvāja's Prayāga āśrama, Rāma is directed to settle at Citrakūṭa as the ideal tapovana _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Guha the Niṣāda, sage Bharadvāja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/chitrakoot-kamadgiri.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 54)
- **Ṛcīka's swapped oblations and the birth of Jamadagni** — Two caru-porridges meant for brahmin and warrior sons are exchanged between Satyavatī and her mother, deferring the kṣatriya temper a generation so Jamadagni is born serene but Paraśurāma becomes the axe-bearer _(actors: Ṛcīka, Satyavatī, Gādhi's wife, Jamadagni (unborn))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jamadagni-parashurama.md) — (Mahābhārata 3.115; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15)
- **Counsel at the putrakāmeṣṭi — relaying the Sanatkumāra prophecy** — Sumantra privately advises childless Daśaratha, recalling Sanatkumāra's forecast about Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, prompting the son-seeking sacrifice sealed by Vasiṣṭha _(actors: Sumantra, Daśaratha, Vasiṣṭha, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga (referenced), Sanatkumāra (prophecy))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/sumantra.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa ~8–11)
- **Daśaratha resolves to crown Rāma yuvarāja** — The aged Daśaratha resolves to install Rāma as crown prince while he lives; the assembly acclaims the choice and the rite is rushed under Puṣya nakṣatra _(actors: Daśaratha, Rāma, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/2-ayodhya-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa 1–4)
- **Daśaratha's righteous reign as last pre-Rāma Ikṣvāku king** — Daśaratha, son of Aja and grandson of Raghu, reigns at Ayodhyā as the last Sūryavaṃśa king before Rāma, prosperous but childless, served by Vasiṣṭha and his ministers _(actors: Daśaratha, Aja, Raghu, Vasiṣṭha, Kausalyā, Kaikeyī, Sumitrā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/dasharatha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla 5–8; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.10; Kālidāsa Raghuvaṃśa 8–9)
- **Descent of the Gaṅgā at Gaṅgā-dvāra** — The Gaṅgā debouches from the Himalaya onto the plain at Haridwar, the gateway by which the goddess first enters the world of men, linked to Bhagīratha's bringing-down of the river _(actors: Gaṅgā, Bhagīratha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva)
- **Descent of the Sarayū from Brahmā's Mānasa lake** — The Sarayū flows forth from Brahmā's Mānasa(rovara) lake, whence its name (sarat, 'flows out'), and runs to meet the Gaṅgā _(actors: Brahmā, Sarayū (river); pointed out by Viśvāmitra to Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sarayu-ayodhya-river.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 23–24; (variant) Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya — Viṣṇu's foot-thumb)
- **Devas petition Brahmā for the Nāṭyaveda** — At the Tretā-yuga's dawn the gods ask Brahmā for an accessible 'fifth Veda' diversion open to all four varṇas _(actors: Devas, Brahmā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/natya-shastra-and-the-classical-arts.md) — (Nāṭya Śāstra ch. 1)
- **Dilīpa's childlessness and the journey to Vasiṣṭha** — The ideal Sūryavaṃśa king Dilīpa, childless despite a flawless reign, drives with queen Sudakṣiṇā to Vasiṣṭha's hermitage to seek the cause and cure _(actors: Dilīpa, Sudakṣiṇā, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dilipa-nandini.md) — (Raghuvaṃśa 1.12–58 (Kālidāsa))
- **Dilīpa's childlessness and Vasiṣṭha's diagnosis** — The childless King Dilīpa and Queen Sudakṣiṇā learn from Vasiṣṭha that a slight to the wish-cow Surabhi keeps them sonless _(actors: Dilīpa, Sudakṣiṇā, Vasiṣṭha, Surabhi/Kāmadhenu)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raghuvamsha-kalidasa-kings.md) — (Raghuvaṃśa 1.31–55)
- **Ganga springs from Vishnu's foot (Vamana)** — When Vamana's raised step pierces the cosmic shell, the Causal Ocean pours in and washes his foot, becoming the Ganga, hence Vishnupadi _(actors: Ganga, Vamana/Vishnu)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ganga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 5.17)
- **Gādhi's place in the Kuśika line** — Gādhi, Lunar-dynasty king of Kānyakubja in the Kuśika branch, stands as the genealogical hinge-node father of Viśvāmitra and Satyavatī _(actors: Gādhi, Kuśa, Kuśanābha, ancestors of the Kuśika line)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/gadhi-and-the-caru-swap.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.7; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.15; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 32–34; Mahābhārata Ādi & Vana Parva)
- **Guha welcomes Rama at Shringaverapura** — The Nishada chief Guha rushes out, embraces his friend Rama, and offers his whole kingdom; Rama accepts only water and fodder _(actors: Guha, Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Nishadas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/guha.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana Ayodhya-kanda 50)
- **Hanumān meets Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa** — Sent by the anxious Sugrīva, Hanumān approaches the brothers disguised as a mendicant, is reassured of their good faith, and carries them on his shoulders to Sugrīva _(actors: Hanumān, Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/4-kishkindha-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Kiṣkindhā Kāṇḍa 3–4)
- **Hanumān's leap across the ocean** — From Mount Mahendra Hanumān launches a hundred-yojana leap across the southern ocean toward Laṅkā _(actors: Hanumān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/5-sundara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Sundara Kāṇḍa 1)
- **Hanumān's leap and search of Laṅkā** — Hanumān crosses the ocean, searches Rāvaṇa's city by night, and comes upon the Aśoka-vāṭikā _(actors: Hanumān, Rāvaṇa (city))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/lanka-ramayana-trail-ashoka-vatika.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Sundara Kāṇḍa 14–15)
- **Hariścandra's vow to Varuṇa and Rohita's birth** — Childless Hariścandra vows to sacrifice his firstborn to Varuṇa; a son Rohita is born, but the king endlessly postpones the offering _(actors: Hariścandra, Varuṇa, Rohita, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sunahshepa.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 7.13-14)
- **Harishchandra's vow to Varuna for a son** — Childless King Harishchandra prays to Varuna and vows to sacrifice his promised son; Varuna grants the boon and Rohita is born _(actors: Harishchandra, Varuna, Rohita, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sunahshepa.md) — (Aitareya Brahmana 7.13-14)
- **Śibi and the dove — the flesh-offering** — Indra (hawk) and Agni (dove) test King Śibi, who protects the refugee dove by offering his own flesh equal to its weight, finally his whole body _(actors: Śibi, Indra, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shibi.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~130-131)
- **Indumatī's svayaṃvara at Vidarbha** — At her bride-choice, Indumatī passes the gallery of suitor-kings and garlands Aja, choosing him before all the assembled royalty _(actors: Aja, Indumatī, Sunandā, the suitor-kings of Magadha/Aṅga/Avantī/etc.)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/aja-indumati.md) — (Kālidāsa, Raghuvaṃśa canto 6)
- **Jabali counsels Rama (materialist argument)** — The brahmin Jabali urges Rama with proto-Carvaka materialist arguments (no afterlife, ritual for the dead is futile); Rama rebukes him _(actors: Jabali, Rama)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/nastika-darshanas-and-the-astika-nastika-frame.md) — (Ramayana, Ayodhya Kanda 108-109)
- **Janaka's debate-assembly convened** — King Janaka of Videha assembles the learned Brahmins at a sacrifice, offering a thousand gold-horned cattle to the greatest knower of Brahman; Yājñavalkya claims the prize, provoking eight challengers _(actors: King Janaka of Videha, Yājñavalkya, the assembled Brahmins)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/gargi-and-maitreyi.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.1)
- **Kabandha's double curse and disfigurement** — The celestial being (Viśvāvasu/Danu) is struck by Indra's vajra into a headless trunk and cursed by sage Sthūlaśiras to remain a monster until Rāma severs his arms and burns him _(actors: Viśvāvasu/Kabandha, Indra, Sthūlaśiras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kabandha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 71)
- **Kaikasī's washed-away earthen liṅga** — Rāvaṇa's mother Kaikasī loses her daily sand liṅga to the tide and Rāvaṇa vows to fetch Śiva's true Ātma-liṅga _(actors: Kaikasī, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gokarna-mahabaleshwar-atma-linga.md) — (Gokarṇa-māhātmya; Sahyādri tradition)
- **Kaikeyī's marriage-condition** — Aśvapati gives Kaikeyī to Daśaratha on the condition that her son inherit Ayodhyā's throne _(actors: Aśvapati, Daśaratha, Kaikeyī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kaikeyi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā 107/99)
- **Kauśika's hospitality at Vasiṣṭha's hermitage** — King Kauśika, resting with his army, is feasted entirely by Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā/Kāmadhenu, igniting his covetousness for it _(actors: Viśvāmitra (Kauśika), Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vishwamitra-vasishtha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 51-53)
- **Kāmadhenu conflict — the spark** — King Kauśika tries to seize Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Śabalā/Nandinī by force after the sage refuses to sell her _(actors: Viśvāmitra (Kauśika), Vasiṣṭha, Śabalā/Nandinī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vishwamitra-vasishtha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 51-55; Mahābhārata)
- **Lakṣmaṇa's request for liberating knowledge** — After Rāma's coronation at Ayodhyā, Lakṣmaṇa asks his brother to teach him the bhakti and jñāna by which one crosses saṃsāra, supplying the Gītā's seeker-frame _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rama-gita.md) — (Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa (book 7) sarga 5)
- **Mantharā sees Ayodhyā festive** — Mantharā climbs the palace terrace and learns Rāma is to be consecrated yuvarāja the next dawn _(actors: Mantharā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/manthara.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā Kāṇḍa 7)
- **Mataṅga's disciples promise Śabarī that Rāma will come** — The aged tribal ascetic Śabarī, having humbly served Mataṅga's hermitage, is blessed by the departing sages and told to wait at Pampā for Rāma _(actors: Śabarī, sage Mataṅga and his disciples)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shabari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya-kāṇḍa 74)
- **Mārīca and Subāhu defile Viśvāmitra's sacrifice** — Mārīca and his brother Subāhu rain flesh and blood on Viśvāmitra's forest yajña, which the boy-princes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa are sent to guard _(actors: Mārīca, Subāhu, Viśvāmitra, Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/maricha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 19-26)
- **Nahuṣa installed as Indra** — After Indra flees the sin of slaying Vṛtra, the gods elect the virtuous mortal emperor Nahuṣa to the vacant throne of heaven, augmenting his tapas _(actors: Nahuṣa, Indra, the devas, ṛṣis)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nahusha.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva 11-12; Bhāgavata 6.13)
- **Śāntā fostered from Ayodhyā to Aṅga** — Daśaratha of Ayodhyā gives his daughter Śāntā (born to Kausalyā), elder sister of Rāma, as a foster/adopted daughter to his childless friend King Lomapāda of Aṅga, where she is raised as the Aṅga princess _(actors: Śāntā, Daśaratha, Kausalyā, Lomapāda (Romapāda))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishyashringa.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana-parva ~113; Rāmāyaṇa Bāla-kāṇḍa ~9–11; Purāṇic genealogies)
- **Paraśurāma Fills Five Lakes with Kṣatriya Blood** — Between Tretā and Dvāpara, Paraśurāma in his twenty-one exterminations of the kṣatriyas fills five lakes at Samanta-pañcaka with their blood and offers tarpaṇa, naming the field _(actors: Paraśurāma)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kurukshetra-dharmakshetra.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi-parva 2)
- **Paraśurāma receives the Paraśu from Śiva** — After his austerities, Paraśurāma is gifted Śiva's battle-axe (paraśu), the name-giving weapon of the sixth Daśāvatāra ('Rāma-with-the-axe'), with which he later annihilated the kṣatriya warrior-class twenty-one times over _(actors: Śiva, Paraśurāma)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Mahābhārata; Purāṇic Paraśurāma cycle)
- **Paraśurāma retires to Mahendragiri** — After exterminating the kṣatriyas twenty-one times and ceding the conquered earth (to Kaśyapa / to Rāma Dāśarathi), the immortal sixth avatāra Paraśurāma withdraws from worldly action and retires to Mahendragiri in the Eastern Ghāts to perform tapas until the end of the age, making the peak a living Paraśurāma-tīrtha _(actors: Paraśurāma, Kaśyapa, Rāma Dāśarathi)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Mahābhārata (Vana-parva, Śānti-parva); Rāmāyaṇa (Bāla-kāṇḍa))
- **Puṣpaka halted over Kailāsa** — Rāvaṇa's aerial car Puṣpaka is mysteriously halted as he crosses Mount Kailāsa returning from conquest _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Puṣpaka (vimāna))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ravana-kailasa-ravananugraha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttarakāṇḍa 16)
- **Purūravas born of Budha and Ilā** — Purūravas is born to Budha (son of the Moon) and Ilā, Manu's gender-shifting child, grafting Manu's line onto the Moon's at the hinge of the Lunar dynasty _(actors: Purūravas, Budha, Ilā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pururavas-urvashi.md) — (Bhagavata Purana IX.1, IX.14; Vishnu Purana IV.1, IV.6)
- **Putrakāmeṣṭi and the divine pāyasa** — Daśaratha's son-seeking sacrifice via Ṛṣyaśṛṅga yields divine pāyasa from the fire to be shared among the queens _(actors: Daśaratha, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Yajña-puruṣa, Kausalyā, Kaikeyī, Sumitrā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/sumitra.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 15-16)
- **Putrakāmeṣṭi sacrifice and the divine pāyasa** — Daśaratha performs the son-seeking sacrifice; a being from the fire brings golden pāyasa to beget heirs in whom Viṣṇu descends _(actors: Daśaratha, Ṛṣyaśṛṅga, Agni/divine messenger, the three queens)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kausalya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 14–16)
- **Reṇukā's chastity and the magic pot** — Reṇukā, chaste wife of Jamadagni, carries water in an unbaked sand pot held together by her faith alone _(actors: Reṇukā, Jamadagni)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/renuka-yellamma.md) — (Mahābhārata 3.116; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; folk Māhātmyas)
- **Reṇukā's unbaked-pot chastity feat** — Reṇukā, by the power of her perfect chastity, daily moulds a fresh unbaked clay/sand pot at the riverbank and carries water in it back to Jamadagni's hermitage, sometimes balancing it on a live coiled cobra _(actors: Reṇukā, Jamadagni)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-forms-and-navadurga.md) — (Mahābhārata 3 (Vana-parvan); Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; South Indian folk Māhātmyas)
- **Rāma despondent before the final duel** — On the battlefield before Laṅkā, a war-weary and anxious Rāma faces Rāvaṇa advancing for the climactic duel _(actors: Rāma, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/aditya-hridayam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa 105.1–4)
- **Rāma dissolves the Setu with his bow-tip at Dhanuṣkoḍi** — After the war, at Vibhīṣaṇa's request so the causeway could not be reused for invasion, Rāma touches the tip of his bow (dhanuṣ-koḍi) to the Setu to dissolve it, naming the southernmost headland of Pamban Island _(actors: Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/rameswaram-setu-bandha.md) — (Rāmanātha sthala-purāṇa; Sethu Purāṇa (Tamil tradition))
- **Rāma exhausted on the battlefield** — After a punishing day of war, Rāma stands worn out and anxious before the undefeated Rāvaṇa for the final duel _(actors: Rāma, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/aditya-hridayam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 105.1)
- **Rāma reaches Śṛṅgaverapura; Guha welcomes him** — On the first stage of exile Rāma arrives at the Niṣāda town on the Gaṅgā and Guha, chief of the Niṣādas and Rāma's friend, comes out with gifts and offers his kingdom _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Guha (Niṣāda king))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sringaverapura-guha-ganga-crossing.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 50; Rāmcaritmānas, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa)
- **Rāma singles out the Māṇḍūkya for Hanumān** — In the Muktikā dialogue Rāma instructs Hanumān on a graded path of Upaniṣadic study, declaring 'the Māṇḍūkya alone is enough for the liberation of the seeker.' _(actors: Rāma, Hanumān)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mandukya-upanishad.md) — (Muktikā Upaniṣad 1.26–29)
- **Rāma threatens the ocean and Setu is built** — When the sea-lord refuses passage to Laṅkā, Rāma readies the brahmāstra; Varuṇa appears, submits, and advises building Rāma Setu with Nala's help _(actors: Rāma, Varuṇa/Samudra, Nala)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/varuna.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Rāvaṇa's digvijaya reaches Ayodhyā** — In his world-conquest Rāvaṇa marches against the Solar kings and comes to Anaraṇya, reigning Ikṣvāku sovereign of Ayodhyā _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Anaraṇya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/anaranya-ravana-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 19 (within 18–23))
- **Satyavrata commits the three sins** — As a wild prince Satyavrata angers his father, abducts a bride, and kills and eats Vasishtha's sacred cow, for which Vasishtha curses and names him Trishanku _(actors: Satyavrata, Trayyaruna, Vasishtha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trishanku.md) — (Harivamsha; Puranic)
- **Slander of Sītā in Ayodhyā** — A washerman's grumble about taking back a wife who lived in another man's house becomes public censure (loka-apavāda) that Rāma the king cannot ignore _(actors: Rāma's spies, citizens, the washerman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttara-ramayana-lava-kusha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa 43-45)
- **Slaying of Virādha** — The rākṣasa Virādha seizes Sītā; the brothers bury him alive, and dying he reverts to the gandharva Tumburu, released by Rāma's touch _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Virādha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/3-aranya-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya Kāṇḍa 2–4)
- **Sītā's abduction and Rāma's grief (frame)** — After Rāvaṇa carries off Sītā, Rāma wanders the Daṇḍaka forest in despair, the crisis that occasions the Gītā _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shiva-gita.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Śiva-Gītā 1; cf. Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya Kāṇḍa)
- **Sītā's earth-birth in the furrow of Mithilā** — King Janaka, ploughing the sacrificial field, lifts an infant girl (Sītā) from the furrow and takes her as his daughter; she is ayonijā, born of Earth _(actors: Janaka (Sīradhvaja), Sītā (Jānakī, Maithilī), Bhūmi (Earth))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/janakpur-mithila-sita-janmabhumi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 66; Adhyātma Rāmāyaṇa (Lakṣmī variant); Adbhuta Rāmāyaṇa & Jaina tellings (Rāvaṇa's-daughter variant))
- **The fourfold Mithilā wedding** — All four princes of Ayodhyā wed on a single day at Mithilā: Sītā–Rāma, Ūrmilā–Lakṣmaṇa, Māṇḍavī–Bharata, and Śrutakīrti–Śatrughna, the latter two being Kuśadhvaja's daughters _(actors: Bharata, Śatrughna, Māṇḍavī, Śrutakīrti, Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Ūrmilā, Janaka, Kuśadhvaja, Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bharata-shatrughna-and-their-wives.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 71–73)
- **The wager over Hariścandra's truthfulness** — Vasiṣṭha praises Hariścandra as the most truthful king; Viśvāmitra disputes it and undertakes to break him, with the king as the stake _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, Hariścandra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hariscandra.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 7; Devī Bhāgavata Purāṇa 7)
- **Trijaṭā among the Aśoka-vana guard** — Trijaṭā is set among the rākṣasīs guarding the captive Sītā in Rāvaṇa's Aśoka grove in Laṅkā _(actors: Trijaṭā, Sītā, Rāvaṇa, guard rākṣasīs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/trijata.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Sundara Kāṇḍa)
- **Trishanku's three sins and curse-naming** — Prince Satyavrata angers his father, abducts a bride, and kills Vasiṣṭha's cow, earning the curse-name Triśaṅku from the sage _(actors: Satyavrata/Triśaṅku, Vasiṣṭha, Trayyāruṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/trishanku.md) — (Harivaṃśa; Purāṇas)
- **Urvaśī weds Purūravas under three conditions** — The apsarā Urvaśī marries the first Lunar king Purūravas on conditions including that she never see him naked _(actors: Purūravas, Urvaśī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/pururavas-urvashi.md) — (Ṛgveda X.95; Śatapatha Brāhmaṇa XI.5.1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.6)
- **Vamana avatara & subduing of Bali** — Vishnu as a dwarf brahmana begs three paces from asura-king Bali, grows cosmic (Trivikrama), and pushes Bali to Patala _(actors: Vamana/Vishnu, Bali, Kashyapa, Aditi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana, Vishnu Purana, Vamana Purana)
- **Vamana Subdues Bali (Boon of Future Indra-hood)** — Vishnu as Vamana reclaims the three worlds from the daitya king Bali in three strides, pushing him to Patala/Sutala but granting that Bali will become Indra in the future Savarni manvantara as recompense for his truthfulness _(actors: Vishnu; Vamana; Bali; Virochana)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-08-savarni.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.2; Bhagavata Purana 8.13.15, 8.22-23)
- **Vamana subdues Bali (Trivikrama)** — Vishnu, born as the dwarf brahmana Vamana, begs three paces of land from the asura-king Bali, then grows cosmic (Trivikrama), covers earth and heaven in two strides, and sets his third foot on Bali's head pushing him to rule Patala _(actors: Vamana/Vishnu, Bali, Kashyapa, Aditi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23; Vishnu Purana; Vamana Purana)
- **Varuṇa grants Hariścandra a son to be sacrificed** — Counselled by Nārada, the sonless Hariścandra prays to Varuṇa, who grants him a son, Rohita, on condition the boy be sacrificed back to Varuṇa _(actors: Hariścandra, Varuṇa, Nārada, Rohita)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hariscandra.md) — (Aitareya Brāhmaṇa 7.13–14)
- **Vibhīṣaṇa defects to Rāma** — Spurned by Rāvaṇa for urging Sītā's return, Vibhīṣaṇa surrenders to Rāma, who rules that a refuge-seeker must never be turned away and pre-crowns him king of Laṅkā _(actors: Vibhīṣaṇa, Rāma, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 17–19)
- **Vibhīṣaṇa's tapas and boon of righteousness** — In joint austerities at Gokarṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa alone asks that his mind never stray from dharma; pleased, Brahmā additionally grants him immortality _(actors: Vibhīṣaṇa, Brahmā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vibhishana.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Vibhandaka sheds his seed and the doe conceives Rishyashringa** — The ascetic Vibhandaka, overcome at a lake, involuntarily sheds his seed; a doe (a cursed apsaras) drinks it and conceives, bearing a boy and being freed of her curse _(actors: Vibhandaka, the doe-apsaras, Urvashi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishyashringa.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana-parva ~110)
- **Virādha seizes Sītā in Daṇḍaka** — On entering the Daṇḍaka forest, the man-eating rākṣasa Virādha takes up Sītā in his arms — the first abduction-attempt of the epic _(actors: Virādha, Sītā, Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/viradha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 2)
- **Vālmīki composes the first śloka** — Grief at seeing a hunter kill a krauñca bird bursts from Vālmīki as the first anuṣṭubh verse (śoka becoming śloka), birthing Sanskrit poetry _(actors: Vālmīki)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Vālmīki witnesses the krauñca bird's death and utters the first śloka** — Grieving a hunter's killing of a mating curlew, Vālmīki's sorrow bursts out as metrical verse, birthing the anuṣṭubh meter and poetry itself _(actors: Vālmīki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 2)
- **Vānara host reaches the Setu-kshetra bridgehead** — Rāma marches the vānara army to the Pamban/Dhanuṣkoṭi shore opposite Laṅkā and petitions the ocean-god Sāgara for passage _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Sugrīva, the vānara host, Sāgara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/rameswaram-setu-bandha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 19–22)
- **Vāyu fathers Hanumān upon Añjanā** — Vāyu fathers Hanumān upon the apsarā-turned-vānarī Añjanā by his wind-agency, making Hanumān Vāyuputra/Pavanaputra _(actors: Vāyu, Añjanā, Hanumān)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vayu.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Kiṣkindhā 66, Uttara 35-36)
- **Aditi's Payovrata** — Grieving for her dispossessed sons, Aditi performs the twelve-day Payovrata milk-vow on Kaśyapa's instruction; Viṣṇu promises to be born as her son _(actors: Aditi, Kaśyapa, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vamana-bali.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 8.16–8.17)
- **Agastya approaches and offers the secret** — The sage Agastya, watching the war among the devas, steps forward and offers Rāma an eternal secret for victory _(actors: Agastya, Rāma, the devas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/aditya-hridayam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 105.2-3)
- **Agastya approaches Rāma** — The sage Agastya, present among the watching gods, draws near and offers Rāma an eternal secret _(actors: Agastya, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/aditya-hridayam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha-kāṇḍa 105.1)
- **Agastya prescribes the Pāśupata vow** — Sage Agastya comes to the grieving Rāma and prescribes the Pāśupata vrata and worship of Śiva as the means to recover Sītā _(actors: Agastya, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shiva-gita.md) — (Padma Purāṇa, Śiva-Gītā 1–2)
- **A lifetime of waiting at Pampā** — Śabarī keeps the empty āśram ready and gathers fruit day after day for years, watching the road for the promised prince _(actors: Śabarī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shabari.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Araṇya-kāṇḍa 74; bhakti tradition)
- **Anaraṇya gives battle** — Unlike kings who submitted, Anaraṇya accepts battle to defend Ayodhyā and the honor of the Ikṣvāku line _(actors: Anaraṇya, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/anaranya-ravana-curse.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Uttara Kāṇḍa 19)
- **Śarabhaṅga's self-immolation** — Having gained Rāma's darśana, the sage Śarabhaṅga enters the fire and ascends in a radiant body to Brahmaloka _(actors: Śarabhaṅga, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/3-aranya-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya Kāṇḍa 5)
- **Arrival of Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa at Mithilā under Viśvāmitra** — Viśvāmitra escorts Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa to Janaka's court, where they are received by Janaka and his priest Śatānanda, and Viśvāmitra asks that the boys be shown Śiva's bow _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Viśvāmitra, Janaka, Śatānanda)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/janakpur-mithila-sita-janmabhumi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla-kāṇḍa 66)
- **Avatara of Mayureshvara** — Ganesha descends in Treta Yuga as the peacock-mounted Mayureshvara and slays the demon Sindhu(rasura); his Morgaon form heads the Ashtavinayaka shrines _(actors: Ganesha (Mayureshvara), Sindhurasura)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/ganesha-and-mudgala-upapuranas.md) — (Ganesha Purana (Krida-khanda))
- **Bharadvāja's miraculous feast for Bharata's army** — Bharata, marching with his army to bring Rāma back, halts at Bharadvāja's āśrama; the sage by ascetic power conjures a vast miraculous feast — divine food, palaces, music and apsaras — entertaining the whole host before Bharata proceeds to Chitrakūṭa _(actors: Bharadvāja, Bharata)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/prayagraj-triveni-sangam.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa sarga ~91)
- **Birth of Bharata** — Kaikeyī bears Bharata from her share of the sacrificial pāyasa _(actors: Kaikeyī, Bharata, Daśaratha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kaikeyi.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla 16–18)
- **Birth of Kauśika (Viśvāmitra), Gādhi's son** — Gādhi's son Kauśika, born a kṣatriya prince, renounces kingship and rises by tapas to brahmarṣi status as Viśvāmitra _(actors: Gādhi, Kauśika/Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/gadhi-and-the-caru-swap.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Mahābhārata Ādi & Vana Parva)
- **Birth of Rāma at Ayodhyā** — Rama, the seventh avatar of Vishnu, is born at Ayodhya on the Sarayu in the Treta Yuga _(actors: Rama)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sapta-puri-and-sacred-cities.md) — (Garuda Purana; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Birth of the horned Rishyashringa** — Because of his doe-mother the child is born with a single horn on his forehead, hence Rishyashringa, and is raised in total forest isolation ignorant of women _(actors: Rishyashringa, Vibhandaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishyashringa.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana-parva ~110-111)
- **Brahma Commissions the Ramayana** — Brahma appears to Valmiki and commissions him to compose the story of Rama, establishing the adi-kavya (first poem) _(actors: Brahma, Valmiki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/README.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Bala Kanda 2)
- **Brahmā commissions Vālmīki to compose the Rāmāyaṇa** — Brahmā commands Vālmīki to compose Rāma's life in the new meter, granting divine insight into every event _(actors: Brahmā, Vālmīki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 2)
- **Brahmā creates the Fifth Veda from the four Vedas** — Brahmā draws recitation from Ṛg, song from Sāma, abhinaya from Yajus, and rasa from Atharva to form the Nāṭyaveda _(actors: Brahmā)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/natya-shastra-and-the-classical-arts.md) — (Nāṭya Śāstra 1.17–1.18)
- **Brahmā gives Ahalyā to Gautama in marriage** — Brahmā fashions Ahalyā as the most beautiful woman and awards her to Gautama (in a variant, via a contest to circle the worlds that Gautama wins over Indra), seeding Indra's resentment _(actors: Brahmā, Ahalyā, Gautama, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ahalya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 48; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **Building of the Setu (Rāma-Setu)** — After Rāma's penance compels the ocean-god Sāgara, the vānara Nala directs the building of a hundred-yojana floating causeway in five days, and the army crosses to Laṅkā _(actors: Rāma, Nala, Sāgara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa 21–22)
- **Courtesans lure Ṛśyaśṛṅga to end Aṅga's drought** — King Lomapāda sends courtesans disguised as ascetics to lure the chaste sage to Aṅga; his arrival breaks the years-long drought with rain _(actors: Ṛśyaśṛṅga, Lomapāda, the courtesans, Indra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rishyashringa.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva ~111-112)
- **Descent of Vishnu as Rama** — In the standard avatar-to-yuga mapping of this Mahayuga, Vishnu descends as Rama in the Treta Yuga _(actors: Vishnu; Rama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3; Valmiki Ramayana)
- **Dilīpa's cow-service to Nandinī** — As penance Dilīpa devotedly tends Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Nandinī, grazing and guarding her by day _(actors: Dilīpa, Sudakṣiṇā, Nandinī, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/raghuvamsha-kalidasa-kings.md) — (Raghuvaṃśa 1.56–95, 2.1–9)
- **Forester's vow and Lakṣmaṇa's night-watch** — Rāma declines cooked food and beds, taking only water and fodder; Lakṣmaṇa keeps vigil with Guha through the first night by the sleeping Rāma and Sītā _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Guha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sringaverapura-guha-ganga-crossing.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa 50–52)
- **Gālava's Horses and Mādhavī's Loaning** — Pressed for 800 special horses as guru-dakṣiṇā, Gālava loans Yayāti's daughter Mādhavī to three kings and Viśvāmitra to earn sons and horses, the debt finally closed by Garuḍa _(actors: Gālava, Viśvāmitra, Mādhavī, Yayāti, Aṣṭaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/minor-upakhyanas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva 105-121)
- **Gārgī's first questioning — the warp-and-woof chain** — Gārgī Vācaknavī asks on what each cosmic level is woven 'warp and woof', driving Yājñavalkya up a regress from water through air, sun, moon, stars, the gods, Indra and Prajāpati to the worlds of Brahman _(actors: Gārgī Vācaknavī, Yājñavalkya)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/gargi-and-maitreyi.md) — (Bṛhadāraṇyaka Upaniṣad 3.6)
- **Hanumān passes Maināka and outwits Surasā** — On the crossing Hanumān courteously refuses the rest offered by the golden mountain Maināka and outwits the nāga-mother Surasā's mouth-test of strength and wit _(actors: Hanumān, Maināka, Surasā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/5-sundara-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Sundara Kāṇḍa 1)
- **Hanumān's leap from Mahendragiri to Laṅkā** — From the summit of Mahendra(giri) Hanumān makes his great ocean-leap to Laṅkā, treading the peak down under the force of his spring at the opening of the Sundara-kāṇḍa _(actors: Hanumān)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/meru-kailash-and-cosmic-mountains.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa (Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa, Sundara-kāṇḍa))
- **Hariścandra surrenders his kingdom** — To appease Viśvāmitra, Hariścandra gives away Ayodhyā and all its wealth, keeping only his wife, son, and bark-cloth, then owes a further gold dakṣiṇā _(actors: Hariścandra, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/hariscandra.md) — (Mārkaṇḍeya Purāṇa 7-8)
- **Hariscandra's vow to Varuna for a son** — Childless Ikshvaku king Hariscandra, counselled by Narada, prays to Varuna for a son and vows to sacrifice the boy back; Rohita is born _(actors: Hariscandra, Narada, Varuna, Rohita)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/vedas/brahmanas/aitareya-brahmana.md) — (Aitareya Brahmana 7.13)
- **Harishchandra defers the sacrifice and Varuna curses him with dropsy** — Harishchandra repeatedly postpones offering Rohita; for the broken vow Varuna seizes him with dropsy, and the grown Rohita flees to the forest _(actors: Harishchandra, Varuna, Rohita)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sunahshepa.md) — (Aitareya Brahmana 7.14)
- **Indra strikes the infant Hanuman's jaw** — Mistaking the sun for a fruit, infant Hanuman leaps to swallow it; Indra strikes him with the vajra, breaking his jaw and giving him his name _(actors: Hanuman, Indra, the sun)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/hanuman.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda; Ramcharitmanas)
- **Śiva presses the mountain down** — Śiva pins Rāvaṇa beneath Kailāsa with the toe of His foot, crushing his arms _(actors: Śiva, Pārvatī, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shiva-tandava-stotra.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttarakāṇḍa)
- **Jamadagni's marriage to Reṇukā** — Jamadagni weds Reṇukā, daughter of King Prasenajit/Reṇu, a model pativratā whose yogic merit lets her carry water in unbaked clay _(actors: Jamadagni, Reṇukā, Prasenajit/Reṇu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/jamadagni-parashurama.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa)
- **Kabandha seizes Rāma and Lakṣmaṇa** — Searching south after Jaṭāyu's death, the brothers are caught one in each of Kabandha's yojana-long arms and drawn toward his belly-mouth _(actors: Kabandha, Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kabandha.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Araṇya-kāṇḍa 69)
- **Kaikeyī's boons and Bharata's absence** — While Bharata and Śatrughna are away in Kekaya, Kaikeyī (prompted by Mantharā) extracts the boons exiling Rāma and crowning Bharata; the brothers return to find Daśaratha dead _(actors: Kaikeyī, Mantharā, Bharata, Śatrughna, Daśaratha, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bharata-shatrughna-and-their-wives.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Ayodhyā-kāṇḍa)
- **Kapila's Wrath Burns Sagara's Sons** — Sage Kapila's wrath burns Sagara's 60,000 sons to ash, the catastrophe that prompts the eventual descent of Gaṅgā to redeem them; his ashrama tradition is localized at Haridwar _(actors: Kapila, sons of Sagara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/haridwar-rishikesh-ganga-dwara.md) — (Wikipedia, Haridwar)
- **Kausalyā receives the foremost half of the pāyasa** — Daśaratha gives the senior queen Kausalyā a full half of the divine pāyasa, from which Rāma is conceived _(actors: Daśaratha, Kausalyā, Sumitrā, Kaikeyī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kausalya.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 16)
- **Kāmadhenu at the hermitage** — Jamadagni's āśrama holds the wish-cow Kāmadhenu (Suśīlā/Surabhi) who furnishes endless hospitality _(actors: Jamadagni, Kāmadhenu)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/parashurama.md) — (Mahābhārata 3.116; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15)
