- **Indrajit's illusory slaying of Sītā** — To break morale Indrajit conjures a phantom Sītā and beheads 'her' before the vānaras; Rāma collapses in grief until Vibhīṣaṇa exposes the illusion as cover for the Nikumbhilā yajña _(actors: Indrajit, Hanumān, Rāma, Vibhīṣaṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/indrajit-meghnad.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Parasurama clears the kṣatriyas twenty-one times** — The warrior-brahmana avatara Parasurama rids the earth of the kṣatriya class twenty-one times _(actors: Parasurama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9)
- **Rama Teaches the Rama-Hridaya to Hanuman** — In the inset Rama-Hridaya ('Heart of Rama'), Hanuman is taught Rama's true Brahman-nature _(actors: Rama, Hanuman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/adhyatma-ramayana.md) — (Adhyatma Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
- **Rāma slays Kumbhakarṇa** — Rāma severs Kumbhakarṇa's arms and legs with celestial astras and finally decapitates the giant with the supreme Indra-astra; his death breaks Rāvaṇa, marking the turn toward his own end _(actors: Rāma, Kumbhakarṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kumbhakarna.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa ch. 67-68)
- **Vamana's Three Steps and Bali's Surrender** — The dwarf-avatara Vamana measures the cosmos in three steps and Bali surrenders himself, ceding his sovereignty _(actors: Vamana, Bali)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23)
- **Hanuman finds Sita in the Ashoka grove** — Hanuman finds Sita in the Ashoka-vana, gives Rama's ring as proof, and receives her crest-jewel (chudamani) as a return token _(actors: Hanuman, Sita, Ravana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/5-sundara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Sundara Kanda))
- **Kanyakumari Consecrated by Parashurama** — Consecration of the Kanyakumari shrine at the subcontinent's southern tip is attributed to Parashurama _(actors: Parashurama)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Skanda Purana)
- **Kumbha and Nikumbha die in the war** — Kumbhakarṇa's sons Kumbha and Nikumbha fight and die against Rāma's forces in the Laṅkā war _(actors: Kumbha, Nikumbha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kumbhakarna.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Rama Teaches the Rama-Gita to Lakshmana** — After the coronation Rama instructs Lakshmana in pure Advaita Vedanta in the inset Rama-Gita, modelled on the Bhagavad-Gita _(actors: Rama, Lakshmana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/adhyatma-ramayana.md) — (Adhyatma Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
- **Setu-bandha (building the bridge to Lanka)** — The vanaras led by Nala build a causeway to Lanka over the ocean, which yields after Rama threatens it with arrows _(actors: Rama, Nala, the vanaras)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Sītā's earth-birth from the furrow** — Janaka relates that Sītā was found ayonijā in the ploughed sacrificial field, a daughter of the Earth _(actors: Janaka, Sītā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 66)
- **The Nikumbhilā sacrifice interrupted** — Guided by Vibhīṣaṇa, Lakṣmaṇa and Hanumān break into the Nikumbhilā grove and shatter Indrajit's sacrifice before the chariot manifests, denying him invulnerability _(actors: Lakṣmaṇa, Vibhīṣaṇa, Hanumān, Indrajit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/indrajit-meghnad.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Burning of Lanka** — Captured by Indrajit's Brahmastra and his tail set alight, Hanuman breaks free and torches the golden city of Lanka _(actors: Hanuman, Indrajit, Ravana, Vibhishana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/5-sundara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Sundara Kanda))
- **Lakṣmaṇa slays Indrajit with the Aindrāstra** — In the final duel Lakṣmaṇa beheads Indrajit with the Aindrāstra, the weapon of the very god Indra the rākṣasa had once conquered, breaking the back of the rākṣasa army _(actors: Lakṣmaṇa, Indrajit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/indrajit-meghnad.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Rāma breaks the bow of Śiva and wins Sītā** — At Mithilā Rāma lifts and strings Janaka's colossal Śiva-bow (Pināka), snapping it with a thunderclap, and so wins Sītā by the bride-price of valour _(actors: Rāma, Janaka, Sītā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 66–67)
- **Vibhishana defects to Rama** — Ravana's righteous brother Vibhishana joins Rama after counselling Ravana in vain to return Sita _(actors: Vibhishana, Rama, Ravana)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Deaths of Kumbhakarna and Indrajit; Lakshmana revived** — In the great battle Kumbhakarna and Indrajit/Meghanada fall, and Lakshmana, felled by Indrajit's weapon, is revived when Hanuman fetches the Sanjivani herb by carrying the whole Dronagiri mountain _(actors: Kumbhakarna, Indrajit, Lakshmana, Hanuman)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Saubhari Weds Mandhata's Fifty Daughters** — The sage Saubhari, disturbed by mating fish, multiplies his body to wed all fifty daughters of King Mandhata, then renounces everything _(actors: Saubhari, Mandhata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.6)
- **Sulocanā becomes satī on Indrajit's pyre** — In later tradition Indrajit's wife Sulocanā, daughter of Śeṣa-nāga, becomes satī on his funeral pyre, celebrated as a model pativratā _(actors: Sulocanā, Indrajit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/indrajit-meghnad.md) — (Rāmacaritamānasa; regional Rāmāyaṇas)
- **The four-fold marriage at Mithilā** — Rāma weds Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa weds Ūrmilā, and Bharata and Śatrughna wed Kuśadhvaja's daughters Māṇḍavī and Śrutakīrti in a quadruple fire-wedding _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Lakṣmaṇa, Bharata, Śatrughna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 73)
- **Vibhishana's defection (sharanagati)** — Spurned by Ravana, his righteous brother Vibhishana surrenders to Rama, who accepts him and pre-crowns him king of Lanka _(actors: Vibhishana, Rama, Ravana, Sugriva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Building of the bridge (Nala-Setu / Rama-Setu)** — Under Nala's direction the vanaras build a 100-yojana causeway across the ocean, and the army crosses to Lanka _(actors: Rama, Nala, Sagara, vanaras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Paraśurāma confronts Rāma and yields his power** — The wrathful Paraśurāma challenges Rāma with Viṣṇu's Śārṅga bow; Rāma strings it, Paraśurāma recognizes him as Viṣṇu, surrenders his tapas, and withdraws _(actors: Paraśurāma, Rāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/1-bala-kanda.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa 74–76)
- **Rama slays Ravana** — Rama kills the ten-headed Lanka-king Ravana with the Brahmastra, preceded by the Aditya-hridaya hymn taught by Agastya _(actors: Rama, Ravana, Agastya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Trishanku Hung Between Worlds** — King Trishanku seeks heaven in his mortal body and is left suspended between earth and sky _(actors: Trishanku)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.7)
- **Death of Kumbhakarna** — Ravana's colossal sleeping brother Kumbhakarna is roused, rampages through the vanaras, and is dismembered and beheaded by Rama _(actors: Kumbhakarna, Rama, Ravana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Sagara's Sons Burnt and the Descent of Ganga** — Sagara's 60,000 sons are burnt to ash by Kapila's glance, and Bhagiratha's tapas brings Ganga down to liberate their ashes _(actors: Sagara, Kapila, Bhagiratha, Ganga)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.8-9)
- **Sita's fire ordeal (Agni-pariksha)** — Sita proves her chastity by entering fire, and Agni returns her unharmed _(actors: Sita, Agni, Rama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Agastya Releases the Kaveri** — In a famine, the gods via Ganesha as a crow tip Agastya's water-pot so the maiden Kaveri flows out to relieve the drought, becoming the life-river of Tamil country _(actors: Agastya, Kaveri, Ganesha)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/yamuna-and-river-goddesses.md) — (Skanda Purana, Kaveri-mahatmya; Tamil tradition)
- **Khatvanga's Liberation in One Muhurta** — King Khatvanga, granted a single muhurta of life on returning from aiding the devas, attains liberation in that hour by total surrender _(actors: Khatvanga)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.9)
- **Kārtavīrya steals Kāmadhenu from Jamadagni** — Kārtavīrya Arjuna's theft of the wish-cow Kāmadhenu from the sage Jamadagni triggers Paraśurāma's vengeance _(actors: Kārtavīrya Arjuna, Jamadagni, Paraśurāma)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Kamadhenu (Wikipedia))
- **Rama's return and coronation (Rama-rajya)** — Rama flies home in the Pushpaka-vimana and is crowned at Ayodhya, inaugurating the ideal reign of Rama-rajya, later celebrated as Dipavali/Vijayadashami _(actors: Rama, Sita)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Yuddha Kanda)
- **Sanjivani herb & revival of Lakshmana** — Lakshmana felled by Indrajit's/Ravana's weapons is revived when Hanuman fetches the Sanjivani herb, carrying the whole Dronagiri mountain _(actors: Hanuman, Lakshmana, Jambavan, Sushena)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Indrajit slain by Lakshmana** — Guided by Vibhishana, Lakshmana disrupts the Nikumbhila sacrifice and beheads Indrajit (Meghanada) with the Aindrastra _(actors: Lakshmana, Indrajit, Vibhishana, Hanuman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Rāvaṇa wins the Ātma-liṅga and is tricked at Gokarṇa** — Rāvaṇa wins Śiva's Ātma-liṅga by tapas on condition it never touch ground before Laṅkā; Gaṇeśa as a cowherd-boy and Vishnu's false dusk make him set it down at Gokarṇa, where it roots immovably as Mahābaleśvara, and the hurled wrappings spring up as the Sajjeśvara, Dhāreśvara, Guṇavanteśvara and Mūrudeśvara liṅgas _(actors: Rāvaṇa; Śiva; Gaṇeśa; Vishnu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Gokarṇa-māhātmya (Skanda Purāṇa, Sahyādri-khaṇḍa))
- **Sampāti reveals Sītā's location in Laṅkā** — Hearing the mourning vānaras name his dead brother, the wingless Sampāti descends and, with his far-sight, declares Sītā held across the sea in Rāvaṇa's Laṅkā in the Aśoka grove, converting a hopeless search into the ocean-leap mission _(actors: Sampāti, Aṅgada, Hanumān)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/jatayu-and-sampati.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 56-63)
- **Vasiṣṭha's brahmadaṇḍa swallows Viśvāmitra's Brahmāstra** — Vasiṣṭha's defensive brahmadaṇḍa absorbs the Brahmāstra hurled by king Viśvāmitra, the humiliation that turns the warrior-king toward brahminhood _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa, Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Lava-Kusha and the Ashvamedha** — Lava and Kusha, taught the Ramayana by Valmiki, recite it at Rama's horse-sacrifice and capture the sacrificial horse, confronting their father _(actors: Lava, Kusha, Rama, Valmiki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
- **Nandinī conjures armies against Viśvāmitra** — When king Viśvāmitra (then Kauśika) tries to seize Vasiṣṭha's wish-cow Nandinī, she conjures whole armies (Pahlavas, Śakas, Yavanas, Kāmbojas) to rout him, setting him on the path to brahmin-hood _(actors: Nandinī, Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa; Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Niśākara's prophecy and Sampāti's wings restored** — Fulfilling the sage Niśākara's prophecy that telling the vānaras of Sītā would be his great deed, Sampāti's feathers sprout and his wings regrow after he serves Rāma's cause, and he flies off rejoicing _(actors: Sampāti, Niśākara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/jatayu-and-sampati.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Kiṣkindhā-kāṇḍa 60-63)
- **Parashurama Clears the Earth of Kshatriyas** — The Bhrigu avatara Parashurama clears the earth of kshatriyas twenty-one times in the Kartavirya/Jamadagni cycle _(actors: Parashurama, Kartavirya, Jamadagni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 9.15-16)
- **Rāma marks the Setu's start at Dhanuṣkoḍi** — At the south-eastern sandspit of Rāmeśvaram island Rāma marks the start of the Nala-setu to Laṅkā with the tip (koḍi) of his bow (dhanuṣ) — and in the return-telling breaks the now-needless bridge there at Vibhīṣaṇa's request — giving Dhanuṣkoḍi its name and its sankalpa-snāna tīrtha and Kodaṇḍarāma shrine _(actors: Rāma; Vibhīṣaṇa; Hanumān; Sītā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa; Skanda Purāṇa (Setu-māhātmya))
- **Slaying of Ravana** — Renewed by the Aditya-Hridayam, Rama looses the Brahmastra into Ravana's navel, drying the amrita that sustained him and killing the ten-headed king _(actors: Rama, Ravana, Matali, Agastya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Agni-pariksha (fire ordeal)** — Sita enters fire to prove her chastity; Agni rises bearing her unharmed and testifies to her purity _(actors: Sita, Rama, Agni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Bharata enthrones Rāma's pādukās to rule Ayodhyā** — Bharata enthrones Rāma's sacred sandals (pādukās) to rule Ayodhyā in his stead during Rāma's exile, an emblem of surrender at the lotus-feet _(actors: Bharata, Rāma)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-symbols-and-emblems.md) — (Knowledge of India; Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Rama's departure into the Sarayu** — Rama renounces the world and walks into the Sarayu river to return to Vaikuntha as Vishnu, ending the avatar _(actors: Rama)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
- **Return to Ayodhya & coronation (Rama-rajya)** — Rama flies home in the Pushpaka-vimana, reunites with Bharata, and is crowned king, inaugurating the ideal reign of Rama-rajya _(actors: Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Bharata, Hanuman, Vibhishana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/6-yuddha-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Yuddha Kanda))
- **Treta Yuga — the Age of Three-Quarter Dharma** — Dharma declines by one leg; sacrifice (yajna), kingship, agriculture, and the first wars arise, with humans living ~10,000 years _(actors: humanity, Rama)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 1.3, Bhagavata Purana 12.3)
- **Descent of the Ganga (Gangavatarana)** — King Bhagiratha does immense penance to bring the celestial Ganga down to liberate the ashes of Sagara's 60,000 sons; Shiva breaks the river's fall in his hair and Ganga flows to Patala to redeem the ancestors, earning the epithet Bhagirathi _(actors: Bhagiratha, Ganga, Shiva, Sagara, Kapila)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Ramayana Bala Kanda; Vishnu Purana; Bhagavata Purana 9.8-9; Mahabharata)
- **Rise of Ravana & Brahma's boon** — The rakshasa brothers do great tapas; Ravana wins invulnerability to all beings except men and monkeys, seizes Lanka from Kubera, and conquers the three worlds _(actors: Ravana, Kumbhakarna, Vibhishana, Brahma, Kubera)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Valmiki composes the Rāmāyaṇa** — The adi-kavi Valmiki composes the Rāmāyaṇa, the chronicle of Rāma's exile, Sītā's abduction, the war in Laṅkā and the return to Ayodhyā _(actors: Valmiki)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/README.md) — (Ramayana (Valmiki); Itihasa (Wikipedia))
- **Ahalya Cursed to Stone and Redeemed by Rama** — Gautama's wife Ahalya is cursed to stone and redeemed by the touch of Rama, linking the sage-line Gautama to the Solar epic _(actors: Ahalya, Gautama, Rama)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Ramayana Bala Kanda)
- **Harishchandra's trial of truth** — The Ikshvaku king Harishchandra, to honor a debt to sage Vishvamitra, surrenders his kingdom, sells his wife and son, and becomes a chandala's servant at the cremation ground; his unbroken truthfulness restores all and elevates him to heaven _(actors: Harishchandra, Vishvamitra, Shaivya, Rohitashva)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/02-treta-yuga.md) — (Markandeya Purana; Aitareya Brahmana; Devi Bhagavata)
- **Śiva gifts the Chandrahāsa sword to Rāvaṇa** — Śiva gifts his curved sword Chandrahāsa to Rāvaṇa for his devotion; it returns to harm the wielder if used unjustly _(actors: Śiva, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divyastras-and-divine-weapons.md) — (Astra (weapon) (Wikipedia))
- **Kārtavīrya Arjuna's sons slay Jamadagni** — The sons of Kārtavīrya Arjuna slay the sage Jamadagni over the wish-cow Kāmadhenu, triggering Paraśurāma's vengeance _(actors: Jamadagni, Kārtavīrya Arjuna)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15–16; Mahābhārata)
- **Vedavati's curse (reborn as Sita)** — Ravana molests the chaste ascetic Vedavati, who immolates herself vowing to be reborn as the cause of his death, i.e. as Sita _(actors: Ravana, Vedavati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Banishment of Sita** — A washerman's slander prompts Rama to exile the pregnant Sita to Valmiki's hermitage, where she bears twins Lava and Kusha _(actors: Rama, Sita, Lakshmana, Valmiki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Jaṭāyu fights Rāvaṇa and dies telling Rāma of Sītā** — The vulture-king Jaṭāyu fights Rāvaṇa to save the abducted Sītā, has his wings severed, and dies telling Rāma the direction of her captor; Rāma performs his funeral rites as for a father _(actors: Jaṭāyu, Rāvaṇa, Sītā, Rāma)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Paraśurāma clears the earth of kṣatriyas 21 times** — The axe-bearing 6th avatāra of Viṣṇu, Paraśurāma, avenges his father by clearing the earth of corrupt kṣatriyas 21 times and reclaims Konkan/Kerala from the sea _(actors: Paraśurāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 9.15–16; Mahābhārata)
- **Vishvamitra Becomes Brahmarshi** — Born a Kshatriya king Kaushika, Vishvamitra earns brahmarshi status, tests Harishchandra, and trains Rama and Lakshmana, bridging Kshatriya and Brahmana lines _(actors: Vishvamitra)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Ramayana; Mahabharata)
- **Lava-Kusha & the Ashvamedha** — Vālmīki teaches the Rāmāyaṇa to Sita's twins Lava and Kusha, who recite it at Rama's horse-sacrifice and are revealed as his sons _(actors: Lava, Kusha, Valmiki, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Hanumān leaps the ocean to Laṅkā and finds Sītā** — Hanumān, son of Vāyu and partial aṃśa of Śiva, leaps the ocean to Laṅkā and finds the captive Sītā, in supreme devotion to Rāma _(actors: Hanumān, Sītā, Rāma)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Killing of Shambuka** — Rama beheads the shudra ascetic Shambuka for performing tapas forbidden to his varna in Treta, reviving a dead brahmana boy; a highly disputed passage _(actors: Rama, Shambuka, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Rāma slays Vālin and allies with Sugrīva** — Rāma slays the usurping vānara Vālin (son of Indra) with his arrow and allies with Sugrīva (son of Sūrya), restoring him as king of Kiṣkindhā _(actors: Rāma, Vālin, Sugrīva)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Sita's return to the earth** — Asked to prove her purity again, Sita calls on her mother Bhumi (Earth), who opens and receives her forever _(actors: Sita, Rama, Bhumi-Devi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Agastya presses down the Vindhya mountains** — Agastya humbles the growing Vindhya range, pressing it down and opening the southward spread of Vedic culture _(actors: Agastya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva)
- **Nala and Nīla architect Rāma's bridge to Laṅkā** — The engineer-vānaras Nala and Nīla architect the floating bridge (Setu) by which Rāma's monkey host crosses to storm Laṅkā _(actors: Nala, Nīla, Rāma, the vānaras)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Rama returns to Ayodhya (Diwali)** — Rama, Sita, and Lakshmana return to Ayodhya after fourteen years' exile; the city lights lamps to guide them, the charter of Diwali night _(actors: Rama, Sita, Lakshmana)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Ramayana, Uttara Kanda)
- **Rama's departure (Mahaprasthana)** — Rama enters the Sarayu river in jala-samadhi, resumes his form as Vishnu, and ascends to Vaikuntha; Hanuman is granted deathlessness _(actors: Rama, Lakshmana, Brahma, Hanuman, Kala)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/7-uttara-kanda.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana (Uttara Kanda))
- **Ahalya's Redemption by Rama's Touch** — In Kamban's devotional reframing, Rama's touch delivers Ahalya as an act of divine grace _(actors: Rama, Ahalya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/kamban-iramavataram.md) — (Kamban, Iramavataram, Bala Kandam)
- **Jain variant: Lakṣmaṇa slays Rāvaṇa, Rāma attains mokṣa** — In Vimalasūri's Jain Paümacariya, the non-violent Rāma (Padma) does not kill Rāvaṇa — Lakṣmaṇa does — and Rāma attains mokṣa as a Jain layman _(actors: Rāma, Lakṣmaṇa, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Paümacariya (Vimalasūri))
- **Viśvāmitra attains Brahmaṛṣi rank** — Born a kṣatriya king, Viśvāmitra forces his way to Brahmaṛṣi rank by colossal tapas, the only Saptarṣi who was not a born brahmin _(actors: Viśvāmitra)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa 51–65; Mahābhārata)
- **Hanumān carries the Sañjīvanī mountain to revive Lakṣmaṇa** — Unable to identify the resurrection-herb Sañjīvanī on Droṇagiri, Hanumān carries the whole mountain to revive the wounded Lakṣmaṇa _(actors: Hanumān, Lakṣmaṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha Kāṇḍa)
- **Kapila incinerates the sons of Sagara** — The wrathful sage Kapila's glance incinerates the 60,000 sons of Sagara in the Ganga-descent story, referenced from the Sankhya profile _(actors: Kapila, sons of Sagara)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/darshanas/samkhya-karika.md) — (Ramayana; Bhagavata Purana 9.8)
- **Viśvāmitra creates Triśaṅku's heaven** — Viśvāmitra builds a separate heaven for King Triśaṅku in his contest of tapas _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Triśaṅku)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Puṣpaka Vimāna flies Rāma home to Ayodhyā** — The self-moving flying palace Puṣpaka — made by Viśvakarmā, passing Brahmā to Kubera to the seizing Rāvaṇa — finally flies Rāma, Sītā and the army home to Ayodhyā, then is returned to Kubera _(actors: Rāma, Sītā, Viśvakarmā, Kubera, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/divine-objects-and-treasures.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa, Yuddha/Uttara Kāṇḍa; Pushpaka Vimana (Wikipedia))
- **Matali drives Indra's chariot for Rāma against Rāvaṇa** — Indra's charioteer Matali drives the celestial ratha lent to Rāma for the duel with Rāvaṇa (and later to Arjuna for his heaven-journey) _(actors: Matali, Indra, Rāma, Rāvaṇa)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/vahanas-and-celestial-vehicles.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa; Mahabharata)
- **Vasiṣṭha-Viśvāmitra cow-war and death of Vasiṣṭha's sons** — The arch-rivalry of Vasiṣṭha and Viśvāmitra over the wish-cow erupts in war, and Vasiṣṭha's hundred sons (including Śakti) are killed by Viśvāmitra's agency _(actors: Vasiṣṭha, Viśvāmitra, Śakti)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Ṛgveda; Vālmīki Rāmāyaṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **Gautama curses Ahalyā to stone** — The sage Gautama curses his wife Ahalyā (the Indra-deception myth) to become stone, later restored by Rāma's touch _(actors: Gautama, Ahalyā, Indra, Rāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/rishi-lineages-and-gotras.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Akal-bodhan — Rama's Autumn Worship of Durga** — With Chandika shielding Ravana, Brahma counsels Rama to propitiate Durga out of season in autumn; Rama performs the untimely worship from Sashthi to Dashami, the mythic charter of Sharadiya Durga Puja _(actors: Rama, Durga/Chandika, Indra, Brahma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan; Devi-Bhagavata; Kalika/Brihaddharma Purana)
- **The 108 Blue Lotuses and Rama's Eye** — Hanuman fetches 108 celestial blue lotuses for the worship; Durga hides one to test Rama, who prepares to pluck out his own lotus-eye to complete the count, whereupon Durga stays his hand and grants victory _(actors: Rama, Hanuman, Durga, Vibhishana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan)
- **Mahiravana Abducts Rama and Lakshmana; Hanuman's Patala Rescue** — The sorcerer-king Mahiravana of Patala abducts the sleeping Rama and Lakshmana; Hanuman descends to the netherworld, learns the demon's life resides in bees, and slays him to rescue them _(actors: Mahiravana, Rama, Lakshmana, Hanuman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan (folk interpolation))
- **Śeṣa incarnates as Lakṣmaṇa** — When Viṣṇu becomes Rāma, Śeṣa accompanies him as the ever-devoted younger brother Lakṣmaṇa _(actors: Śeṣa, Lakṣmaṇa, Rāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Vaiṣṇava tradition; Rāmāyaṇa commentary)
- **Martyrdom of Taranisen** — Taranisen, the Rama-devotee son of Vibhishana, fights for Ravana's side out of duty while chanting Rama's name and is slain by Rama — a poignant martyrdom motif _(actors: Taranisen, Vibhishana, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan (folk interpolation))
- **Birth of Bhagiratha from Two Co-widows** — In a Krittivasi accretion, Bhagiratha (later bringer of the Ganga to earth) is born of King Dilipa's two co-widows by divine blessing — a rare premodern parthenogenic/same-sex generation motif _(actors: Bhagiratha, two co-widows of Dilipa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/krittivasi-ramayan.md) — (Krittivasi Ramayan (late interpolation))
- **Sita Slays Sahasra-Ravana as Mahakali (Adbhuta Ramayana)** — When the thousand-headed Sahasra-Ravana of Pushkara fells Rama on the battlefield, Sita assumes the form of Mahakali and slays him, inverting hero and heroine roles _(actors: Sita/Mahakali, Sahasra-Ravana, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/adhyatma-and-variant-ramayanas.md) — (Adbhuta Ramayana)
- **Vamana pushes Bali to the netherworld (Bali Pratipada/Onam)** — Vamana, after the three-strides boon, pushes the asura-king Bali/Mahabali to Patala, who is granted one yearly return celebrated as Onam and Bali Pratipada _(actors: Vamana, Bali (Mahabali))_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Bhagavata Purana; Kerala tradition)
- **Sita Born to Mandodari (Adbhuta Ramayana)** — In the Shakta Adbhuta Ramayana, Sita — the supreme Shakti — is born to Ravana's queen Mandodari rather than discovered by Janaka _(actors: Sita, Mandodari, Ravana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/adhyatma-and-variant-ramayanas.md) — (Adbhuta Ramayana)
- **Ravana Abducts Kausalya (Ananda Ramayana)** — In the Ananda Ramayana, foretold that Kausalya's son by Dasharatha will kill him, Ravana abducts Kausalya but fails to keep her — a peripheral back-story _(actors: Ravana, Kausalya, Dasharatha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/adhyatma-and-variant-ramayanas.md) — (Ananda Ramayana)
- **Vasishtha Instructs Young Rama (Yoga-Vasishtha)** — A young, world-weary Rama is instructed by the sage Vasishtha in radical Advaita (ajatavada, non-origination) across hundreds of nested parables in the Yoga-Vasishtha _(actors: Vasishtha, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/adhyatma-and-variant-ramayanas.md) — (Yoga-Vasishtha / Vasishtha Ramayana)
- **Vamana's three strides subdue Bali** — Vishnu as the dwarf Vamana begs three paces of land from the asura king Bali, then swells to cosmic size (Trivikrama), covering earth and heaven in two strides and pushing Bali to the netherworld with the third _(actors: Vamana/Trivikrama (Vishnu), Bali)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Rig Veda 1.154; Bhagavata Purana 8.15-23; Vishnu Purana)
- **Parashurama exterminates the kshatriyas** — After King Kartavirya Arjuna steals his father Jamadagni's wish-cow and kills the sage, the axe-bearing Parashurama annihilates the tyrant and the entire kshatriya class twenty-one times over _(actors: Parashurama, Kartavirya Arjuna, Jamadagni)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva; Bhagavata Purana 9.15-16; Vishnu Purana)
- **Rama slays Ravana and recovers Sita (Ramayana)** — Rama, exiled prince of Ayodhya, allies with Hanuman and the vanaras, builds a bridge to Lanka, slays the rakshasa king Ravana, and recovers his abducted wife Sita _(actors: Rama, Sita, Ravana, Hanuman)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Valmiki Ramayana; Bhagavata Purana 9.10-11)
- **Lakshmana Kills Ravana (Jain Ramayanas)** — In the Jain tradition the Vasudeva Lakshmana, not the non-violent Baladeva Rama, slays the Prativasudeva Ravana — and consequently falls to hell, while Rama attains moksha _(actors: Lakshmana, Ravana, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/jain-and-buddhist-ramayanas.md) — (Paumacariya; Padma-purana)
- **Vali Renounces and Attains Nirvana (Paumacariya)** — In Vimalasuri's Paumacariya, after the conflict with Sugriva, Vali renounces to become a muni and attains nirvana instead of being shot dead by Rama _(actors: Vali, Sugriva, Rama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/jain-and-buddhist-ramayanas.md) — (Paumacariya)
- **Sita Born of Ravana and Mandodari, Then Abandoned (Gunabhadra/Sanghadasa)** — In the Gunabhadra and Sanghadasa Jain strands, Sita is born to Ravana and Mandodari and exposed because of a prophecy of family destruction, making Ravana's later abduction unwitting near-incest _(actors: Sita, Ravana, Mandodari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/jain-and-buddhist-ramayanas.md) — (Uttara-purana (Gunabhadra); Sanghadasa)
- **Rama Attains Kevala-jnana and Moksha (Jain ending)** — The Jain epic closes with Rama attaining omniscience (kevala-jnana) and liberation at Tungi Giri, Lakshmana and Ravana going to hell, and Sita becoming a nun and ascending to heaven _(actors: Rama, Lakshmana, Ravana, Sita)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramayana/recensions/jain-and-buddhist-ramayanas.md) — (Paumacariya; Jain tradition)
- **Rāvaṇa drives Kubera from Laṅkā** — Rāvaṇa drives his half-brother Kubera from Laṅkā and seizes his flying chariot, after which Kubera removes to Alakā in the Himālayas _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Kubera)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Rāvaṇa steals the Puṣpaka Vimāna** — Kubera's self-moving aerial chariot, a gift of Brahmā, is stolen by Rāvaṇa and later used by Rāma to return to Ayodhyā _(actors: Rāvaṇa, Kubera, Rāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa)
- **Nalakūbara curses Rāvaṇa** — Kubera's son Nalakūbara, consort of Rambhā, curses Rāvaṇa that his head will burst if he forces a woman, a curse that later protects Sītā _(actors: Nalakūbara, Rāvaṇa, Sītā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Uttara Kāṇḍa)
- **Suketu's daughter Tāḍakā born by boon and cursed by Agastya** — The yakṣa king Suketu obtains a daughter Tāḍakā by boon, who, cursed by Agastya, becomes a man-eating ogress later slain by Rāma _(actors: Suketu, Tāḍakā, Agastya, Rāma)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/yakshas-and-guhyakas.md) — (Rāmāyaṇa Bāla Kāṇḍa)
- **Birth of Rama (Rama Navami)** — Rama, the 7th dashavatara, is born to Dasharatha of Ayodhya, opening the Bala Kanda; commemorated on Chaitra Shukla Navami _(actors: Rama, Dasharatha)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Ramayana, Bala Kanda)
- **Birth of Hanuman (Hanuman Jayanti)** — Hanuman, the vanara devotee of Rama and a partial incarnation of Shiva/Vayu, is born, commemorated on Hanuman Jayanti _(actors: Hanuman)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Ramayana tradition)
- **Lakshmi ties a thread on Bali (Raksha Bandhan)** — Lakshmi, disguised as a poor woman, ties a protective thread on Bali to win back her husband Vishnu, a Raksha Bandhan charter linked to the Vamana cycle _(actors: Lakshmi, Bali, Vishnu)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Puranic)
- **Birth of Parashurama / descent of the Ganga (Akshaya Tritiya)** — Akshaya Tritiya stacks charters including the birth of Parashurama, the descent of the Ganga, the start of Treta Yuga, and Vyasa beginning the Mahabharata _(actors: Parashurama, Ganga, Vyasa)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/festivals-and-vratas.md) — (Puranic)

## Dvāpara Yuga  ·  1419 events

*Dharma on two legs. Kṛṣṇa and the Mahābhārata.*

- **Abduction of Draupadī by Jayadratha** — Jayadratha, smitten, carries Draupadī off by force from the Pāṇḍava forest hermitage while the brothers hunt _(actors: Jayadratha, Draupadī, Dhaumya, Kotikāsya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/jayadratha.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva 263–267)
- **Abduction of the Kāśi princesses** — Bhīṣma storms the svayaṃvara of Kāśī and carries off Ambā, Ambikā, and Ambālikā by force as war-brides for Vicitravīrya _(actors: Bhīṣma, Ambikā, Ambālikā, Ambā, Vicitravīrya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ambika-ambalika.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~102)
- **Abduction of the three Kāśī princesses** — Bhīṣma seizes Ambā, Ambikā and Ambālikā by force from the Kāśī svayaṃvara as brides for Vicitravīrya, defeating the assembled kings including Śālva _(actors: Bhīṣma, Ambā, Ambikā, Ambālikā, Śālva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~102; Udyoga Parva ~173)
- **Abhimanyu Born to Arjuna and Subhadra** — Abhimanyu is born at Indraprastha to Arjuna and Subhadra as the incarnation of Varcas son of Soma, fated to return after only sixteen years _(actors: Abhimanyu, Arjuna, Subhadra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Sambhava))
- **Akrūra summoned to Vraja** — Kaṃsa sends the devotee-noble Akrūra to fetch Krishna and Balarāma to Mathurā for the bow-sacrifice festival _(actors: Kaṃsa, Akrūra, Krishna, Balarāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kamsa-vadha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.36–38; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Śalya marches to join the Pāṇḍavas** — Śalya sets out from Madra with his army intending to fight for his sister's sons, the Pāṇḍavas _(actors: Śalya, the Pāṇḍava host)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shalya.md) — (Mahābhārata, Udyoga Parva (Sainyodyoga))
- **Arjuna and the Gandharva — the 'Tāpatya' frame** — Arjuna defeats the gandharva Aṅgāraparṇa/Citraratha on the Gaṅgā, is hailed as 'Tāpatya,' and asks why — prompting the Saṃvaraṇa–Tapatī tale _(actors: Arjuna, Aṅgāraparṇa/Citraratha)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/samvarana-tapati.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Caitraratha-parvan ~169)
- **Arjuna Conceived by Indra** — Kunti uses the Durvasa boon-mantra to invoke Indra, who begets Arjuna, the third Pandava, in the Shatashringa hermitage _(actors: Kunti, Indra, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~123)
- **Arjuna reaches Maṇipura on his tīrtha-yātrā** — During the twelfth year of his exile-pilgrimage, Arjuna arrives at the kingdom of Maṇipura and beholds the princess Citrāṅgadā _(actors: Arjuna, Citrāṅgadā, Citravāhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/chitrangada.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~206–207)
- **Arjuna sees Subhadrā at Dvārakā** — During his tīrtha-pilgrimage Arjuna comes to Dvārakā/Raivataka and is smitten by Subhadrā at the Vṛṣṇi festival _(actors: Arjuna, Subhadrā, Kṛṣṇa, Vṛṣṇi Yādavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/subhadra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva (Subhadrā-haraṇa Parva))
- **Bāṇa's boon of war** — The thousand-armed asura Bāṇāsura, vain of his arms, begs Śiva for a worthy battle; Śiva foretells his humbling when his banner-staff breaks _(actors: Bāṇāsura, Śiva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/banasura-usha-aniruddha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.62; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Bṛhadaśva Begins the Tale of Nala** — In exile Yudhiṣṭhira asks if any king suffered worse than he; the sage Bṛhadaśva answers with Nala's story and teaches him the secret of dice _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bṛhadaśva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 50, 78)
- **Bṛhadaśva narrates Nala's tale to Yudhiṣṭhira** — Sage Bṛhadaśva consoles the exiled Yudhiṣṭhira with the Nala story and teaches him the akṣa-hṛdaya (secret of dice) _(actors: Bṛhadaśva, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nala-damayanti.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 50, 78)
- **Bhima Born of Vayu** — Kunti uses the Durvasa-mantra to summon Vayu, who begets Bhima, the second Pandava endowed with superhuman strength _(actors: Kunti, Vayu, Bhima)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~123)
- **Bhishma's terrible vow** — Devavrata renounces the throne and vows lifelong celibacy so Satyavati's line may inherit, earning the name Bhishma and the boon of death-at-will _(actors: Devavrata/Bhishma, Shantanu, Satyavati)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Bhīma Catches the Bull-Form Shiva at Guptakāśī** — Fleeing the Pandavas seeking expiation for the Kurukshetra slaughter, Shiva as a bull is recognized by Bhima at Guptakashi; seized by the tail, the bull dives into the earth to re-emerge in five parts across Garhwal _(actors: Bhima, Pandavas, Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-kedar-pancha-badri.md) — (Skanda Purana (Kedara-khanda); Mahabharata tradition)
- **Bhīṣma Delivers the Mokṣadharma** — From his bed of arrows the dying Bhīṣma teaches Yudhiṣṭhira the dharma of liberation, the largest philosophical block of the epic _(actors: Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mokshadharma-dialogues.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva (Mokshadharma))
- **Bhīṣma Recites the Nārāyaṇīya** — In the aftermath of Kurukṣetra, the dying Bhīṣma teaches Yudhiṣṭhira the Nārāyaṇīya, systematizing Kṛṣṇa-Vāsudeva as supreme Brahman and Pāñcarātra theology _(actors: Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narayaniya.md) — (Mahabharata Shanti Parva (Mokshadharma) 321-339)
- **Birth as an aṃśa of Dvāpara** — Śakuni, son of Subala and brother of Gāndhārī, is born of a portion of the age-spirit Dvāpara, the embodiment of the gambling-die _(actors: Śakuni, Subala, Gāndhārī, Dvāpara)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/shakuni.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva (Aṃśāvataraṇa ~1.61))
- **Birth from the fish** — Born of King Uparicara Vasu's seed and the cursed apsarā-fish Adrikā, the girl twin is raised by the fisher-chief and carries a fish-smell (Matsyagandhā) _(actors: Uparicara Vasu, Adrikā, the fisher-chief (Dāśa), Satyavatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/satyavati.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~57)
- **Birth of Babhruvahana to Arjuna and Chitrangada** — Babhruvahana is born to Chitrangada of Manipura during Arjuna's tirtha-exile, bound by pact to remain as matrilineal heir of Manipura _(actors: Babhruvāhana, Arjuna, Citrāṅgadā, Citravāhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/babhruvahana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~207–208)
- **Birth of Babhruvāhana to Arjuna and Citrāṅgadā** — Babhruvāhana is born to Arjuna and Citrāṅgadā of Maṇipura, raised as her matrilineal heir _(actors: Arjuna, Citrāṅgadā, Citravāhana, Babhruvāhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/babruvahana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~207–208)
- **Birth of Barbarīka** — Barbarīka is born to Ghaṭotkaca and Maurvī/Kāmakaṇṭakaṭā, grandson of Bhīma, carrying both rākṣasa and Pāṇḍava blood _(actors: Barbarīka, Ghaṭotkaca, Maurvī/Kāmakaṇṭakaṭā, Bhīma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/barbarika-khatu-shyam.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa (Kāmārika Khaṇḍa); folk Mahābhārata traditions)
- **Birth of Duhshasana from the flesh-ball** — Duhshasana is born as the second of the hundred Kauravas, the second piece to ripen from Gandhari's divided ball of flesh _(actors: Duḥśāsana, Gāndhārī, Vyāsa, Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/dushasana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~107; Aṃśāvataraṇa ~61)
- **Birth of Irāvān to Arjuna and Ulūpī** — During his exile Arjuna unites with the Nāga princess Ulūpī (daughter of Kauravya) beneath the Gaṅgā, begetting Irāvān, who is reared in the serpent-realm _(actors: Arjuna, Ulūpī, Kauravya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/aravan-iravan.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~206)
- **Birth of Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana on the island** — Parāśara fathers Vyāsa on the fisher-maiden Satyavatī on a Yamunā island; he is born dark and island-born, matures instantly, and vows to come whenever remembered _(actors: Parāśara, Satyavatī (Matsyagandhā), Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyasa.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 3.3; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.4)
- **Birth of Kripa and Kripi from Sharadvat's seed** — Sage Sharadvat's seed falls on shara-grass at the sight of the apsara Janapadi and splits into twin children, Kripa and Kripi _(actors: Sharadvat, Janapadi (apsara), Kripa, Kripi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kripa.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~129-130)
- **Birth of Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa** — Vyasa is born on a river island to sage Parashara and Satyavati, dark-complexioned and regarded as a partial amsha incarnation of Vishnu _(actors: Vyasa, Parashara, Satyavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana 3.3-3.4)
- **Birth of Kuru to Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī** — Kuru is born to the Pauravā king Saṃvaraṇa and Tapatī, daughter of Sūrya, grafting a solar strand onto the Lunar line _(actors: Kuru, Saṃvaraṇa, Tapatī, Sūrya/Vivasvān)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/kuru-the-eponym.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Caitraratha-parvan ~167–173); Viṣṇu Purāṇa IV.19)
- **Birth of Pradyumna as Kāmadeva reborn** — Rukmiṇī bears Kṛṣṇa's eldest son at Dwārakā, declared to be the god of love Kāma re-embodied after Śiva burnt him _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Rukmiṇī, Pradyumna (Kāmadeva))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/pradyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.55; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Birth of Shishupala with three eyes and four arms** — Shishupala, son of Damaghosha and Shrutashrava, is born deformed with an extra eye and two extra arms, his abandonment forbidden by an aerial voice _(actors: Shishupala, Shrutashrava, Damaghosha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shishupala.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha-parva 40)
- **Birth of Vikarṇa among the hundred Kauravas** — Vikarṇa, third son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Gāndhārī, ripens from the māṃsapeśī flesh-ball split by Vyāsa, born an aṃśa of the Paulastya rākṣasas _(actors: Vikarṇa, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vikarna.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~107 (Sambhava); Aṃśāvataraṇa ~1.61)
- **Birth of Vyasa** — Krishna Dvaipayana Vyasa is born on a Yamuna island to Parashara and Satyavati, a partial amsha of Vishnu _(actors: Vyasa, Parashara, Satyavati)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva; Vishnu Purana 3.3-3.4)
- **Birth of Yuyutsu from the vaishya serving-woman** — Yuyutsu is born to Dhritarashtra by a vaishya serving-woman (Sughada/Sauvali) during Gandhari's failed two-year pregnancy, set apart from the hundred Kauravas by birth _(actors: Dhritarashtra, Sughada/Sauvali (vaishya maid), Gandhari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yuyutsu.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva (Sambhava-parva ~115))
- **Boon of Durvasa to Kunti** — The sage Durvasa, pleased by Kunti's year of service, grants her a mantra to summon any deity and beget a child sharing his nature _(actors: Durvasa, Kunti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/karna.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva ~305; Adi Parva 1.104)
- **Boyhood friendship with Droṇa and the half-kingdom vow** — Young Drupada, schooled beside Droṇa at Bharadvāja's āśrama, vows to share half his future kingdom with him _(actors: Drupada, Droṇa, Bharadvāja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/drupada.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~129)
- **Bride-price marriage of Mādrī to Pāṇḍu** — Bhīṣma secures the Madra princess Mādrī as Pāṇḍu's second queen by paying the customary bride-price (śulka) to her people _(actors: Mādrī, Bhīṣma, Pāṇḍu, Śalya, the Madra people)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/madri.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Building of Indraprastha** — Granted the wild tract Khāṇḍavaprastha, the Pāṇḍavas transform it into the splendid capital Indraprastha, its assembly-hall built by the asura architect Maya _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Pāṇḍavas, Maya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi/Sabhā Parva)
- **Composition of the Bhagavata Purana** — Narada finds Vyasa unsatisfied after dividing the Veda and composing the Mahabharata and prescribes singing Hari's lila, leading Vyasa to compose the Bhagavata Purana _(actors: Vyasa, Narada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.4-6)
- **Curse of Mahābhiṣa and Gaṅgā** — King Mahābhiṣa and the goddess Gaṅgā exchange desire in Brahmā's court and are cursed to mortal birth, fixing Mahābhiṣa's rebirth as Śāntanu _(actors: Mahābhiṣa (future Śāntanu), Gaṅgā, Brahmā)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/shantanu.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Saṃbhava-parvan ~96))
- **Death of Shalya** — On Day 18 Shalya rampages as fourth commander until Yudhishthira, fated to kill him, hurls a mantra-consecrated dart that pierces his chest, ending the Madra resistance _(actors: Shalya, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/09-shalya-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Shalya Parva I (Shalya-vadha))
- **Departure for the Kamyaka forest and the Akshaya-patra** — The exiles leave Hastinapura for the Kamyaka forest, and Surya grants Yudhishthira the inexhaustible vessel that yields unlimited food daily _(actors: the Pandavas, Draupadi, Surya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/03-vana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva 1-10)
- **Descent of portions (amshavatarana)** — Devas and asuras incarnate on earth to relieve its burden, with key heroes declared portions of gods _(actors: devas, asuras)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/01-adi-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva 59-64)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra's sleeplessness and summons of Vidura** — Tormented by foreboding of war over the Pāṇḍavas' kingdom, the blind king cannot sleep and summons Vidura, framing the Prajāgara discourse _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vidura-niti.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva 33)
- **Droṇa rejects Ekalavya** — The Niṣāda prince Ekalavya approaches Droṇa for archery training and is refused on account of his low birth and Droṇa's vow that none would surpass Arjuna _(actors: Ekalavya, Droṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ekalavya.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Drona consecrated as Kaurava commander** — On Bhishma's counsel Duryodhana installs Drona as commander-in-chief; Drona promises to capture Yudhishthira alive if Arjuna can be drawn away _(actors: Drona, Duryodhana, Bhishma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/07-drona-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Drona Parva 1-16 (Dronabhisheka))
- **Duryodhana consecrates Ashvatthaman as final commander** — The three surviving Kaurava warriors reach the dying Duryodhana, who with his last strength consecrates Ashvatthaman as the final commander-in-chief _(actors: Duryodhana, Ashvatthaman, Kripa, Kritavarman)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/10-sauptika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva 1)
- **Earth appeals to the gods and Viṣṇu plucks two hairs** — Oppressed by demonic kings, Earth appeals to the gods; Viṣṇu agrees to descend, and the plucking of a dark and a light hair becomes Krishna and Balarāma _(actors: Bhūmi/Pṛthivī, Viṣṇu, Krishna, Balarāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Viṣṇu Parva)
- **Ekalavya Surrenders His Thumb** — The Nishada prince Ekalavya learns archery before Drona's clay image and surrenders his right thumb as guru-dakshina _(actors: Ekalavya, Drona)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/README.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva)
- **Entry into Kāmyaka-vana** — The Pāṇḍavas leave Hāstinapura after the dice-game and settle first in Kāmyaka on the Sarasvatī's desert-edge, attended by Dhaumya and brahmins _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadī, Dhaumya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamyaka-dvaita-pandava-exile-forests.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva 5, 36)
- **Fire-birth of Dhṛṣṭadyumna** — Born full-grown and armed from Drupada's putrakāmeṣṭi revenge-sacrifice, named by a sky-voice as the fated slayer of Droṇa _(actors: Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Drupada, Yāja, Upayāja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/dhrishtadyumna.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~155-169)
- **Gāndhārī's curse on Krishna** — The bereaved Kuru queen Gāndhārī, having lost all hundred sons, curses Krishna that his Vrishni-Andhaka kinsmen will perish in fratricidal strife and he himself will die ignobly alone in the wilderness 36 years hence _(actors: Gāndhārī, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.1 (Mausala); Stri Parva 11)
- **Govardhana-dhāraṇa līlā** — Boy Kṛṣṇa lifts Govardhana hill on his little finger for seven days to shelter Braj from Indra's deluge — the act the Nathdwārā icon eternally depicts _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Indra, Nanda and the cowherds, cows of Braj)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/nathdwara-shrinathji.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.24–27)
- **Indra and Agni test King Shibi (dove and hawk)** — Indra as a hawk and Agni as a dove fall upon King Shibi, testing whether he will protect a refugee at any cost _(actors: Indra, Agni, Shibi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shibi.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva)
- **Jarasandha's seventeen sieges of Mathura** — Jarasandha of Magadha, Kamsa's father-in-law, besieges Mathura seventeen times to avenge Kamsa and is repelled each time, Krishna deliberately sparing him _(actors: Jarasandha, Krishna, Balarama, Yadavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/muchukunda-and-kalayavana.md) — (Bhagavata Purana X.50; Vishnu Purana V.22; Harivamsha (Vishnu Parva))
- **Kṛṣṇa commissions Uddhava as envoy to Vraja** — From Mathurā, Kṛṣṇa sends his cousin and minister Uddhava to console the grieving cowherds and gopīs of Vṛndāvana with a consoling message _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Uddhava)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhramara-gita-uddhava-sandesha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.46.1–11)
- **Karna consecrated as third Kaurava commander** — With Bhishma and Drona fallen, Duryodhana installs Karna as the third commander-in-chief; Karna vows to slay Arjuna or die and demands Shalya as a charioteer equal to Krishna _(actors: Duryodhana, Karna, Shalya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/08-karna-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Karna Parva 6-32)
- **Kṛṣṇa slays Mura at the Prāgjyotiṣa moat-fortress** — Kṛṣṇa, attacking Narakāsura's capital Prāgjyotiṣa/Kāmarūpa, first confronts and slays the thousand-armed (five/seven-headed) Dānava general Mura, who guards the moat-fortress with his many sons; Kṛṣṇa decapitates/destroys him with the Sudarśana chakra immediately before reaching Narakāsura. This slaying yields Viṣṇu/Kṛṣṇa's devotional epithets Murāri, Murahara, and Murabhid _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Mura (Murāsura), Mura's sons, Narakāsura)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/asura-wars-and-roster.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.59; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.29)
- **King Vareṇya's question to Gajānana** — Troubled by worldly sorrow and the problem of right action, King Vareṇya asks the Gajānana incarnation of Gaṇeśa for the highest knowledge, mirroring Arjuna's despondency _(actors: Gajānana (Gaṇeśa), King Vareṇya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ganesha-gita.md) — (Gaṇeśa Purāṇa, Krīḍā-khaṇḍa ch. 138)
- **King Śveta's self-directed giving** — A righteous, generous king performs every rite and gives lavishly but heaps all his gifts and feasts upon himself, never feeding guests or the needy _(actors: King Śveta)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/dana-upakhyanas-shveta-and-the-mongoose.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva (Tīrtha-yātrā / Mārkaṇḍeya block))
- **Kāliya's flight to the Yamunā** — The nāga Kāliya, fleeing Garuḍa from Ramaṇaka Dvīpa, takes refuge in a Yamunā pool barred to Garuḍa by Saubhari's curse _(actors: Kāliya, Garuḍa, sage Saubhari)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kaliya-mardana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.16; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5; Harivaṃśa)
- **Krishna curses Ashvatthama to deathless wandering** — After the night-massacre and the Brahmastra aimed at Uttara's womb, Krishna revives Parikshit and curses Ashvatthama to wander 3,000 years suffering until Kali's end _(actors: Krishna, Ashvatthama, Parikshit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/the-chiranjivis.md) — (Mahabharata Sauptika Parva)
- **Krishna Narrates the Vrikasura Tale** — Krishna tells Yudhishthira the cautionary tale of Vrikasura after the Rajasuya/Ashvamedha sacrifices, answering why Shiva-worshippers gain wealth _(actors: Krishna, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.88.6-7)
- **Krishna's Flight West and Founding of Dvaraka** — Harried repeatedly by Jarasandha and threatened by Kalayavana, Krishna abandons Mathura and leads the Yadava clans west to the sea-girt safety of Saurashtra, earning the epithet Ranchhod _(actors: Krishna, Jarasandha, Kalayavana, Yadavas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Bhagavata 10.50-52; Vishnu Purana 5.23; Harivamsha)
- **Kṛtavarma's lineage as a Bhoja-Vṛṣṇi chief** — Kṛtavarma, son of Hṛdika (hence Hārdikya), is a Bhoja-branch chief of the Vṛṣṇi/Yādava confederacy of Dvārakā and kinsman of Kṛṣṇa and Balarāma _(actors: Kṛtavarma, Hṛdika, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kritavarma.md) — (Mahābhārata; Bhāgavata Purāṇa IX.24)
- **Kuntī adopted by Kuntibhoja** — Śūrasena gives his firstborn daughter Pṛthā in adoption to his childless cousin Kuntibhoja, who renames her Kuntī and rears her _(actors: Śūrasena, Pṛthā/Kuntī, Kuntibhoja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Maṇḍavya's impalement and his curse on Yama** — Falsely accused, the silent ascetic Maṇḍavya is impaled but survives; learning his torment stemmed from a boyhood insect-piercing, he reforms cosmic law on the age of innocence and curses Yama to be born among men as a Śūdra _(actors: Aṇī-Maṇḍavya, Yama/Dharma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva CVIII)
- **Markandeya tells the Ramopakhyana to console Yudhishthira** — After Jayadratha's attempt to abduct Draupadi, the deathless sage Markandeya narrates the whole Rama story to console the humiliated Yudhishthira that even greater men suffered and recovered _(actors: Markandeya, Yudhishthira, Jayadratha, Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/ramopakhyana.md) — (Mahabharata, Vana Parva 257)
- **Marriage and self-blindfolding** — Gāndhārī of Gandhāra weds the blind Dhṛtarāṣṭra and binds her own eyes for life to share his darkness _(actors: Gāndhārī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Bhīṣma, Śakuni)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/gandhari.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Maya builds the illusory assembly hall** — In gratitude, Maya raises a peerless hall of optical illusion at Indraprastha with materials from Lake Bindusaras _(actors: Maya Danava, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/02-sabha-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Sabha Parva 1-3)
- **Mārkaṇḍeya narrates the Dharma-vyādha tale** — During the forest exile Mārkaṇḍeya answers Yudhiṣṭhira on whether women and the low-born can be wise by telling the story of Kauśika and the butcher _(actors: Mārkaṇḍeya, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/vyadha-gita.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Mārkaṇḍeya-samasyā)
- **Mudgala lives by uñchavṛtti at Kurukṣetra** — The brāhmaṇa-sage Mudgala subsists only on gleaned fallen grain, owning nothing in reserve, sustaining a fortnightly iṣṭi sacrifice and his family _(actors: Mudgala, his wife, his son)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mudgala.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva 246)
- **Mudgala's uñchavṛtti livelihood** — The brāhmaṇa Mudgala of Kurukṣetra subsists solely by gleaning fallen grain, yet performs the new/full-moon Iṣṭi and feeds gods, ancestors and guests before himself _(actors: Mudgala, his wife and son)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/mudgala.md) — (Mahābhārata, Vana Parva, Mārkaṇḍeya-samāsya (Mudgala-Upākhyāna), ~258-260 / CE ~246-247)
- **Naraka's tyranny and theft from heaven** — Bhaumāsura plunders the worlds, stealing Aditi's earrings, Varuṇa's parasol and the Maṇi-parvata jewel-seat and imprisoning 16,100 royal women _(actors: Narakāsura (Bhauma), Aditi, Varuṇa, the captive women)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/narakasura-vadha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.59; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Pandavas choose Matsya for ajnata-vasa** — As the 12 forest years close, the Pandavas decide to spend their 13th incognito year at King Virata's prosperous kingdom of Matsya _(actors: Yudhishthira, Pandava brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/04-virata-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Virata Parva 1)
- **Pandavas take service at Virata's Matsya court** — The five Pandavas and Draupadi pass their thirteenth incognito year disguised as servants in King Virata's prosperous, dharmic kingdom of Matsya _(actors: Virata, Yudhishthira, Bhima, Arjuna, Nakula, Sahadeva, Draupadi, Sudeshna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/virata-and-his-children.md) — (Mahabharata, Virata Parva 1-5)
- **Pūtanā and the poison-breast (and her mokṣa)** — The child-killing demoness sent by Kaṃsa suckles the infant Krishna with a poisoned breast and is drained of life, yet is granted liberation for coming in the form of a mother _(actors: Krishna (infant), Pūtanā, Kaṃsa, Yaśodā, gopīs)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-balya-lila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.6; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Raivataka festival & the abduction of Subhadrā** — At the Vṛṣṇi-Andhaka spring festival on the Raivataka slopes, Arjuna abducts Subhadrā on Kṛṣṇa's counsel _(actors: Arjuna, Kṛṣṇa, Subhadrā, Vṛṣṇi-Andhaka Yādavas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/girnar-raivataka-datta-tirtha.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~218-223; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10)
- **Rukmī blocks the match and pledges Rukmiṇī to Śiśupāla** — Rukmiṇī's arrogant brother Rukmī, hating Kṛṣṇa, vetoes the desired marriage and betroths her to Śiśupāla, ally of Jarāsandha _(actors: Rukmī, Bhīṣmaka, Rukmiṇī, Śiśupāla, Jarāsandha)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rukmini-harana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.52; Harivaṃśa Viṣṇu-parva; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.26)
- **Sañjaya as Dhṛtarāṣṭra's court sūta and truth-teller** — The sūta Sañjaya Gāvalgaṇi serves as the blind king's charioteer-bard, minister, and confidant, openly blaming Dhṛtarāṣṭra's partiality and Duryodhana's greed for the coming war _(actors: Sañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/sanjaya.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā / Udyoga Parvas)
- **Sanjaya granted divine sight** — Vyasa grants the charioteer-bard Sanjaya the eye of the gods (divya-drishti) so he can narrate the entire war to the blind king Dhritarashtra _(actors: Vyasa, Sanjaya, Dhritarashtra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/06-bhishma-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Bhishma Parva 2)
- **Sāmba's curse and leprosy** — Sāmba, Kṛṣṇa's son by Jāmbavatī, is cursed (via Nārada's contrivance) and afflicted with leprosy _(actors: Sāmba, Kṛṣṇa, Jāmbavatī, Nārada)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/konark-sun-temple-arka-kshetra.md) — (Sāmba Purāṇa; Bhaviṣya Purāṇa)
- **Sāmba's leprosy and cure by Sūrya** — Sāmba, son of Kṛṣṇa, is cursed with leprosy (by Durvāsā or Nārada), performs a twelve-year penance to Sūrya, recovers a Sun-image from the Candrabhāgā river, installs it, and is healed _(actors: Sāmba, Kṛṣṇa, Sūrya, Durvāsā, Nārada)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/bhavishya-purana.md) — (Bhaviṣya Purāṇa (Brahma Parva); Sāmba Purāṇa; Varāha Purāṇa)
- **Sūrya gives the Syamantaka to Satrājit** — The sun-god rewards his votary Satrājit with the radiant Syamantaka jewel that yields gold daily and wards off calamity _(actors: Sūrya, Satrājit)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/syamantaka-jewel.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.56; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.13)
- **Sudama and Krishna at Sandipani's gurukula** — The poor brahmin Sudama (Kuchela) and Krishna study together under guru Sandipani at Avanti, forming a boyhood friendship _(actors: Sudama/Kuchela, Krishna, Balarama, guru Sandipani)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudama-kuchela.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 10.80.6; cf. 10.45)
- **Sudāmā's poverty and the wife's urging** — The poor brāhmaṇa Sudāmā, boyhood schoolmate of Kṛṣṇa, is urged by his starving wife to seek aid from his now-royal friend at Dvārakā _(actors: Sudāmā (Kucela), Sudāmā's wife, Kṛṣṇa (referenced))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sudama-kuchela.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.80.6–11)
- **The Brāhmaṇa's araṇi stolen by a deer** — As the exile nears its end a deer bounds off with a Brāhmaṇa's fire-churning sticks, robbing him of his agni-hotra and setting the Yakṣa-praśna in motion _(actors: a Brāhmaṇa, the deer)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/yaksha-prashna.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva 311)
- **The interrupted Indra-yajña and Kṛṣṇa's argument** — Kṛṣṇa questions Nanda's annual Indra-sacrifice and argues for worshipping Govardhana, the cows and brāhmaṇas instead, on karma/svadharma grounds _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Nanda, the cowherd elders of Vraja)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/govardhana-dharana.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.24; Harivaṃśa (Viṣṇu Parva); Viṣṇu Purāṇa Book 5)
- **The iron statue of Bhima** — Intending to crush Bhima in revenge for Duryodhana, the blind Dhritarashtra is given an iron effigy by Krishna; he crushes it to powder and weeps with remorse before learning of the substitution _(actors: Dhritarashtra, Bhima, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/11-stri-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Stri Parva 11-12)
- **The musala-curse at Piṇḍāraka** — At the Saurāṣṭra coastal tīrtha of Piṇḍāraka near Dvārakā, the sages Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva and Nārada, mocked by Yādava youths who disguised Sāmba as a pregnant woman, curse that Sāmba will bear an iron pestle (musala) that will annihilate the Vṛṣṇi–Andhaka race — the trigger of the Yādava self-slaughter and Kṛṣṇa's departure at the Dvāpara–Kali hinge _(actors: Viśvāmitra, Kaṇva, Nārada, Sāmba, the Yādava (Vṛṣṇi–Andhaka) youths)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/mahabharata-tirtha-yatra-fords.md) — (Mahābhārata Mausala Parva 1; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.37)
- **The Raivataka festival and abduction of Subhadrā** — On the Raivataka (Girnar) festival slopes beside Dvārakā, Arjuna abducts Kṛṣṇa's sister Subhadrā on Kṛṣṇa's counsel _(actors: Arjuna, Subhadrā, Kṛṣṇa, Balarāma, Vṛṣṇi-Andhakas)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/girnar-raivataka-datta-tirtha.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva ~218-223; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10)
- **The Vasus Steal Nandini and Are Cursed** — The eight Vasus steal the wish-cow Nandini from Vasishtha, who curses them to be born as mortals, with the chief offender Dyaus to live a full long human life _(actors: The Vasus, Vasishtha, Dyaus)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhishma.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~99)
- **The Vyadha-gita: the righteous butcher teaches Kaushika** — A proud brahmana is humbled by a housewife and a righteous butcher who teaches that liberation lies in honestly doing one's appointed work _(actors: Kaushika, Dharma-vyadha, Markandeya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/lesser-gitas-catalog.md) — (Mahabharata Vana Parva ~3.197-206)
- **The war-council at Upaplavya** — With the exile fulfilled, the allied kings assemble; Krishna declares the Pandavas want their rightful kingdom and that an envoy should be sent, while Balarama counsels moderation and Satyaki force _(actors: Krishna, Pandavas, Drupada, Balarama, Satyaki)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Sainyodyoga)
- **Ulūpī abducts Arjuna into the Gaṅgā** — During Arjuna's twelve-year tīrtha-exile, the Nāga princess Ulūpī draws the bathing Arjuna down beneath the Gaṅgā into her father Kauravya's serpent-palace _(actors: Ulūpī, Arjuna, Kauravya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ulupi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~206 (vulgate 213–219))
- **Uttaṅka's quest for the celestial earrings** — The disciple Uttaṅka journeys to fetch a queen's earrings as guru-fee, swallowing dung that is secretly amṛta and surviving a curse-duel _(actors: Uttaṅka, Veda, King Pauṣya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Paushya sub-parva)
- **Uttanka's guru-fee demand for the celestial earrings** — After completing his studies Uttanka is set the impossible gurudakshina of fetching the queen's celestial earrings within a fixed time _(actors: Uttanka, Veda, Veda's wife)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva Paushya sub-parva)
- **Vasu's tapas and Indra's intervention** — The devout Cedi king Vasu Uparicara performs severe tapas; Indra, fearing rivalry, lures him back to kingship with gifts _(actors: Vasu Uparicara, Indra, the gods)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/uparichara-vasu.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva (Sambhava ~63))
- **Śvetaki's twelve-year sacrifice and Agni's indigestion** — King Śvetaki's unbroken sacrifice gorges Agni on ghee until the fire-god grows sick and dyspeptic _(actors: Śvetaki, Agni)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/khandava-vana-and-the-burning.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi-parva 214-215)
- **Veṇu-gītā (Song of the Flute)** — The gopīs rapturously describe Kṛṣṇa's flute-playing as the autumn season opens, the lyric overture that kindles desire for the rāsa _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, the gopīs of Vṛndāvana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/rasa-lila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.21)
- **Vidura summons Sanatsujata to teach Dhritarashtra** — On the war's eve the sleepless Dhritarashtra asks for higher wisdom; Vidura, pleading his shudra birth, meditates upon and summons the deathless sage Sanatsujata to teach in his stead _(actors: Dhritarashtra, Vidura, Sanatsujata)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/sanatsujatiya.md) — (Mahabharata, Udyoga Parva 5.41)
- **Vishvamitra's penance broken by Menaka** — Fearing Vishvamitra's severe tapas, Indra sends the apsara Menaka, who with Vayu and Kamadeva breaks the sage's penance, and he unites with her _(actors: Vishvamitra, Indra, Menaka, Vayu, Kamadeva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Viṣṇu dispatches Yoganidrā/Yogamāyā** — Viṣṇu sends his sleep-power Yogamāyā to transfer Balarāma to Rohiṇī and be born to Yaśodā as the substitute for the infant Kṛṣṇa _(actors: Viṣṇu, Yoganidrā/Yogamāyā, Devakī, Balarāma, Rohiṇī, Yaśodā)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/vindhyavasini.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5.1; Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.2–3)
- **Vṛkāsura wins the incinerate-by-touch boon from Śiva** — After a flesh-offering penance at Kedāra, the asura Vṛka extracts a death-by-touch boon and turns it on Śiva, who flees to Vaikuṇṭha _(actors: Vṛkāsura, Śiva, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhasmasura-and-vrikasura.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.88)
- **Vāraṇāvata escape into the forest** — The Pāṇḍavas and Kuntī flee the burning lac-house and halt exhausted in the rākṣasa-haunted forest where Bhīma keeps watch _(actors: Bhīma, Kuntī, Yudhiṣṭhira and the Pāṇḍava brothers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/hidimba-hidimbi.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva, Hiḍimba-vadha Parva (~154))
- **Vyasa Divides the Veda into Four** — Krishna-Dvaipayana Veda-Vyasa, the 28th and current Vyasa, splits the single Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama and Atharva and teaches them to four pupils, also authoring the Mahabharata _(actors: Krishna-Dvaipayana Vyasa; Paila; Vaishampayana; Jaimini; Sumantu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.3-3.4; Bhagavata Purana 1.4; Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Vyāsa and Kṛṣṇa prescribe the Aśvamedha to console Yudhiṣṭhira** — Yudhiṣṭhira sinks back into grief over the slain kinsmen; Vyāsa and Kṛṣṇa console him and prescribe the horse-sacrifice as expiation and a seal of universal sovereignty _(actors: Vyāsa, Kṛṣṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/14-ashvamedhika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 14.1-3)
- **Vyāsa narrates the Devī Bhāgavata to Janamejaya** — Vyāsa instructs King Janamejaya in the Goddess's Bhāgavata at the Naimiṣa assembly so the listener may attain mukti through Goddess-devotion _(actors: Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, frame)
- **Yadavas destroy themselves at Prabhasa** — Cursed by the brahmanas and maddened by drink, the Yadavas slaughter one another at Prabhasa as Krishna's avatara nears its end _(actors: Yadavas, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.1; Mahabharata Mausala Parva)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira approaches the dying Bhīṣma** — After Kurukṣetra, the grief-struck new king approaches Bhīṣma on his bed of arrows for instruction on dharma and liberation _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/vishnu-sahasranama.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIII.135)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira asks Bhīṣma for the thousand names of Śiva** — Having heard the Viṣṇu Sahasranāma, Yudhiṣṭhira requests the thousand names of Mahādeva/Śiva _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīṣma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/shiva-sahasranama.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIII)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira resolves to renounce the kingdom** — Sickened by the slaughter of kin and elders, Yudhiṣṭhira declares the kingdom worthless and resolves to abandon it for the forest as an ascetic _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/12-shanti-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 12 (Shanti Parva))
- **Abhimanyu Learns the Cakravyuha in the Womb** — While in Subhadra's womb Abhimanyu overhears Arjuna narrate how to penetrate the cakravyuha but not how to exit it, as Subhadra falls asleep mid-telling _(actors: Abhimanyu, Arjuna, Subhadra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/abhimanyu.md) — (Mahabharata tradition)
- **Śakaṭāsura the cart-demon** — A demon enters a heavy handcart to crush the babe, who overturns and smashes it with a kick of his tiny foot _(actors: Krishna (infant), Śakaṭāsura, Kaṃsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/krishna-balya-lila.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.7; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Akrūra's vision in the Yamunā** — Bathing en route, Akrūra sees Krishna and Balarāma within the river as Viṣṇu on Śeṣa, confirming their divinity _(actors: Akrūra, Krishna, Balarāma)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/kamsa-vadha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa X.39)
- **Śambara abducts the infant and casts him into the sea** — The asura Śambara, fated to die by Pradyumna, steals the ten-day-old child and flings him into the ocean, where a fish swallows him _(actors: Śambara, infant Pradyumna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/pradyumna.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 10.55; Harivaṃśa; Viṣṇu Purāṇa 5)
- **Ambā released to wed Śālva** — Ambā confesses she had chosen Śālva; Bhīṣma honorably releases her to her beloved while her sisters wed Vicitravīrya _(actors: Ambā, Bhīṣma, Śālva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/amba-shikhandi.md) — (Mahābhārata Udyoga Parva ~173)
- **Arjuna and Duryodhana seek Krishna's aid** — Both go to Dvaraka; Krishna offers either himself unarmed or his Narayani army; Arjuna chooses Krishna (who becomes his charioteer and vows to bear no weapon), Duryodhana takes the army _(actors: Arjuna, Duryodhana, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/05-udyoga-parva.md) — (Mahabharata Udyoga Parva, Sainyodyoga)
- **Arjuna and the Eye of the Bird** — In Drona's archery test only Arjuna sees nothing but the wooden bird's eye, and Drona declares his one-pointedness the mark of a master _(actors: Arjuna, Drona)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva ~123)
- **Arjuna Defeats Chitraratha (Aṅgāraparṇa)** — The gandharva-king Chitraratha challenges the Pāṇḍavas at the Gaṅgā; Arjuna burns his chariot with the Āgneyāstra and, sparing him, exchanges weapons and receives the Cākṣuṣī-mantra _(actors: Arjuna, Chitraratha/Aṅgāraparṇa, Kumbhīnasī)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/gandharvas-and-kinnaras.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva, Caitrarathaparva 169-172)
- **Aśvamedha horse reaches Manipura** — Yudhishthira's sacrificial horse, guarded by Arjuna, enters Manipura, where King Babhruvahana greets his father with homage rather than battle _(actors: Babhruvāhana, Arjuna, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/babhruvahana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Āśvamedhika Parva ~71–79)
- **Bhīṣma defers and Kṛṣṇa recites the Śiva Sahasranāma** — The dying Bhīṣma declines to expound Śiva's names himself and names Kṛṣṇa as the fit reciter, who then recites them _(actors: Bhīṣma, Kṛṣṇa, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/shiva-sahasranama.md) — (Mahābhārata, Anuśāsana Parva XIII)
- **Bhīṣma resumes teaching the still-grieving Yudhiṣṭhira** — Despite all of the Śānti Parva, Yudhiṣṭhira remains crushed by guilt, so Bhīṣma resumes his deathbed teaching on dāna-dharma, fate and effort _(actors: Bhīṣma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/13-anushasana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 13.1)
- **Birth and abandonment of Shakuntala** — A daughter is born to Menaka on the Malini river and abandoned; sheltered by shakunta birds, she is found and adopted by sage Kanva, who names her Shakuntala _(actors: Menaka, Vishvamitra, Shakuntala, Kanva)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/shakuntala-bharata.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva, Sambhava)
- **Birth of Vidura by niyoga** — When Ambikā sends her handmaid in her place, Vyāsa begets upon the gracious maid the supremely wise Vidura, born of a Śūdra-status mother and barred from the throne — the incarnation of Dharma fulfilling Maṇḍavya's curse _(actors: Vyāsa, the maidservant, Vidura, Satyavatī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/vidura.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
- **Boyhood warnings against Duryodhana's plots** — As the one righteous Kaurava insider, Yuyutsu (in retelling tradition) alerts the Pandavas/Vidura to Duryodhana's schemes against Bhima, including the poisoning at Pramanakoti _(actors: Yuyutsu, Duryodhana, Bhima, the Pandavas, Vidura)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yuyutsu.md) — (Mahabharata, Adi Parva [folk])
- **Brahma asks Krishna to return to his abode** — Brahma with the gods comes to Dvaraka and asks Krishna to return home; Krishna consents and turns to settle his devotees _(actors: Brahma, Krishna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uddhava-gita.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.6)
- **Brahmā prescribes the burning of Khāṇḍava** — Brahmā tells Agni he must consume the Khāṇḍava forest to cure his digestion, but only with Nara-Nārāyaṇa's aid _(actors: Brahmā, Agni)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/khandava-vana-and-the-burning.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi-parva 215-216)
- **Charvaka the rakshasa reviles Yudhishthira** — A rakshasa disguised as a brahmin named Charvaka denounces Yudhishthira after the Kurukshetra war and is destroyed by the assembled brahmins _(actors: Charvaka (rakshasa), Yudhishthira, the brahmins)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/nastika-darshanas-and-the-astika-nastika-frame.md) — (Mahabharata, Shanti Parva 38-39)
- **Conception of Droṇa from Bharadvāja and Ghṛtācī** — At the Gaṅgā the sage Bharadvāja sees Ghṛtācī; a breeze disrobes her, his seed escapes, and he catches it in a wooden trough (droṇa) from which the ayonija boy Droṇa develops, making Ghṛtācī ancestress of the weapons-master line _(actors: Bharadvāja, Ghṛtācī, Droṇa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/apsaras.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~130)
- **Division of the Veda** — Vyasa splits the one Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama, Atharva and teaches them to four disciples _(actors: Vyasa, Paila, Vaishampayana, Jaimini, Sumantu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.4; Bhagavata Purana 1.4, 12.6)
- **Division of the Veda into four** — Vyasa splits the primordial Veda into Rig, Yajur, Sama, and Atharva for the declining age and teaches them to his four disciples Paila, Vaishampayana, Jaimini, and Sumantu _(actors: Vyasa, Paila, Vaishampayana, Jaimini, Sumantu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.4; Bhagavata Purana 1.4, 12.6)
- **Draupadi Born of Fire** — The Panchala princess Draupadi is born from the sacrificial fire and becomes common wife of the five Pandavas _(actors: Draupadi)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/README.md) — (Mahabharata, Sabha/Vana Parvas)
- **Drupada humiliates the impoverished Droṇa** — Now a proud king, Drupada repudiates the boyhood promise and insults Droṇa, declaring friendship exists only between equals _(actors: Drupada, Droṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/drupada.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva ~129)
- **Duhshasana drags Draupadi by the hair** — After Draupadi is lost at dice, Duhshasana seizes her by the hair and hauls her, menstruating and in one garment, into the men's assembly _(actors: Duḥśāsana, Draupadī, Duryodhana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/dushasana.md) — (Mahābhārata, Sabhā Parva 60)
- **Durvāsa grants Kuntī the deity-invocation mantra** — After Kuntī serves the volatile sage Durvāsa flawlessly, he grants her an ātharvaṇa mantra to summon any deity to beget a child upon her _(actors: Durvāsa, Kuntī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kunti.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva)
