- **Brahmā's hurled discus names the forest (nemi/cakra)** — Brahmā releases his mind-made wheel and bids the sages settle where its rim (nemi) falls; the rim sinks here, naming the forest Naimiṣa and opening the Chakra-tīrtha spring _(actors: Brahmā, the ṛṣis)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Brahmāṇḍa Purāṇa; Naimiṣāraṇya-māhātmya)
- **Definition of the identity-grammar (āsana, mudrā, āyudha, vāhana, dhyāna-śloka)** — Pratimā-lakṣaṇa rules fix a deity's identity through posture, gesture, held attributes, mount and meditation-verse, generating named forms by attribute-permutation _(actors: Purāṇic compilers; Mārkaṇḍeya–Vajra dialogue of the Citrasūtra)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Agni Purāṇa; Matsya Purāṇa; Garuḍa Purāṇa pratimā-lakṣaṇa chs.; Viṣṇudharmottara III)
- **Deities Afflicted by Hunger Seek an Abode** — The emitted deities fall into the cosmic ocean, suffer hunger and thirst, and ask the Self for a dwelling _(actors: Ātman; the presiding deities; hunger and thirst)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.1-2)
- **Descent of Chaitanya Mahaprabhu (Closing-Age Teacher)** — In Gaudiya tradition the next descent after Krishna in this Mahayuga is Chaitanya Mahaprabhu within the present Kali Yuga, propagating the nama-sankirtana yuga-dharma _(actors: Chaitanya Mahaprabhu)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 11.5.32; Chaitanya Charitamrita)
- **Digvijaya conquest of the eight directions** — As warrior-queen she conquers the eight quarters, subduing kings, the dik-pālas, Indra and the devas _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Indra, the Lokapālas, the dik-pālas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Durvāsas, the gopīs, and the parting of the Yamunā** — The gopīs cross the Yamunā to feed Durvāsas after the river parts at the claim that Kṛṣṇa is a perpetual brahmacārin, dramatizing His transcendence of His own līlā _(actors: Durvāsas, the gopīs, Kṛṣṇa, the Yamunā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **Kṛṣṇa's Viśvarūpa Darśana to Janamejaya** — Viṣṇu as Kṛṣṇa the Pāṇḍava-envoy grants the cosmic-form darśana to king Janamejaya, commemorated at the Pāṇḍava Dūta temple of Kāñcī _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kanchipuram-city-of-temples.md) — (divyadesam.com)
- **Marriage of Jaratkāru and Vāsuki's sister (Manasā)** — Vāsuki gives his sister, also named Jaratkāru (later Manasā), to the ascetic so her son can halt the snake-sacrifice _(actors: Jaratkāru, Vāsuki, Jaratkāru/Manasā)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 45–47; Manasā-maṅgal tradition)
- **Oṃkāra-turīya identification of Narasiṃha-Brahman** — The Uttara analyses AUM and its fourth soundless mātrā, mapping the four states of consciousness to Narasiṃha as turīya, the supreme non-dual Self _(actors: Narasiṃha as Brahman/Ātman/antaryāmin)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-uttara-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Praśna 4 — sleep, dream and deep sleep** — Pippalāda explains to Sauryāyaṇī how the senses rest in the mind in sleep, the mind projects dreams, and in deep sleep all merge in the imperishable Ātman _(actors: Pippalāda, Sauryāyaṇī Gārgya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 4.1–4.11)
- **Śrīnivāsa's descent and the anthill austerity** — Viṣṇu follows Lakṣmī to earth as Śrīnivāsa and dwells in austerity on Veṅkaṭa hill, in some tellings nursed within an anthill _(actors: Śrīnivāsa (Viṣṇu))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Āruṇi questions Prajāpati on abandoning rites** — The sage Āruṇi (Uddālaka) asks Prajāpati how to relinquish all rites, and is told the physical renunciations (sons, wealth, sacred thread, study) _(actors: Āruṇi (Uddālaka); Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Āruṇeya Upaniṣad)
- **Sambandar's Confrontation with the Jains at Madurai** — At the Meenakshi/Madurai shrine, Sambandar confronts the Jains in the legends focused on the Pandya capital _(actors: Sambandar, Jains)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/275-paadal-petra-sthalams.md) — (Periya Puranam)
- **Second Boon — The Nāciketa Fire** — Naciketas asks the heavenward fire-sacrifice; Yama expounds the Nāciketa fire-altar, names it after the boy, and adds a necklace _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.12-19; Taittiriya Brahmana 3.11.8)
- **Slaying of Kolhāsura** — The Goddess slays the demon Kolhāsura, who dying begs that the city bear his name and that she remain as Mahālakṣmī of Kolhāpura _(actors: Mahālakṣmī, Kolhāsura)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Karavīra-māhātmya; Wikipedia: Kolhapur)
- **The Bhṛgu–Varuṇa inquiry into Brahman** — Bhṛgu asks his father Varuṇa to teach Brahman and, through repeated tapas, ascends from food to breath, mind, knowledge and finally bliss as Brahman — that from which beings are born, live, and into which they return _(actors: Bhṛgu (Vāruṇi) and his father Varuṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad III.1–III.6 (Bhṛgu-vallī))
- **The Bhūtātman Bound by the Guṇas** — The elemental self, overcome by prakṛti's three guṇas, fails to perceive the indwelling Lord and wanders through births _(actors: the bhūtātman (embodied self), the inner Lord)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 3.2)
- **The bow-and-arrow praṇava meditation** — Oṃ is the bow, the self the arrow, Brahman the target; drawn by a mind absorbed in That, one strikes the Imperishable _(actors: Aṅgiras (teacher))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 2.2.3–4)
- **The epic closes with its phala-śruti** — The book declares Vyāsa composed a six-million-verse poem distributed across the worlds, proclaims the merit of reciting the Mahābhārata, and gives the closing self-praise that what is here is found elsewhere and what is not here is nowhere, with benediction to Nārāyaṇa, Nara and Sarasvatī _(actors: Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/18-svargarohana-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 18.5)
- **The five fall one by one on the slopes of Meru** — As they cross the high snow, Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, and Bhīma each fall in turn, Yudhiṣṭhira naming the single fault (partiality, pride in wisdom, vanity of beauty, arrogance in prowess, gluttony and boasting) that bars each from bodily ascent, never looking back _(actors: Draupadī, Sahadeva, Nakula, Arjuna, Bhīma, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.2)
- **The Hidden Carpenter and the Unfinished Images** — Viśvakarmā (or Ananta-mahārāṇā) carves the log behind locked doors; the door is opened early, leaving Jagannātha armless and unfinished, and Brahmā consecrates the temple _(actors: Viśvakarmā / Ananta-mahārāṇā, Indradyumna, Guṇḍicā, Brahmā)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa; Brahma Purāṇa)
- **The 'I am Śiva' (śivo'ham) realization** — The meditator declares his identity with Śiva-Brahman — all is born, established and dissolved in Me; that non-dual Brahman am I; for Me there is no death, fear, caste, birth, father or mother _(actors: the realized meditator (kevalin); Śiva-Brahman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 16-24)
- **The righteous reign** — Parīkṣit rules as a cakravartin at the Dvāpara→Kali cusp, marries Irāvatī, fathers Janamejaya, and performs three Aśvamedhas _(actors: Parīkṣit, Irāvatī, Janamejaya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.16; Mahābhārata)
- **The Sarpa-satra begins at Takṣaśilā** — Janamejaya commissions a serpent session-sacrifice at Takṣaśilā with hotṛ Caṇḍabhārgava; serpents are dragged by mantra into the fire and burned by the thousands _(actors: Janamejaya, Caṇḍabhārgava, the ṛtvij priests, the nāgas)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/janamejaya-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi (Āstīka Parva))
- **The sixteen mantra-saṃskāras and mantra-caitanya** — A received mantra is purified by sixteen saṃskāras and 'awakened' (caitanya), since a mantra may be asleep or cursed and thus inert without it _(actors: Guru and initiate)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Prapañcasāra Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi)
- **The vidyā/avidyā and saṃbhūti/asaṃbhūti balanced pairs** — Devotion to either knowledge or ignorance alone leads to darkness; one crosses death by holding both vidyā and avidyā (and saṃbhūti and asaṃbhūti) together _(actors: the integrating knower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 9–14 (Kāṇva & Mādhyandina recensions; Śaṅkara bhāṣya))
- **The worn-garland miracle (Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār)** — Gōdai secretly wears the Lord's garlands; Viṣṇu declares he will accept only garlands she has first worn, giving her the epithet Cūḍikkoḍutta Nācciyār _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ, Periyāḻvār, Vaṭapatraśāyī Viṣṇu)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Āṇḍāḷ hagiography)
- **War-widows enter the Gaṅgā to rejoin their husbands** — Vyāsa tells the widows that any who wish to rejoin their dead husbands may enter the river; women who do so cast off their bodies in the Gaṅgā and ascend to their husbands' worlds _(actors: Vyāsa, the war-widows)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Putradarshana))
- **Yama's test — wealth offered and refused** — Yama tries to deflect the third boon with sons, herds, gold, long life and apsarases; Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds Yama to the knowledge of the Self _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.1.21–29)
- **Yogakuṇḍalinī rouses the serpent power** — The text describes rousing kuṇḍalinī by bhastrikā breath and bandhas, the khecarī-mudrā and drinking cranial amṛta, culminating in union with Śiva at the sahasrāra _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Yogakuṇḍalinī Up.)
- **Ambubāchī Melā — annual menstruation** — Each Āṣāḍha the Goddess menstruates; the temple closes three days and reopens with red-cloth prasāda, drawing tantric pilgrims _(actors: Kāmākhyā Devī, tāntrikas and ascetics, pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamakhya-nilachala-kamarupa.md) — (regional festival tradition (Ambubachi Mela))
- **Birth of Āstīka** — After Jaratkāru abandons his pregnant wife, the half-brahmin half-nāga boy Āstīka is born and reared by Vāsuki to save the snakes _(actors: Āstīka, Jaratkāru, Jaratkāru/Manasā, Vāsuki, Cyavana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 47–48)
- **Brahma founds the Tirumala Brahmotsavam** — Brahma is said to have first performed the nine-day utsavam on Venkatachala hill to thank Vishnu for descending as Venkateshwara in the Kali Yuga, establishing the paradigm South-Indian brahmotsava form with its sequence of daily vahana processions culminating in Garuda Seva, Rathotsavam and the Chakra-snanam _(actors: Brahma, Vishnu/Venkateshwara (Malayappa Swami))_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/regional-temple-festivals.md) — (Venkatachala Mahatmya / Varaha Purana; Vaikhanasa-Pancharatra Agama; TTD)
- **Composition of the Tiruppāvai and Nācciyār Tirumoḻi** — At Srivilliputhur Āṇḍāḷ composes the thirty-verse Tiruppāvai and the 143-verse Nācciyār Tirumoḻi, vowing to wed only Raṅganātha _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham — Tiruppāvai, Nācciyār Tirumoḻi)
- **Cow and Horse Rejected, Man Accepted** — The deities reject cow and horse as dwellings but accept the human form, exclaiming su-kṛtam ('well made') _(actors: Ātman; the deities)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.3)
- **Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī and Kuntī die in the forest fire** — After two more years of harsh tapas, a wildfire sweeps the wood; too weak to flee, the three elders choose not to escape and the blind king sits in yoga as the flames take all three; Nārada announces their deaths to Yudhiṣṭhira _(actors: Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Gāndhārī, Kuntī, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **Divergence of sectarian Āgamic iconometric canons** — Śaiva, Vaikhānasa and Pāñcarātra Āgamas establish sect-specific bera/pratimā-lakṣaṇa distinguishing dhruva-bera from utsava icons by distinct measures _(actors: Vaikhānasa and Śaiva Āgama lineages)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Vaikhānasa Āgama; Śaiva Āgama kriyāpāda)
- **Doctrine of the Good vs. the Pleasant (śreyas/preyas)** — Satisfied by the test, Yama teaches that the wise choose the Good (śreyas) over the Pleasant (preyas), and that the Self is gained only by the one it chooses _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.2.1–23)
- **Dvā suparṇā — two birds on one tree** — Two companion birds on one tree: the jīva eats the sweet fruit while the witnessing Self looks on; seeing the Lord, the grieving jīva's sorrow departs _(actors: jīva (embodied self), the witnessing Ātman/Īśa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.1–2)
- **Enrollment among the 18 Mahā Śakti Pīṭhas** — Mahālakṣmī of Kolhapur is fixed as the seventh of the Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭhas in the stotram attributed to Ādi Śaṅkara _(actors: Mahālakṣmī, Ādi Śaṅkara (attrib.))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kolhapur-mahalakshmi-karavira.md) — (Aṣṭādaśa Śakti Pīṭha Stotram)
- **Gokarna-Dhundhukari ghost-liberation (Bhagavata-Mahatmya)** — The allegory of Bhakti as a mother with sons Jnana and Vairagya, with the ghost Dhundhukari liberated by recitation of the Bhagavata _(actors: Gokarna, Dhundhukari, Bhakti, Jnana, Vairagya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/padma-purana.md) — (Padma Purana (Uttara Khanda, Bhagavata-Mahatmya))
- **Hiraṇmayena pātreṇa — the golden vessel over Truth's face** — A prayer to Pūṣan/the solar deity to unveil the golden disc hiding the face of Truth, and the identity 'that Person in the sun, He am I.' _(actors: Pūṣan / Sūrya / Yama; the dying seeker)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 15–16)
- **King Indradyumna founds the Jagannātha cult at Puri** — King Indradyumna recovers the divine dāru-brahman image, which Viśvakarmā carves into the Jagannātha–Balabhadra–Subhadrā triad at Puruṣottama-kṣetra (Puri) _(actors: Indradyumna, Viśvakarmā, Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/brahma-purana.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa (Puruṣottama-māhātmya); Skanda Purāṇa)
- **Marriage of Śrīnivāsa and Padmāvatī** — Śrīnivāsa falls in love with and marries Padmāvatī (Alamēlu-maṅgā), lotus-born daughter of King Ākāśarāja and a form of Lakṣmī, enshrined at Tiruchanūr _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Padmāvatī, King Ākāśarāja)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Medha-sūktas invoke intelligence and memory** — Short hymns beg Savitṛ, Sarasvatī, Agni, Indra and the Aśvins to grant medhā (intellect/memory), recited by students before Vedic study _(actors: Medhā; Savitṛ; Sarasvatī; Vedic students)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, Medha-sūktas)
- **Nabakalebara — Periodic Re-embodiment** — The perishable wooden images are periodically replaced and the secret Brahma-padārtha life-essence transferred; historical rites span 1969–2015 _(actors: Jagannātha triad, Dayitāpati priests)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (temple tradition / sthala-purāṇa; academic record)
- **Nanda Dynasty — Exterminator of Kshatriyas** — Mahapadma Nanda, born of a shudra woman, founds the first non-kshatriya empire, styled 'exterminator of all kshatriyas' _(actors: Mahapadma Nanda, Mahanandi)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.10-11)
- **Nādabindu and Haṃsa systematize inner sound (nāda/laya-yoga)** — Laya-yoga dissolves the mind in the ten unstruck inner sounds; the Haṃsa Upaniṣad sets the haṃsa-vidyā/ajapā-gāyatrī in a Sanatkumāra–Gautama dialogue _(actors: Sanatkumāra; Gautama)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Nādabindu Up.; Haṃsa Up.)
- **Nārada questions Prajāpati on the paramahaṃsa** — Nārada asks Prajāpati to define the supreme renouncer, who casts off staff, tuft, and thread and wears only knowledge as his mark _(actors: Nārada; Prajāpati)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Paramahaṃsa Upaniṣad)
- **Praśna 5 — meditation on Oṃ (one, two, three mātrās)** — Pippalāda teaches Śaibya that meditating on Oṃ's one/two/three mātrās wins the world of men, the moon, or Brahma-loka and the supreme Puruṣa _(actors: Pippalāda, Śaibya Satyakāma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 5.1–5.7)
- **Prophesied Descent of Kalki** — Vishnu is prophesied to descend as Kalki at the end of Kali Yuga to end the age of strife and restore Satya Yuga _(actors: Vishnu; Kalki)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2)
- **Puraścaraṇa — the preparatory regimen** — Before a mantra becomes siddha the sādhaka completes a cascade of japa, homa, tarpaṇa, abhiṣeka and brāhmaṇa-bhojana in a one-tenth decadal ratio _(actors: Tantric sādhakas)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Mantra-mahodadhi; Meru-tantra)
- **Takṣaka Slays King Parīkṣit** — The serpent-chief Takṣaka, having been cursed-upon by Śṛṅgin's word against Parīkṣit, slays the king with his venom on the seventh day, triggering Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Takṣaka, Parīkṣit, Śṛṅgin)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Parva)
- **Taming and regulating personified Kali** — Parīkṣit catches Kali beating the bull Dharma and cow Earth, spares the suppliant, and confines adharma by assigning Kali fixed abodes (gambling, drink, illicit sex, slaughter, gold) _(actors: Parīkṣit, personified Kali, Dharma (bull), Bhūmi (cow))_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.16–17)
- **The dog reveals himself as Dharma and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends in the body** — Indra offers to carry Yudhiṣṭhira to Svarga but forbids the dog; Yudhiṣṭhira refuses to abandon the faithful creature, whereupon the dog reveals himself as Dharma (his divine father) who praises his compassion, and Yudhiṣṭhira ascends to heaven in his living mortal body, an unprecedented feat _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, the dog (Dharma))_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/17-mahaprasthanika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 17.3)
- **The food-hymns and 'I am food' realization-chant** — The Bhṛgu-vallī closes with injunctions never to despise food and the liberated knower's exultant chant 'I am food, I am the eater of food.' _(actors: the liberated knower (Bhṛgu); the Taittirīya tradition)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/taittiriya-upanishad.md) — (Taittirīya Upaniṣad III.7–III.10)
- **The gopīs question the nature of the Deity** — The gopīs and sages ask who Kṛṣṇa truly is, how to worship Him, and what His mantra and abode are; the answers reaffirm Kṛṣṇa as the one Brahman behind all gods _(actors: gopīs, sages, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **The Nimiṣa demons slain in a wink** — A host of Nimiṣa demons is destroyed at the site in an instant (nimiṣa), an alternative etymology for the name Naimiṣa _(actors: the ṛṣis, the Nimiṣa demons)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Mahābhārata)
- **The storming of Kailāsa** — Mīnākṣī marches on Śiva's Kailāsa, routs his gaṇas including Nandi and Vīrabhadra, drawing Śiva onto the field _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Śiva's gaṇas, Nandi, Vīrabhadra, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **The Three Guṇas Mapped to the Trimūrti** — The Upaniṣad names sattva, rajas, tamas explicitly and maps them to Viṣṇu, Brahmā and Rudra as the One's threefold unfolding _(actors: sattva/rajas/tamas, Viṣṇu, Brahmā, Rudra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 5.2)
- **The Yakṣa Appears** — Brahman manifests as an unrecognizable yakṣa (spirit) before the gods to humble them _(actors: Brahman (as yakṣa); the devas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.2–3)
- **Third Boon — The Secret of Death Requested** — Naciketas asks the great doubt of whether a man exists after death, the Upaniṣad's metaphysical innovation _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.20)
- **Two-birds image and turīya analysis** — The text re-quotes the two-birds (dvā suparṇā) verse and the witness of waking-dream-deep-sleep, weaving Māṇḍūkya-style turīya analysis into the Śaiva meditation _(actors: the jīva (eating bird); the Lord (witnessing bird))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad 12-17 (cf. Śvetāśvatara 4.6 / Muṇḍaka 3.1.1 / Ṛgveda 1.164.20))
- **Unity of Mantrarāja and Praṇava; Uttara phala-śruti** — The Uttara teaches that the man-lion Mantrarāja and the Oṃkāra are one, and that knowing this Oṃkāra-Narasiṃha grants liberation, crossing death into turīya _(actors: Narasiṃha-Brahman; the liberation-seeking knower)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/nrisimha-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Nṛsiṃha-uttara-tāpanīya Upaniṣad)
- **Vandi-koṇḍa līlā — carrying earth for piṭṭu and taking the cane-blow** — Śiva labours as a coolie for the piṭṭu-seller Vandi to dam the Vaikai; the king's cane-blow on the lazy labourer is felt by every living being _(actors: Śiva, old woman Vandi, King Varaguṇa Pāṇḍya)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Agni Fails to Burn the Straw** — Agni is sent first and cannot burn a single blade of grass set before him by the yakṣa _(actors: Agni; the yakṣa (Brahman))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.4–6)
- **Andal Composes the Tiruppavai at Srivilliputhur** — Andal (Goda) is born at Srivilliputhur, birthplace also of Periyalvar, where the Tiruppavai originates _(actors: Andal, Periyalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Naalayira Divya Prabandham / Alvar hagiography)
- **Bindu-texts interiorize Oṃ (praṇava)** — Amṛtabindu, Dhyānabindu, Amṛtanāda and Brahmavidyā resolve Oṃ into bīja, bindu, nāda and kalā and into the soundless turīya, teaching that the mind alone binds and frees _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Amṛtabindu (Brahmabindu) Up.; Dhyānabindu Up.; Amṛtanāda Up.; Brahmavidyā Up.)
- **Chanakya Uproots the Nandas** — A brahmana (Chanakya/Kautilya) overthrows the Nandas and enthrones Chandragupta, founding the Maurya dynasty _(actors: Chanakya/Kautilya, Chandragupta Maurya)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1.12)
- **Doctrine of māna-doṣa and canonical efficacy** — The texts hold that a correctly-measured image is prāsādika while a proportion-fault (māna-doṣa) brings harm, making the canon a ritual necessity rather than aesthetics _(actors: Varāhamihira; Mayamata and Śukranīti authorities)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/murti-lakshana-and-iconometry.md) — (Bṛhat Saṃhitā 58.30–31; Mayamata; Śukranīti 4)
- **Janamejaya's Sarpa-Satra (Snake-Sacrifice)** — Janamejaya vows to exterminate the serpent race and undertakes the sarpa-satra, whose oblations draw nāgas of every size from across the worlds into the flames _(actors: Janamejaya, nāgas, Takṣaka)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīka Parva)
- **Kaṇṇappa's Eye-Offering at Srikalahasti** — The hunter-saint Kannappa, worshipping the linga his untaught way, gouges out his own eyes to stop the linga's bleeding eye; Shiva seizes his hand, restores his eyes and grants liberation, proving devotion outranks ritual _(actors: Kannappa (Tinnan), Shiva)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/pancha-bhuta-sthalams.md) — (Periya Purana (Kannappa Nayanar Puranam))
- **Kubera's wedding-loan to Śrīnivāsa** — To meet bridal expenses Śrīnivāsa borrows a vast sum from Kubera, vowing repayment with interest through all of Kali-yuga — the basis of the temple hundi donations _(actors: Śrīnivāsa, Kubera)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Lakulisha prophecy, last of the 28 Yogeshvaras** — The Purana prophesies Maheshvara descending in Kali Yuga as the ascetic Lakulisha, 28th Yogeshvara, with four disciples who found the Pashupata sect _(actors: Shiva (Lakulisha), Kushika, Garga, Mitra, Kaurushya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/kurma-purana.md) — (Kurma Purana (ch. 53))
- **Opening the rock / staying the flood for the Pāṇḍya** — Śiva cleaves a rock or stays the Vaikai flood for the Pāṇḍya, delivering the city _(actors: Śiva, Pāṇḍya king)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Parikṣit insults sage Śamīka with a dead snake** — The lone Kuru heir Parikṣit, thirsty while hunting, loops a dead snake on the silent meditating sage Śamīka _(actors: Parikṣit, Śamīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 36–40)
- **Phala-śruti and Śatarudriya benediction** — The closing fruit-of-recitation verses promise that whoever recites this knowledge, chanting it with the Śatarudriya, is purified of the great sins and attains kaivalya, oneness with Śiva _(actors: the reciter; Śiva (Rudra))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kaivalya-upanishad.md) — (Kaivalya Upaniṣad closing verses 23-24 (cf. Yajurveda Śatarudriya/Rudram))
- **Praśna 6 — the Person of sixteen parts (ṣoḍaśa-kala puruṣa)** — Pippalāda answers Sukeśā that the sixteen kalās arise from the Person within the body and dissolve back into him as rivers lose name-and-form in the sea _(actors: Pippalāda, Sukeśā Bhāradvāja; prince Hiraṇyanābha Kausalya (referenced))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/prashna-upanishad.md) — (Praśna Upaniṣad 6.1–6.8)
- **Rudhirādhyāya blood-offering rite** — The Kālikā Purāṇa's blood-chapter prescribes the animal (and ideal human) sacrifice continued at Kāmākhyā _(actors: Kāmākhyā Devī, worshippers)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/kamakhya-nilachala-kamarupa.md) — (Kālikā Purāṇa (Rudhirādhyāya))
- **Sañjaya escapes the fire and departs for the Himālaya** — Before the fire closes in, Dhṛtarāṣṭra orders his faithful charioteer Sañjaya to save himself; bereft of his master, Sañjaya retires to the Himālaya to perform penance and is never heard of again _(actors: Sañjaya, Dhṛtarāṣṭra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/15-ashramavasika-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 15 (Naradagamana))
- **Satyam eva jayate — Truth alone triumphs** — The verse 'satyam eva jayate nānṛtaṃ' declares truth alone triumphs over falsehood; later adopted as the national motto of India under the Lion Capital of Aśoka _(actors: the sages (ṛṣis); Republic of India (adoption))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.1.6; State Emblem of India)
- **Āṇḍāḷ's bridal procession and merging at Śrīraṅgam** — Viṣṇu commands that Gōdai be brought in bridal procession to Śrīraṅgam, where she enters the sanctum and merges into Raṅganātha _(actors: Āṇḍāḷ, Periyāḻvār, Raṅganātha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/srivilliputhur-vatapatrasayi-andal-kshetra.md) — (Āṇḍāḷ hagiography; Guruparamparā)
- **Takṣaka flees to Indra** — The chief target Takṣaka takes refuge with his ally Indra, coiling around the throne, until the priests' mantra begins hauling both Takṣaka and Indra toward the fire and Indra abandons him _(actors: Takṣaka, Indra, the priests)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/janamejaya-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi (Āstīka Parva))
- **The ṣaṭkarma — six applied prayogas** — The six acts (śānti, vaśīkaraṇa, stambhana, vidveṣaṇa, uccāṭana, māraṇa) deploy a perfected mantra, each with assigned deity, season, direction and seat _(actors: Tantric adepts; presiding deities (Rati, Kāmadeva, Kālī, Nirṛti, Bhairava, etc.))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/mantra-shastra.md) — (Mantra-mahodadhi; Śāradā-tilaka Tantra; Agni Purāṇa; Tantrarāja Tantra)
- **The Chakra-tīrtha discus-ford established** — The central tank at Nīmsār marks where the wheel's rim (or Viṣṇu's Sudarśana/Manomaya Cakra) struck the earth, opening a perennial spring said to well up from Pātāla _(actors: Brahmā / Viṣṇu (Hari), pilgrims)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Vāyu Purāṇa; Skanda Purāṇa Naimiṣa-khaṇḍa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4)
- **The chariot allegory of the Self** — Yama teaches the ratha-kalpanā: the Self as rider, body as chariot, intellect as charioteer, mind as reins, senses as horses, sense-objects as roads _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.3.3–9)
- **The cremation prayer — body to ashes, Agne naya supathā** — The dying invocation releasing breath to the immortal Wind and body to ashes, and the closing prayer to Agni to lead by the good path _(actors: Agni; the dying person / cremation officiant)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Īśa Upaniṣad 17–18 (= Ṛgveda 1.189.1))
- **The Devas approach and learn Kṛṣṇa's supremacy** — The gods led by Brahmā and Indra approach the supreme Person and learn He is the inner Self and Lord of all the Devas, who themselves worship Him _(actors: Brahmā, Indra, the Devas, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **The Gods Enter Their Seats in Man** — Each deity enters its station in the human body, becoming the corresponding sense-faculty _(actors: Ātman; Agni, Vāyu, Āditya, the Quarters, herbs/trees, Moon, Death, Waters)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.2.4-5)
- **The Ratha Yātrā Chariot Festival** — On Āṣāḍha dvitīyā the triad rides three giant chariots (Nandighoṣa, Tāḷadhvaja, Darpadalana) to the Guṇḍicā temple; the Gajapati king performs Chera Paṅharā _(actors: Jagannātha, Balabhadra, Subhadrā, Gajapati king)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/jagannath-puri-purushottama-kshetra.md) — (Brahma Purāṇa māhātmya layer; temple tradition)
- **The Sannyāsa corpus as charter of the Daśanāmī orders** — The group supplies the Śruti backing for the ekadaṇḍin Daśanāmī monastic system traditionally organised under Ādi Śaṅkara, who read his order back into these texts _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara; Daśanāmī sannyāsins)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/sannyasa-upanishads-overview.md) — (Sannyāsa group; Daśanāmī tradition)
- **The Six-Limbed Ṣaḍaṅga-Yoga** — Śākāyanya sets out the sixfold yoga — prāṇāyāma, pratyāhāra, dhyāna, dhāraṇā, tarka, samādhi — prefiguring Patañjali _(actors: Sage Śākāyanya, the yogī)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 6.18)
- **The third breast vanishes at the sight of Śiva** — Facing Śiva, her third breast disappears and her battle-fury turns to a bride's modesty, marking him as her destined lord _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **The thirsty hunt and dead-snake insult** — Exhausted and parched, and with Kali entered through his gold crown, Parīkṣit drapes a dead snake on the silently meditating sage Śamīka _(actors: Parīkṣit, sage Śamīka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.18)
- **Yama Tests Naciketas with Bribes** — Yama offers sons, cattle, gold, lands, long life and celestial maidens instead, but Naciketas rejects all fleeting pleasures and holds to the third boon _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.1.21-29)
- **Birth of Nammalvar at Azhwarthirunagari** — Nammalvar (Maran/Satakopan), foremost of the Alvars who sang the most Divya Desams, is born at Tirukkurugur/Azhwarthirunagari _(actors: Nammalvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Alvar hagiography)
- **Buddha absorbed as Vishnu's 9th avatara (Mayamoha rationale)** — Puranic tradition folds the Buddha into the Dashavatara as a deluder (Mayamoha) sent to lead the unworthy/asuras away from the Veda, both absorbing and discrediting Buddhism _(actors: Vishnu (as Buddha/Mayamoha), the asuras)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/nastika-darshanas-and-the-astika-nastika-frame.md) — (Vishnu Purana 3.17-18; Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24)
- **Creation and Pursuit of Food** — The Self creates food, which flees, and is finally seized only by the down-breath (apāna) _(actors: Ātman; the faculties; apāna)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.3.1-10)
- **Dadhīci gives his bones at the kṣetra to forge the Vajra** — At the Naimiṣa kṣetra (Misrikh/Dadhīci-kuṇḍa) the sage Dadhīci surrenders his bones to forge the Vajra that slays Vṛtra _(actors: Dadhīci, Indra, Vṛtra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa 6.9–6.10; local māhātmya)
- **Declaration of Goloka/Vṛndāvana as the supreme abode and phala-śruti** — Kṛṣṇa is declared cause of all causes with Goloka-Vṛndāvana as His eternal transcendent abode; the text closes with the worship-method and a phala-śruti promising His abode and liberation _(actors: Kṛṣṇa, the worshipper)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/gopala-tapaniya-upanishad.md) — (Gopāla-tāpanī Upaniṣad, Uttara-tāpanī)
- **Frame-dialogue Yoga Upaniṣads transmit aṣṭāṅga/tāraka yoga** — Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa (Sun to Yājñavalkya), Triśikhi-brāhmaṇa (Sun to Triśikhi), Darśana (Dattātreya to Sāṃkṛti) and Varāha (Viṣṇu-Boar to Ṛbhu) transmit full eight-limbed/tāraka yoga with chakras and kuṇḍalinī _(actors: Sun-Puruṣa; Yājñavalkya; Triśikhi; Dattātreya; Sāṃkṛti; Viṣṇu (Varāha); Ṛbhu)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/yoga-upanishads-overview.md) — (Maṇḍala-brāhmaṇa Up.; Triśikhi-brāhmaṇa Up.; Darśana Up.; Varāha Up.)
- **Śṛṅgin's curse on Parikṣit** — Śamīka's son Śṛṅgin curses the king to die within seven days from Takṣaka's bite; Parikṣit retreats to a guarded pillar-palace _(actors: Śṛṅgin, Śamīka, Parikṣit, Takṣaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 37–43)
- **Śṛṅgī's seven-day death-curse** — Śamīka's boy-son Śṛṅgī curses the king to die within seven days by the bite of the nāga Takṣaka; Śamīka rebukes his son and sends a warning _(actors: Śṛṅgī, Śamīka, Gauramukha, Parīkṣit)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.18)
- **Hunting the boar (Pandi līlā)** — Śiva pursues a great boar through Pāṇḍya country, founding shrines along the chase _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Śiva pledges the Madurai wedding** — Śiva bids her return to her capital and promises to come as Sundareśvara to wed her at Madurai _(actors: Śiva (Sundareśvara), Mīnākṣī)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Liberation as Union in the Self** — By the sixfold yoga the yogī beholds the golden Person and his stilled thought subsides into its source, attaining unity in the Ātman _(actors: the yogī, the supreme Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/maitrayaniya-upanishad.md) — (Maitrī Upaniṣad 6.30, 6.34)
- **River-into-ocean simile of liberation** — As rivers lose name and form in the ocean, the knower freed from name and form attains the supreme Puruṣa _(actors: the knower (jñānin); Puruṣa)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mundaka-upanishad.md) — (Muṇḍaka Upaniṣad 3.2.8)
- **Śrīnivāsa remains bodily on the hill** — Bound by marriage and debt, Śrīnivāsa stays on Tirumala rather than returning to Vaikuṇṭha, grounding the Kali-yuga refuge promise _(actors: Śrīnivāsa)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/tirumala-tirupati-venkateshwara.md) — (Veṅkaṭācala Māhātmya)
- **Sannyāsa mantras and the tyāga-immortality verse** — Supplies the renunciation formulae (praiṣa, 'fearlessness to all beings') and the verse 'na karmaṇā... tyāgenaike amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ' exalting renunciation as the path to immortality _(actors: the saṃnyāsin initiate; renunciate tradition)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad, sannyāsa anuvāka)
- **Sarayū established as life-purifier and death-liberator tīrtha** — The Ayodhyā-māhātmya fixes the bathing/dying mokṣa-formula on the Sarayū and catalogues its riverfront fords (Svargadvāra, Gopratāra, Rāmkī Paiṛī) for ongoing pilgrimage _(actors: Pilgrims of Ayodhyā; the Skanda/Padma Purāṇa redactors)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sarayu-ayodhya-river.md) — (Skanda Purāṇa Ayodhyā-māhātmya; Padma Purāṇa; pilgrimage tradition)
- **Āstīka Halts the Snake-Sacrifice** — Vāsuki sends his nephew Āstīka, who praises the sacrifice so eloquently that Janamejaya grants a boon to cease it, sparing Takṣaka and the surviving nāgas and ending the enmity _(actors: Āstīka, Vāsuki, Janamejaya, Takṣaka)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata Āstīka Parva)
- **The distinct Liṅga Purāṇa Śiva Sahasranāma** — A separate thousand-name recension with its own selection and frame, used in liṅga worship and not to be merged with the Mbh list _(actors: Purāṇic tradition)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/shiva-sahasranama.md) — (Liṅga Purāṇa, Śiva-sahasranāma)
- **The Pūrṇam śānti-mantra** — The peace-invocation 'Oṃ pūrṇam adaḥ pūrṇam idam' declaring the infinite Absolute undiminished in manifesting the world, conventionally attached to the Īśa _(actors: recitation tradition of the Śukla Yajurveda)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/isha-upanishad.md) — (Śukla Yajurveda śānti-pāṭha; cf. Bṛhadāraṇyaka V.1.1)
- **The razor's-edge path and 'arise, awake'** — Yama exhorts Naciketas to awaken, declaring the spiritual path hard to cross as a razor's sharp edge (kṣurasya dhārā), above a ladder of subtlety culminating in the Puruṣa _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad I.3.10–14)
- **Vishvasphurji Abolishes Caste** — The nadir king Vishvasphurji abolishes caste, scorns Vedas and brahmanas — the symbolic floor of the dynastic prophecy _(actors: Vishvasphurji)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.1, Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Vāyu Fails to Move the Straw** — Vāyu is sent next and cannot blow away the same blade of grass _(actors: Vāyu; the yakṣa (Brahman))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.7–9)
- **Yama Teaches the Knowledge of the Self** — Yama discloses śreyas vs preyas, the unborn Self, OM, the chariot of the body, and yoga as steadiness of the senses _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 1.2-2.6)
- **Ahalyā among the Pañcakanyā** — Ahalyā heads the traditional list of five ideal women (Pañcakanyā) invoked in daily sin-destroying remembrance, paragons of virtue despite irregular sexual histories _(actors: Ahalyā, Draupadī, Kuntī, Tārā, Mandodarī)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/ahalya.md) — (later subhāṣita / smṛti tradition)
- **Entry of the Self Through the Suture of the Skull** — The Self cleaves the crown of the head and enters the body through the suture, the place of bliss, becoming the indwelling seer (cryptically named Indra) _(actors: Ātman)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad I.3.11-14)
- **Gokarṇa as the western Tīrtha-yātrā ford** — The Mahābhārata Tīrtha-yātrā Parva names Gokarṇa among the holy western/southern coastal tīrthas where bathing yields great merit _(actors: Pāṇḍavas (pilgrim frame), sages)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gokarna-mahabaleshwar-atma-linga.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Tīrtha-yātrā Parva)
- **Indra Approaches and the Yakṣa Vanishes** — Indra goes last; the yakṣa disappears, and Indra alone waits at the spot _(actors: Indra; the yakṣa (Brahman))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 3.10–4.1)
- **Naciketas Attains Brahman** — Having received the knowledge of the Self and the whole rule of yoga from Death, Naciketas becomes free of passion and death and attains Brahman _(actors: Naciketas, Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/nachiketa-katha-upanishad.md) — (Katha Upanishad 2.6.18)
- **Naimiṣa named a supreme ford in the Tīrtha-yātrā Parva** — Pulastya (to Bhīṣma) and Nārada/Dhaumya (to Yudhiṣṭhira) rank Naimiṣa on the Gomatī among the supreme pan-sectarian fords, a month's bathing yielding horse-sacrifice merit _(actors: Pulastya, Bhīṣma, Nārada, Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Mahābhārata Vana Parva, Tīrtha-yātrā Parva (~ch. 87))
- **Renunciation and hearing the Bhāgavata from Śuka** — Accepting the curse, Parīkṣit fasts on the Gaṅgā and hears the entire Bhāgavata Purāṇa recited by Śukadeva over seven days (vs the epic's fortified-tower resistance) _(actors: Parīkṣit, Śukadeva (Śuka), assembled sages)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Bhāgavata Purāṇa I.19–XII.5; Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva)
- **Sandhyā, prāṇāyāma and expiation liturgy** — Furnishes a large share of daily twilight-prayer (sandhyā-vandana), the prāṇāyāma vyāhṛti-formula, and aghamarṣaṇa/prāyaścitta expiation mantras of the Yajurvedin _(actors: Yajurvedin worshippers)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/mahanarayana-upanishad.md) — (Mahānārāyaṇa Upaniṣad; Taittirīya Āraṇyaka)
- **Āstīka halts the sacrifice** — The boy-sage Āstīka praises the rite, is offered a boon, and asks that the sacrifice cease; bound by the boon Janamejaya stops the fire, saving Takṣaka and the surviving serpents _(actors: Āstīka, Janamejaya, the priests, Takṣaka)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/janamejaya-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi (Āstīka Parva); Bhāgavata XII)
- **Takṣaka kills Parikṣit** — Takṣaka turns back the healer Kāśyapa, enters the fortress hidden in a fruit, and bites Parikṣit, who burns to death _(actors: Takṣaka, Parikṣit, Kāśyapa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 40–43; cf. Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.16–19)
- **The hunter and the elephant** — Śiva as a hunter subdues a rogue/demon elephant sent against the city or his devotees _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **The thumb-sized Person and yoga of sense-restraint** — Yama reveals the aṅguṣṭha-mātra puruṣa dwelling in the heart, the self-luminous abode, the eleven-gated body-city and the inverted cosmic tree, defining yoga as the firm holding-back of the senses _(actors: Yama, Naciketas)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/katha-upanishad.md) — (Kaṭha Upaniṣad II.1.12–13, II.2.1, II.2.15, II.3.1, II.3.10–17)
- **The Tirukalyāṇam — the divine wedding** — Śiva as Sundareśvara weds Mīnākṣī in the great Tirukalyāṇam at Madurai, the theological centre of the temple _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Sundareśvara (Śiva), the gods)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Hālāsya Māhātmya)
- **Vaiśampāyana First Recites the Mahābhārata** — At Janamejaya's sarpa-satra, Vaiśampāyana, pupil of Vyāsa, first recites the Mahābhārata to the king — the epic's outermost narrative frame _(actors: Vaiśampāyana, Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/nagas-and-serpents.md) — (Mahābhārata)
- **Arjuna's Gandiva fails against the Abhira robbers** — Escorting the Yadava column, Arjuna is ambushed by Abhira bandits and finds his strength gone, unable to string Gandiva or summon his astras; the widows are carried off and the loss of his invincibility signals the divine age has closed _(actors: Arjuna, Abhira robbers, the Yadava widows)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.7-8)
- **Death by Takṣaka** — Takṣaka turns back the physician Kaśyapa, hides as a worm in a fruit, and bites the king, who dies liberated; the death triggers Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Takṣaka, Kaśyapa, Parīkṣit, Janamejaya)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/parikshit.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi Āstīka Parva; Bhāgavata Purāṇa XII.6)
- **Doctrine of the Threefold Birth** — The teaching that a man is born three times: in the womb, at delivery, and through his offspring / spiritual rebirth, exemplified by Vāmadeva _(actors: the father-self; the embryo; Vāmadeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad II.1.1-5 (quoting Ṛgveda IV.27.1))
- **Forest retreat and the dead raised** — Gāndhārī retires to a forest hermitage where Vyāsa raises the slain from the Gaṅgā for one night _(actors: Gāndhārī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Kuntī, Vidura, Vyāsa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/gandhari.md) — (Mahābhārata, Āśramavāsika Parva)
- **Gokarṇa as mukti-kṣetra, the Kāśī of the South** — Gokarṇa is glorified as a liberation-tīrtha with the Koṭi-tīrtha tank and direct touch-darśana of the Ātma-liṅga, styled Dakṣiṇa-Kāśī _(actors: Devotees, the dead (śrāddha rites))_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/gokarna-mahabaleshwar-atma-linga.md) — (Gokarṇa-māhātmya; Skanda Purāṇa Sahyādri-khaṇḍa)
- **Janamejaya vows the sarpa-satra** — On learning how his father died, Janamejaya vows a snake-sacrifice to summon and burn every serpent, with Takṣaka the chief target _(actors: Janamejaya, his ministers)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 13, 49–52)
- **Revelation by Umā Haimavatī** — The goddess Umā Haimavatī appears and reveals to Indra that the yakṣa was Brahman, whose victory the gods had wrongly claimed _(actors: Umā Haimavatī; Indra; (Brahman))_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 4.1–4)
- **The First Three Alvars Meet at Tirukkovilur** — The first three (Mudhal) Alvars — Poigai, Bhutha, and Pey — meet in a storm-narrowed corridor at Tirukkovilur, where the Iyarpa Prabandham begins _(actors: Poigai Alvar, Bhutha Alvar, Pey Alvar)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/108-divya-desams.md) — (Alvar hagiography / Naalayira Divya Prabandham)
- **The Kali-yuga king-list prophecy** — Parashara prophesies the post-Parikshit dynasties of Magadha (Pradyotas, Shaishunagas, Nandas, Mauryas, Shungas, Kanvas, Andhras) and foretells the rise of mleccha and low-born kings _(actors: Parashara, Parikshit)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vishnu-purana.md) — (Vishnu Purana (Amsha 4, ch. 24); cf. Bhagavata 12)
- **The stone elephant that ate sugarcane** — Śiva makes a carved stone elephant come alive and eat sugarcane to confound rivals and vindicate a devotee _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Tiru Naimiśāraṇyam sung as a Divya Desam** — Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār sings Naimiṣāraṇya (Devarāja Perumāḷ, with Puṇḍarīkavalli Thāyār) as one of the 108 Divya Desams in the Nālāyira Divya Prabandham _(actors: Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār, Devarāja Perumāḷ)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Nālāyira Divya Prabandham (Tirumaṅgai Āḻvār))
- **Vaiśampāyana recites the Mahābhārata** — At Vyāsa's bidding his disciple Vaiśampāyana narrates the entire Mahābhārata to Janamejaya at the sacrifice — the epic's outer frame, re-narrated by Ugraśravas Sauti at Naimiṣa forest _(actors: Vyāsa, Vaiśampāyana, Janamejaya, Ugraśravas Sauti)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/janamejaya-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata Ādi 1 (Pauṣya/Āstīka/Aṃśāvataraṇa Parvas))
- **Venkateshvara's marriage to Padmavati and loan from Kubera** — The self-manifest Venkateshvara (Balaji/Srinivasa) of Tirumala marries Padmavati and takes a loan from Kubera, the founding legend of the Tirupati shrine _(actors: Venkateshvara, Padmavati, Kubera)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/skanda-purana-khanda-map.md) — (Skanda Purana (Vaishnava-khanda, Venkatachala-mahatmya))
- **Vishnu Stands on Pundalika's Brick at Pandharpur** — While serving his parents, the reformed son Pundalika tosses a brick for the arriving Vishnu to wait upon; pleased, the Lord stays standing on the brick as Vitthala _(actors: Pundalika, Vishnu/Krishna-Vitthala)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Skanda & Padma Purana Panduranga-mahatmyas)
- **Viṣṇu/Aḻagar gives the bride away** — Her brother Viṣṇu (Aḻagar/Kallaḻagar) performs the kanyādāna; in the festival variant he arrives at the Vaikai too late _(actors: Viṣṇu (Aḻagar/Kallaḻagar), Mīnākṣī, Sundareśvara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Madurai sthala-purāṇa)
- **Vyāsa recounts the 108 Śakti Pīṭhas** — Vyāsa recounts to Janamejaya 108 seats of the Goddess with their locations and the local form of the Devī at each — the most-cited Purāṇic pīṭha-list _(actors: Vyāsa, Janamejaya)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/devi-bhagavata-upapurana.md) — (Devī Bhāgavata, skandha VII)
- **Co-sovereignty and worship-precedence established** — By the marriage Mīnākṣī remains co-sovereign and is worshipped before Sundareśvara, the union re-enacted yearly at the Cittirai festival _(actors: Mīnākṣī, Sundareśvara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/devi-meenakshi.md) — (Madurai sthala tradition; living tradition)
- **Death in the forest wildfire** — A forest conflagration consumes Gāndhārī together with Dhṛtarāṣṭra and Kuntī; Sañjaya survives to report it _(actors: Gāndhārī, Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Kuntī, Sañjaya, Nārada)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/gandhari.md) — (Mahābhārata, Āśramavāsika Parva ~37-39)
- **Disputed canonical status — the Vāyu/Śiva seat** — Vāyu is counted among the 18 Mahāpurāṇas by Matsya/Bhāgavata lists but replaced by the Śiva Purāṇa in others; al-Bīrūnī already recorded the two rival lists _(actors: —)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/puranas/vayu-purana.md) — (Purāṇic concordances [scholarly]; smriti-puranas survey)
- **Hierarchy of the Gods Established** — Because Agni, Vāyu and Indra drew nearest to Brahman, they are held to excel the other gods, Indra most of all _(actors: Agni; Vāyu; Indra)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/kena-upanishad.md) — (Kena Up. 4.2–3)
- **Naimiṣa counted among the Aṣṭa Svayaṃ-vyakta Viṣṇu kṣetras** — Vaiṣṇava tradition lists Naimiṣa among the eight self-manifested shrines of Viṣṇu where the deity appeared without human installation _(actors: Viṣṇu (Hari), Pāñcarātra/Śrīvaiṣṇava tradition)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Pāñcarātra tradition; Vaiṣṇava sthala-purāṇa; Bhāgavata Purāṇa 1.1.4)
- **Prajñānaṃ Brahma — Consciousness Is Brahman** — The inquiry into the Self identifies all faculties and all gods and beings with Prajñāna and declares the Ṛgvedic mahāvākya 'Consciousness is Brahman.' _(actors: the inquiring Self; Brahmā, Indra, Prajāpati, all gods and beings; Vāmadeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/upanishads/aitareya-upanishad.md) — (Aitareya Upaniṣad III.1.1-4)
- **The burning of the nāgas** — Priests' mantras drag serpents by the thousand into the sacrificial fire, fulfilling Brahmā's sanctioned cull _(actors: Janamejaya, the priests, the nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 52–53)
- **Turning jackals into horses (and back)** — Śiva transforms jackals into cavalry horses to rescue Māṇikkavācakar, then turns them back into jackals before vindicating his devotee _(actors: Śiva, Māṇikkavācakar, Pāṇḍya king)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Tiruvācakam hagiography)
- **Vajra installed as king at Indraprastha** — Arjuna reaches Kurukshetra with a remnant and installs Krishna's grandson Vajra as king at Indraprastha, preserving the Yadava line _(actors: Arjuna, Vajra)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.8)
- **Vajranabha Re-founds Dvaraka Worship** — Krishna's lineage through Aniruddha and Vajra is credited with re-founding worship and raising the original Hari-griha shrine after the city's submergence _(actors: Vajranabha, Aniruddha)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/dwarka-bet-dwarka-saurashtra.md) — (Skanda Purana, Dvaraka-mahatmya)
- **Astika halts the sarpa-satra and the Mahabharata is recited** — The young brahmana Astika stops Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice, sparing Takshaka, and it is at this sattra that Vaishampayana first recites the Mahabharata _(actors: Astika, Janamejaya, Takshaka, Vaishampayana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/uttanka.md) — (Mahabharata Astika Parva)
- **Establishing/convening the Tamil Saṅgam** — Śiva sanctions and presides over the Madurai Tamil Saṅgam, legitimising Tamil as a sacred language _(actors: Śiva, Saṅgam poets)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Survival, reconciliation, and tutorship of Parikshit** — Kripa survives the war uncursed, is re-accepted at Hastinapura, and becomes the weapons-teacher of Parikshit _(actors: Kripa, Parikshit, the Pandavas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/kripa.md) — (Mahabharata, Stri / Shanti / Ashvamedhika Parvas)
- **Takṣaka flees to Indra; Indra abandons him** — Takṣaka coils round Indra's throne; the intensified mantra begins to drag Indra and Takṣaka together, and Indra lets him slide toward the fire _(actors: Takṣaka, Indra, the priests)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 53, 56)
- **The Great Departure and the test of the dog** — After Kṛṣṇa's death Yudhiṣṭhira crowns Parikṣit and journeys north; his companions fall one by one, and he refuses Indra's heaven rather than abandon a faithful dog who proves to be Dharma _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Dharma/Yama, a dog)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Mahāprasthānika Parva)
- **The Lalitā / Liṅgadhāriṇī Devī seat** — The kṣetra hosts the Devī Liṅgadhāriṇī (identified with Lalitā), counted in several Śakti Pīṭha rosters, with Bhairava Mahārudra as guardian _(actors: Lalitā/Liṅgadhāriṇī Devī, Bhairava Mahārudra)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/naimisharanya-chakra-tirtha.md) — (Devī-Bhāgavata Purāṇa; Tantra-cūḍāmaṇi (Pīṭhanirṇaya))
- **Vyāsa counsels the Pāṇḍavas to renounce the kingdom** — The grief-stricken Arjuna goes to Vyāsa, who explains all happened by destiny and the ripening of curses, and counsels that the heroes' age is over and the time has come for the Pāṇḍavas to renounce and depart _(actors: Vyāsa, Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/mahabharata/16-mausala-parva.md) — (Mahabharata 16.8-9)
- **Kali-Yuga prophecy (Bhaviṣya Parva)** — The Bhaviṣya Parva forecasts the degenerate age to come — the moral and social decline of Kali Yuga, beginning by tradition at Krishna's departure → [details](04-deep-dives/harivamsha.md) — (Harivaṃśa, Bhaviṣya Parva)
- **Kalki's Epic Wars and Reign (Kalki Purana)** — Kalki marries Padma and Rama, wars against Koka and Vikoka, defeats the demon Kali personified, then reigns and ascends _(actors: Kalki, Padma, Rama, Koka, Vikoka, Kali (demon))_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/04-kali-yuga/README.md) — (Kalki Purana)
- **The final test of heaven and hell** — Seeing Duryodhana in heaven and his loved ones in hell, Yudhiṣṭhira chooses to remain in Naraka with them; the illusion lifts, he sheds his body in the celestial Gaṅgā, and is reunited in true Svarga _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Indra, Dharma/Yama)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/yudhishthira.md) — (Mahābhārata, Svargārohaṇa Parva)
- **The miraculous Saṅgam bench (palakai)** — Śiva grants a floating plank that expands or contracts to seat only true poets, rejecting the unworthy _(actors: Śiva, Saṅgam poets)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Vāsuki sends Āstīka to the sacrifice** — Watching his clan burn, Vāsuki dispatches his grown nephew Āstīka to the sacrificial ground to plead for the snakes _(actors: Vāsuki, Āstīka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 53–54)
- **Kali Yuga prophecy of the Viṣṇu Purāṇa** — The Viṣṇu Purāṇa closes its king-lists with a famed prophecy of the moral decline of Kali Yuga → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-puranas.md) — (Viṣṇu Purāṇa, Book 4)
- **Āstīka halts the rite and saves Takṣaka** — Āstīka's eulogy wins a boon from Janamejaya; he asks that the sacrifice cease, and Takṣaka—suspended over the fire—and the surviving nāgas are saved _(actors: Āstīka, Janamejaya, Takṣaka)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 53–56)
- **The contest with Nakkīrar** — The critic Nakkīrar faults a verse authored by Śiva himself; Śiva opens his third eye but finally pardons the fearless scholar _(actors: Śiva, Nakkīrar)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Nakkīrar hagiography)
- **Bhima's Fall on the Great Departure** — On the final Himalayan march Bhima falls, his flaw named as gluttony and pride in his strength _(actors: Bhima, Yudhishthira)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/bhima.md) — (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva)
- **Gaṇeśa-caturthī moon-curse aetiology** — A vrata-kathā frame explains Kṛṣṇa's slander as the fruit of seeing the moon on Gaṇeśa-caturthī, and prescribes reciting the Syamantaka story to avert false accusation _(actors: Gaṇeśa, Candra, Kṛṣṇa)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/syamantaka-jewel.md) — (Gaṇeśa-Purāṇa / vrata-kathā tradition attached to Bhāgavata 10.56–57)
- **Sending the seven clouds and the great flood** — Śiva commands the seven clouds to deluge the land (the Vaikai flood), showing mastery of the elements over the Pāṇḍya realm _(actors: Śiva)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Āstīka's snakebite-protection blessing** — The grateful serpents grant Āstīka a boon; he decrees that whoever recalls his name shall fear no snakes—the charm tied to Nāga Pañcamī _(actors: Āstīka, the nāgas)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 58; Nāga Pañcamī folk tradition)
- **Grace-sports: curing the king, granting children, restoring devotees** — A cluster of miracle-sports in which Śiva heals the Pāṇḍya, grants heirs, and answers devotees' vows _(actors: Śiva, Pāṇḍya king, devotees)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam)
- **Recitation of the Mahābhārata at the sacrifice** — With the snakes spared, Vyāsa's pupil Vaiśampāyana narrates the entire Mahābhārata to Janamejaya at this very session, and Sauti later retells it at Naimiṣāraṇya _(actors: Vaiśampāyana, Janamejaya, Vyāsa, Ugraśravas Sauti)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/astika-sarpa-satra.md) — (Mahābhārata, Ādi Parva 1, 4–5, 54–58)
- **Disciplining rival sects / the Jain (Samaṇa) contests** — Sports vindicating Śaivism against Jain (Samaṇa) opponents at Madurai, the sectarian-polemic layer of the cycle _(actors: Śiva, Tamil Śaiva saints, Jain opponents)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/shiva-tiruvilaiyadal-64-lilas.md) — (Tiruviḷaiyāḍal Purāṇam; Tamil Śaiva hagiography)
- **The Dharma Daivas Appear at Birmanna Pergade's House** — Four guardian spirits of Dharma test and are pleased by the Jain chieftain Birmanna Pergade's hospitality, then ask him in a dream to dedicate his home to their worship, founding Dharmasthala _(actors: Kalarahu, Kalarkayi, Kumarasvami, Kanyakumari, Birmanna Pergade)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/sthala-puranas-major-temples.md) — (Dharmasthala daiva legend)
- **Arjuna Returns Gandiva to the Waters** — After Krishna's death, his powers gone, Arjuna casts Gandiva back into Varuna's waters on the final journey and ascends north toward Svarga _(actors: Arjuna)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/characters/arjuna.md) — (Mahabharata, Mahaprasthanika Parva)
- **Birth of Hariharaputra (Shiva + Mohini)** — After the Samudra Manthana, Vishnu reassumes the Mohini form for Shiva, and from their union the divine child Sasta/Ayyappa is born, deliberately to produce the being able to slay the demoness Mahishi _(actors: Shiva, Vishnu-as-Mohini, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Brahmanda Purana, Bhutanatha Upakhyana; Bhagavata Purana 8; Keralan tradition)
- **Mahishi's boon of unslayability** — The buffalo-demoness Mahishi, sister of Mahishasura, does penance and Brahma grants that she can be killed only by a being born of both Vishnu and Shiva — the engine of Ayyappa's birth _(actors: Mahishi, Brahma)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Pandalam/Keralan legend)
- **The infant Ayyappa left on the Pampa** — The divine child is left on the banks of the Pampa river with a golden bell at his neck, to be found and adopted as Manikandan by the childless King Rajashekhara of Pandalam _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, King Rajashekhara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan Pandalam legend)
- **The tiger's-milk plot against Manikandan** — Resentful of the favored foundling, the queen feigns an illness curable only by tigress's milk, sending Manikandan on a seemingly fatal forest errand _(actors: Manikandan, the queen, the Diwan)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan Pandalam legend)
- **Ayyappa slays Mahishi** — In the forest Manikandan confronts and kills the demoness Mahishi (often on the Azhutha river), fulfilling his cosmic mission; her death-dance is commemorated _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, Mahishi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Janamejaya's Snake-Sacrifice** — Avenging his father Parikshit, killed by Takshaka, Janamejaya holds the sarpasatra, the occasion at which the Mahabharata is first recited by Vaishampayana _(actors: Janamejaya, Takshaka, Vaishampayana)_ → [details](03-lineages-vamsha/suryavamsha-and-chandravamsha.md) — (Mahabharata Adi Parva)
- **Ayyappa returns riding a tiger** — Manikandan returns to Pandalam astride a tiger (Indra and the devas in tiger-forms), revealing his divinity and fulfilling the milk-errand _(actors: Ayyappa/Manikandan, Indra, the devas)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Kali Yuga begins (3102 BCE)** — The Age of Strife begins at Krishna's departure with dharma on a single leg; chanting the divine name becomes the prescribed yuga-dharma _(actors: Krishna, humanity)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Surya Siddhanta, Bhagavata Purana 12.2-3)
- **Founding of the Sabarimala shrine** — Ayyappa shoots an arrow and ordains a temple be built where it lands — at Sabari, where the Ramayana ascetic Sabari awaited Rama — then merges into the deity-form _(actors: Ayyappa, King Rajashekhara)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Onset of Kali Yuga, Parikṣit restrains personified Kali** — Kali Yuga formally begins as Kṛṣṇa leaves the earth (traditionally 3102 BCE); Parikṣit confronts and restrains a personified Kali _(actors: Parikṣit, Kali)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.16-17)
- **Curse of Leela into demonic form** — The celestial woman Leela is cursed to buffalo/demonic form (becoming Mahishi) after refusing to return to the divine realm with sage Dattatreya, and is freed upon her death at Ayyappa's hands _(actors: Leela, Dattatreya, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan supplementary tradition)
- **Parikṣit cursed to die in seven days** — Parikṣit is cursed by the boy-brahmana Sṛṅgi to die in seven days by the snake Takṣaka, the dramatic engine for the rest of the Bhagavata _(actors: Parikṣit, Sṛṅgi, Takṣaka)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1)
- **Malikappurathamma's deferred marriage proposal** — The goddess Malikappurathamma wishes to marry Ayyappa, who replies he will wed her only when no first-time pilgrim comes to Sabarimala — forever deferring the marriage and preserving his celibacy _(actors: Malikappurathamma, Ayyappa)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan legend)
- **Suka teaches Parikṣit on the Ganga** — Sukadeva Gosvami speaks the bulk of the Bhagavata to King Parikṣit on the bank of the Ganga during the seven days before his death _(actors: Sukadeva, Parikṣit)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 2-12)
- **The great departure of the Pāṇḍavas** — The Pāṇḍavas and Draupadī walk toward Mount Meru and fall one by one; only Yudhiṣṭhira and a dog (Dharma in disguise) reach heaven's gate _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira, Pāṇḍavas, Draupadī, Dharma)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Mahābhārata 17 (Mahāprasthānika Parva))
- **Ayyappa defeats the bandit Udayanan** — Aided by his companion Vavar and local forces, Ayyappa defeats the forest robber-chief Udayanan _(actors: Ayyappa, Vavar, Udayanan)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/ayyappa.md) — (Keralan temple/pilgrimage tradition)
- **Yudhiṣṭhira's heaven-test and ascension** — Yudhiṣṭhira is tested by an illusion of his kin in hell/heaven, then reconciled, and the heroes attain their celestial states _(actors: Yudhiṣṭhira)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/smriti-itihasa-epics.md) — (Mahābhārata 18 (Svargārohaṇa Parva))
- **Ugrashravas recites the Mahabharata to the Naimisha sages** — The outermost frame of the Gita is Ugrashravas' recitation of the epic to the sages of the Naimisha forest, nesting Vaishampayana's and Sanjaya's reports within it _(actors: Ugrashravas, Naimisha sages)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavad-gita/README.md) — (Mahabharata frame narrative)
- **Future-dynasty prophecy** — Suka foretells the post-Mahabharata kings (Magadha, Nanda, Maurya, Sunga, Andhra) down into Kali in the prophetic past tense _(actors: Sukadeva)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/bhagavata-purana-skandha-map.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12)
- **Death of Parikshit by Takshaka** — King Parikshit fearlessly meets death by the serpent Takshaka's bite, closing the frame, followed by Janamejaya's snake-sacrifice _(actors: Parikshit, Takshaka, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/bhagavata-tales-catalog.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.5-6)
- **Manu's law-code narrated to the sages** — The Manava-Dharmasastra (Laws of Manu) is narrated by Manu to the sages, codifying dharma, varna, and ashrama for the current age _(actors: Manu, sages)_ → [details](90-literature-corpus/agamas-tantras-dharmashastras.md) — (Manusmṛti)
- **The Pandavas' Great Departure (Mahaprasthana)** — Hearing of Krishna's death, the Pandavas crown Parikshit and walk north toward the Himalayas, all dying on the way except Yudhishthira, who ascends to heaven with a dog who is Dharma in disguise _(actors: the Pandavas, Parikshit, Yudhishthira, Dharma)_ → [details](01-manvantaras/manvantara-07-vaivasvata/mahayuga-28-current/03-dvapara-yuga.md) — (Mahabharata Mahaprasthanika and Svargarohana Parvas)
- **Kalki avatara ends Kali Yuga** — Kali Yuga closes with the Kalki avatara, who destroys adharma and ushers in a new Satya Yuga, restarting the Mahayuga _(actors: Kalki)_ → [details](00-time-and-cosmology/yugas-and-mahayuga.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 12.2; Kalki Purana; Vishnu Purana 4.24)
- **Śeṣa incarnates as Patañjali** — Ādiśeṣa takes birth as the sage Patañjali, falling as a tiny serpent into the cupped hands of his mother Goṇikā, to witness Śiva's Tāṇḍava and honour him as first teacher of yoga _(actors: Śeṣa, Patañjali, Goṇikā)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/shesha-ananta.md) — (Vaiṣṇava & Yoga tradition; Patañjali hagiography)
- **Buddha avatar deludes the asuras** — Vishnu descends in ascetic Buddha form, in one reading to delude the asuras away from the Vedic path so the devas can defeat them, and in another to stop Vedic animal sacrifice out of compassion _(actors: Buddha (Vishnu), the asuras)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/dashavatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24; Vishnu Purana 3.17-18; Gita Govinda)
- **Jīmūtavāhana offers his body to Garuḍa** — The compassionate Vidyādhara prince Jīmūtavāhana offers his own body to Garuḍa in place of a Nāga victim, halting Garuḍa's serpent-slaughter _(actors: Jīmūtavāhana, Garuḍa)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara; Nāgānanda)
- **Naravāhanadatta consecrated emperor of the Vidyādharas** — The mortal-born prince Naravāhanadatta wins the vidyās and is consecrated Cakravartin emperor of the Vidyādharas across the Kathāsaritsāgara _(actors: Naravāhanadatta)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Kathāsaritsāgara)
- **Tulasī Vivāha — annual marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu** — The ceremonial marriage of Tulsī to Viṣṇu/Śālagrāma is performed each year from Prabodhinī Ekādaśī to Kārttika Pūrṇimā, ending Cāturmāsya and opening the wedding season _(actors: Tulsī, Viṣṇu)_ → [details](09-artifacts-symbols-and-arts/sacred-flora-and-fauna.md) — (Tulasi in Hinduism (Wikipedia))
- **Vaishampayana recites the Anugita to Janamejaya** — The Anugita reaches the world as Vaishampayana's recitation to King Janamejaya at the snake-sacrifice, reporting the postwar exchange between Krishna and Arjuna _(actors: Vaishampayana, Janamejaya)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/anugita.md) — (Mahabharata)
- **Caṇḍeśa made lord of the gaṇas' provisions** — In the Nāyanār tradition the boy-saint Caṇḍeśa strikes his own father to defend Śiva-worship and is made steward and lord of the gaṇas' provisions _(actors: Caṇḍeśa, Śiva)_ → [details](08-beings-and-bestiary/vidyadharas-siddhas-and-spirits.md) — (Śaiva Siddhānta)

## Kali Yuga — Documented History  ·  827 events

*The academic/historical timeline (flagged distinct from scripture).*

- **Adi Shankara Organizes the Greater Char Dham** — Adi Shankara (c. 8th c. CE) is traditionally credited with organizing the four pan-India abodes (Badrinath, Dwarka, Puri, Rameswaram) into one pilgrimage to bind the subcontinent _(actors: Adi Shankara)_ → [details](06-sacred-geography/char-dham-and-chota-char-dham.md) — (Wikipedia, Char Dham)
- **Adi Shankara Renounces as a Boy at Kaladi** — Born at Kaladi to an aged childless couple, the precocious Shankara renounces as a boy after a crocodile seizes his leg, forcing his mother's consent to sannyasa _(actors: Adi Shankara, Aryamba)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/adi-shankara.md) — (Madhaviya Shankara-Digvijaya)
- **Ajātaśatru's survey of the six heretical teachers** — King Ajātaśatru of Magadha reports to the Buddha that he had previously questioned each of the six rival śramaṇa teachers (Pūraṇa Kassapa, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, Ajita Kesakambali, Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta/Mahāvīra, Makkhali Gosāla) about the visible fruits of the ascetic life and found their answers unsatisfying — the canonical doxographic frame of the 6th–5th c. BCE heterodox field _(actors: Ajātaśatru, the Buddha, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Pakudha Kaccāyana, Sañjaya Belaṭṭhaputta, Ajita Kesakambali, Nigaṇṭha Nātaputta (Mahāvīra), Makkhali Gosāla)_ → [details](05-concepts-and-dharma/nastika-darshanas-and-the-astika-nastika-frame.md) — (Sāmaññaphala Sutta, Dīgha Nikāya 2)
- **Śaṅkara encounters the aged grammarian in Kāśī** — Ādi Śaṅkara, walking Vārāṇasī with his disciples, comes upon an old Brahmin drilling Pāṇinian grammar (ḍukṛñ-karaṇe) as death nears _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara, the aged grammarian, Śaṅkara's disciples)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/bhaja-govindam.md) — (Bhaja Govindam / Mohamudgara frame-story; Śaṅkara-vijaya hagiographies)
- **Śaṅkara encounters the old grammarian in Kāśī** — Walking the lanes of Vārāṇasī with his disciples, Ādi Śaṅkara comes upon an aged Brahmin grammarian rote-drilling the Pāṇinian rule 'ḍukṛñ-karaṇe' as death nears him _(actors: Ādi Śaṅkara, his disciples, an unnamed old Brahmin grammarian)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/stotras/bhaja-govindam.md) — (Bhaja Govindam (traditional frame); Śaṅkara-vijaya hagiographies)
- **Andal Discovered Beneath the Tulasi** — The Alvar Periyalvar finds the infant girl Kodai (Andal) under a tulasi plant in the Srivilliputhur temple garden and raises her in Krishna-devotion, her earth-birth underwriting her Bhu-devi identity _(actors: Periyalvar, Andal)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/andal.md) — (Andal — Wikipedia)
- **Basava rejects the sacred thread** — As a boy Basava rejects the Brahminical sacred thread (upanayana) in protest at birth-based hierarchy and leaves for Kudalasangama to study, taking Kudalasangamadeva as his form of Shiva _(actors: Basava)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/lingayat-vachana-poets.md) — (Basava hagiography (traditional))
- **Bhagavata announcement of the Buddha-avatara** — Vishnu foretold to descend as Buddha, son of Anjana, in Kikata (Magadha) at the start of Kali-yuga to delude the enemies of the faithful _(actors: Vishnu, Buddha, Anjana)_ → [details](04-deep-dives/buddha-avatara.md) — (Bhagavata Purana 1.3.24, 1.3.26)
- **Birth and identity of Bahiṇābāī** — A Deśastha Brāhmaṇa woman, c. 1628–1700 CE, becomes a Vārkarī sant, distinct from the later 1880–1951 Khandeshi folk-poet of the same name _(actors: Bahiṇābāī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/bahinabai.md) — (Wikipedia 'Bahina Bai'; Feldhaus, Bahina Bai: A Translation; Tharu & Lalita, Women Writing in India)
- **Birth and life of Eknāth at Paithan** — Eknāth, a Deśastha Brāhmaṇa householder-saint descended from Bhānudās, lives at Paithan on the Godāvarī as the pivotal mid-tradition Vārkarī figure (c. 1533–1599 CE) _(actors: Eknāth, Bhānudās (ancestor), wife Girijābāī, son Hari Paṇḍit)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/eknath.md) — (Wikipedia Eknath; Britannica; Vārkarī hagiography)
- **Birth and marriage of Puṉitavati** — Born Puṉitavati, devout daughter of merchant Taṉatattaṉ of Kāraikkāl, married to the merchant's son Paramatattaṉ _(actors: Puṉitavati, Taṉatattaṉ, Paramatattaṉ)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/karaikkal-ammaiyar.md) — (Periya Purāṇam (Cēkkiḻār))
- **Birth and milk legend of Sambandar** — Born at Sirkazhi to a Brahmin couple, the toddler Sambandar is fed divine milk by Pārvatī from a golden cup and sings his first hymn, earning his name _(actors: Sambandar, Pārvatī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/the-nalvar-tamil-shaiva-saints.md) — (Wikipedia, Sambandar)
- **Birth and traditional dating of Sūrdās** — Sūrdās, blind Braj-bhāṣā poet, born (trad. c. 1478 CE, near Delhi/Braj); scholarship favors an earlier, shorter 16th-c. floruit _(actors: Sūrdās)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/surdas.md) — (Wikipedia Surdas; Britannica; Hawley; Caurāsī Vaiṣṇavan kī Vārtā)
- **Birth as Nārāyaṇ at Jāmb** — Born Nārāyaṇ Ṭhosar c. 1608 at Jāmb in Marathwada to a Deśastha Brahmin sun-worshipping family _(actors: Nārāyaṇ (Rāmdās), Sūryājipant Ṭhosar, Rāṇūbāī, brother Gaṅgādhar)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/samarth-ramdas.md) — (Wikipedia (Samarth Ramdas); Hindupedia)
- **Birth at Gangākheḍ and placement in Nāmdev's household** — Janābāī is born to low-caste Vārkarī parents Dāmā and Karuṇḍ at Gangākheḍ on the Godāvarī and, after her mother's death, is placed as a maidservant (dāsī) in Nāmdev's Pandharpur household _(actors: Janābāī, Dāmā, Karuṇḍ, Nāmdev's family)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/janabai.md) — (Wikipedia (Janabai); Vārkarī hagiography)
- **Birth of Śaṅkaradeva** — Śrīmanta Śaṅkaradeva, founder of Ekaśaraṇa Dharma, is born into a Bhuyan Kāyastha family at Bordowā/Batadrava in Nagaon, Assam (traditionally 1449) _(actors: Śaṅkaradeva)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/sankaradeva-and-assamese-vaishnavism.md) — (Wikipedia, Sankardev)
- **Birth of Bonbibi and Shah Jangali in Arabia** — Bonbibi and her twin brother Shah Jangali are born to the fakir Ibrahim and his second wife Gulalbibi and abandoned in the forest, where Bonbibi is suckled by a deer _(actors: Bonbibi, Shah Jangali, Ibrahim, Gulalbibi)_ → [details](02-deities-and-cosmic-hierarchy/bonbibi.md) — (Bonbibi Jahuranama)
- **Birth of Nammalvar and the subduing of Shatha** — Born Maran to a non-Brahmin Vellalar family, the infant Nammalvar subdues Shatha (the wind afflicting newborns), earning the title Shathakopa, and never cries, eats or speaks _(actors: Nammalvar, Kari, Udaya Nankai)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nammalvar.md) — (Nammalvar hagiography (traditional))
- **Birth of Nāmdev into the śimpī community** — Nāmdev is born (c. 1270) into the low-caste śimpī tailor/calico-printer community of Pandharpur, into a Viṭṭhal-devotee household _(actors: Nāmdev, Dāmāśeṭī (father), Goṇāī (mother))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/namdev.md) — (Wikipedia Namdev; Vārkarī hagiography)
- **Birth of Ravidās at Seer Govardhanpur** — Ravidās is born into a Camār (leather-worker / Dalit) family in a village on the edge of Vārāṇasī, c. 1450 CE (traditional) _(actors: Ravidās, parents Santokh Dās and Kalsā)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/ravidas.md) — (Wikipedia Ravidas; Grokipedia Guru Ravidass Jayanti)
- **Birth of the four prodigy siblings** — Viṭṭhalapant and Rukmiṇībāī's four children — Nivṛttināth, Jñāneśvar, Sopāndev, Muktābāī — born c. 1273–1279 at Āpegāv/Āḷandī, all later venerated as saints _(actors: Viṭṭhalapant, Rukmiṇībāī, Nivṛttināth, Jñāneśvar, Sopāndev, Muktābāī)_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/nivritti-sopan-muktabai.md) — (Wikipedia (Nivruttinath, Sopan, Muktabai, Dnyaneshwar))
- **Birth to the courtesan Śyāmā of Mangalveḍhā** — Kānhopātrā is born to Śyāmā, a wealthy courtesan of Mangalvedha, and raised in song and dance _(actors: Kānhopātrā, Śyāmā (her courtesan mother))_ → [details](07-acharyas-and-sampradayas/kanhopatra.md) — (Vārkarī hagiography)
